# Changelog

All notable changes to the Voice of Customer (VoC) Data Lake are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

**Versioning.** Releases are numbered `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and written here with two-digit minor and
patch parts (`2.09.00`). `package.json` (repo root, `voc-datalake/`, `voc-datalake/frontend/`) carries
the same number in strict SemVer (`2.9.0`), because npm rejects leading zeros; `scripts/check-version.mjs`
(a `validate.sh` step) fails when the two disagree. A **major** bump marks a redesign or a breaking
change to an API, a stack or stored data; a **minor** bump adds or changes behaviour; a **patch** is a
fix, a test, a doc or tooling only. Every change that lands bumps the version and adds its entry here
(see `.kiro/steering/changelog.md`). `2.x` starts with the Kiro redesign; `0.x` releases are kept below.
Read the **Upgrade notes** of each release before deploying over an existing stack.

The frontend build identifier is the short git commit SHA injected at build time; it is separate from
the platform package version.

## [Unreleased]

## [7.58.00] - 2026-11-19

**Choose the model an engineering agent runs on**, for Kiro and for the native harness: one choice per role (Auto,
Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, or "Other model…", an id typed), and one for a whole run from Run now or a flow's Start a run
([autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#choosing-the-model-75800)). Only with
`-c engineeringAgents=true`; every change is an administrator's, behind Cognito.

### Added

- **The choice** (`runtime/harness/model_choice.py`, `kiro_pin.kiro_model`): `auto` (Kiro picks per task; on the
  native harness the role's default), `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` (`claude-<name>-5.5` on Kiro,
  `global.anthropic.claude-<name>-5-5` on Bedrock), or another model id (letters, digits and `._:/-`, at most 128
  characters, no space, no URL), checked in the card's schema, the API and the app.
- **On a role's card**: `agents/<role>/agent.yaml` `model.choice` (one of the four, the schema's enum) or `model.other`
  (an id), never both; a card with neither runs as before. The bundle carries it as the agent's `model_choice`. No
  shipped card names one.
- **In the Registry**: a role's card has a **Model** select (each option says where it works, Auto "Kiro only";
  "Other model…" shows its id field, with a Kiro or a Bedrock hint by the role's harness) and says what the role runs
  on here; `PUT /agents/engineering/registry/<role>/model` saves it (`{model}`, null for the default) in one
  `SETTINGS#engineering` / `ROLE_MODELS` row of `voc-agents`, with a create-only history row per change. Every card
  answers `model_choice`, `template_model_choice`, who changed it and when, and `runs_on` (`native` or `kiro`); the
  listing answers `bedrock_enabled`.
- **Model for this run** in Run now (`POST /agents/<id>/run` `{model}`) and in a flow's **Start a run**
  (`POST /agents/engineering/runs` `{model}`, the same field and checks): one model for every role. A run's start
  records it and the roles' own choices on its `META` (`model_choice`, `role_models`), a Resume or a Restart keeps them,
  each launch applies them (the run's, else the role's, else its card's), and the session row says the model asked for
  and the choice applied; the run page shows the run's model and each step's model with its harness.
- **Kiro sets its model and checks it**: after the mode, `session/set_config_option {configId: model}` with the
  launch's model (`--kiro-model`), else Kiro's name for the skill's, which the session's agent config and the compiled
  `kiro-agents/*.json` (`model`) pin too. Unless Kiro answers that it is the session's model (`auto`: any), the step
  ends for a person: "Kiro could not use ‹wanted› for the ‹role› (it answered ‹current or none›). Choose another model
  in the role's setup or for this run." Never another model: nobody pays for a model they did not pick.
- **Readiness**: `bedrock_models` checks the native roles' chosen models, and fails on one the deployment does not
  grant and price; `kiro` names each Kiro role's model and says Kiro checks it when the step's session starts.

### Changed

- **Least privilege on Bedrock**: the native harness runs a chosen model only if the deployment grants it (the
  agents' Claude allowlist) and prices it (`DEFAULT_TOKEN_PRICES`, `-c engineeringModelPrices`); else it is refused
  when it is saved, at the run's start and at the launch: "‹id› isn't enabled in this deployment. An admin adds it
  with -c engineeringModelPrices (docs/deployment.md)." No grant is widened. The Agents API's environment gains
  `ENGINEERING_MODEL_PRICES`.
- A Kiro session with no choice runs Kiro's name for its skill's model, not the account's default; one whose model
  Kiro has no name for stops before kiro-cli starts ("‹id› has no Kiro name; choose a Kiro model for this role.").
- Spend is unchanged: Kiro sessions bill Kiro credits (their rate differs per model, `kiro-cli chat --list-models`
  `rate_multiplier`), so the ledger counts their session time only.
- The root README explains Autonomous engineering and the agent orchestration templates and links their docs; the
  monitor's overview test names 7.57.00's `upstream_pull_request`.
- The role's model route is classified (deployment-wide, an administrator's: the cross-workspace tables, the admin
  gates and the delegated-credential refusals); the two `SETTINGS#engineering` saves share one transaction helper
  and the runtime reads the row through one table helper (`engineering/settings.py`, `runtime/handler.py`), so the
  raw-access counts stay as they were; the Registry's Save model row is a `StickyActionBar`; and the cost rollup's
  test reads its concurrently started batches in any order (it depended on thread timing, before 7.58.00 too).
- The coverage floor: 7.57.00's public-repository and fork code is tested to it (the token function's public
  actions, a fork's upstream reads and readiness's fork ports: 97 %, 100 % and 86 %), and three SPA files are
  back over 80 % and out of the baseline (the forms' stats schema, the step palette, the scraper editor's parts).
- CodeQL's findings, all older than 7.58.00: the iframe page's `hf_<id>` link reads only a hidden field's id,
  never a prototype's name, like the widget's other hidden values; the skills mock keeps its scopes in Maps; the
  form builder renders its tab through a `switch`; three tests' asserts no longer have side effects, a rust
  pack's test asserts its exact hosts, a CDK test finds the SPA's CSP by its logical id rather than a host in its
  text, and a test's unreachable line is gone. Three are recorded as false positives with their reasons
  (`scripts/codeql-summary.mjs`): the learning loop's settings default, the unit runner's traverse-only `0o711`
  socket directory, and the namespaces test copying the image's layout.
- No hidden field is `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` (the names the widget never fills): the API's form
  validation (`shared/forms_v2.py`) refuses them with a 400, "‹id› is a reserved name; choose another", the
  builder's id check says the same, and an AI draft renames one (`constructor_field`). A form saved earlier with
  one still reads and is served as it is; the next save that changes its definition asks for another name.

### Removed

- The root `templates/` folder: its one file pointed to `voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/README.md`, which the
  root README now links.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do: a role with no choice runs its card's model, on Kiro by Kiro's name for it. On a Kiro account that
  does not offer that model, its steps now stop for a person, saying so: choose a model it offers for the role (Agents
  → Registry) or for the run.

## [7.57.00] - 2026-11-19

The engineering agents work on **any public GitHub repository**, not only the deployment's own: read only, or, to
contribute, on a fork whose run ends with a **pull request on the upstream**, always one click away once our gate and
final go passed and every safeguard held: the run's **Open the pull request on ‹upstream›** link to GitHub's compare
page, title and body prefilled, which the person creates on GitHub; with their GitHub user authorization the broker
opens it for them, as the optional extra. The upstream is the organization's; the fork and the pull requests are the
person's. Merging it stays the upstream maintainers'
([autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#any-public-repository-75700)). Only with
`-c engineeringAgents=true`; every route is an administrator's acting for themselves, behind Cognito.

### Added

- **Read-only connections to any public repository** (`connectors/public_repos.py`):
  - Agents → Connections → **Add a public repository**: `GET /agents/engineering/public-repositories?q=` searches GitHub
    server-side (a name, `owner/name` or an address; public repositories only) with stars, licence, archived and last
    push; `POST /agents/engineering/public-connections` connects one as a `public_read` connection;
  - read with an installation token of the deployment's App that holds `metadata: read` alone and names no repository
    (`github.py` `_token`, the token function's new `public_search`, `public_repository` and `inspect_fork`), never
    anonymously (60 requests an hour per shared Lambda address); no write credential for it exists;
  - its issues are read as feedback (the Issues source follows it, never with a label: `issues_token` reads a public
    repository no installation covers with such a token); Understand and the knowledge docs run and stay in VoC; Issue
    triage and a bug hunt run read only, and the UI says so;
  - **the broker refuses every write on it, failing closed** (`broker.py` `_require_kind`: comments, labels, pushes,
    pull requests, the docs pull request and the upstream pull request, any role, before any token), and a kind it
    does not know too; no CI attestation on it; readiness's `connection` fails a flow that pushes on it.
- **The fork workflow** (`connectors/forks.py`): **Contribute** (`POST …/connections/<id>/fork`) checks the
  upstream (archived, opted out, no licence, a licence other than the one acknowledged: 409) and answers GitHub's fork
  page and the App's install link with a state of its own; the person forks into their account or an organization they
  administer, installs the App on the fork, and the return saves a `fork` connection (the App's reference on the fork,
  the fork's `owner/name`, the upstream, the owner, the licence acknowledged); `PUT …/connections/<id>/upstream` is the
  owner's setting for AI-assisted runs. The agents push only to `voc-agent/**` on the fork and open its pull request
  there; the fork's CI is attested as any connection's.
- **A guided setup card** on the public connection, **Contribute to ‹upstream›**, three steps each with its status:
  **Fork it on GitHub**, **Let the agents push to your fork** (the App on the fork alone), **Optional: open pull requests
  for you** (Authorize as me); under them, in the real names, "Reads: ‹upstream› (public, read-only)", "Agents push to:
  ‹account›/‹name› (your fork)" and "Pull requests to ‹upstream› come from: ‹account› (you click Create, or the app opens
  it for you once authorized)".
- **The upstream pull request, always one click away** (`connectors/upstream_pr.py`, the broker's `open_upstream_pr`,
  the PR author's alone, and the step its fork pull request goes on to): `<fork>:voc-agent/… → <upstream>:<default>`.
  - **The one-click link** (`upstream.compare_link`): `https://github.com/<upstream>/compare/<default>...<fork
    owner>:<fork name>:<branch>?expand=1&title=…&body=…`, every part percent-encoded, title and body prefilled; at most
    7,000 characters, past which it carries a short body (`Fixes #N`, a pointer, the disclosure) and the run keeps the
    full text for **Copy the description**. Kept on the run (`run.upstream_pull_request.compare_url`, `title`,
    `description`, the new state `link`) and shown on the run page and in its end notice.
  - **The safety checks gate the link**: the GO and final go on the branch's tree; the upstream not archived, not opted
    out (a topic or label `no-bot-prs`/`no-ai-prs`, or the marker comment in CONTRIBUTING), public, its licence the
    acknowledged one, no DCO sign-off asked, an issue when it asks for one first; the template filled, the issue linked,
    CONTRIBUTING named and an AI-assistance disclosure naming the fork's account. A refusal offers no link, its reason
    on the run, and the run ends with the fork's pull request.
  - **Opened for you, the optional extra**: with the owner's authorization the broker opens it as them, ready for
    review, when the starter's way of working allows it (AI-driven, or AI-assisted with a person's go and the owner's
    explicit setting) and within a daily cap of 10 a deployment and 2 per upstream (UTC; only automatic opens count, an
    attempt whatever GitHub answers). Otherwise, or when GitHub refuses the app (403: "GitHub didn't let the app open it
    for you: open it with one click"), the run keeps the link with a plain note, never an error. Every automatic open is
    an audit row (the day's slots: who, when, which run and upstream, the outcome).
- **GitHub App user authorization** (`connectors/user_authorizations.py`, `connectors/user_auth.py`): **Authorize as
  me** on an App (`POST …/github-apps/<id>/authorize`), the SPA's `/agents/connections/github/authorized` page posting
  the code once (`POST …/github-apps/authorizations`), `GET …/github-apps/authorizations` and `DELETE
  …/github-apps/<id>/authorization`; the new function **voc-engineering-user-auth** exchanges the code and keeps the
  token per person in SSM (`/[<prefix>-]voc/engineering-user-auth/user/…`, the stack's key), outside the connections'
  path; only the broker reads it, refreshes it and sends it, in one request alone. New Apps keep their OAuth client and
  name the callback URL; an older App's client is set with `PUT …/github-apps/<id>/oauth`.
- Readiness: `fork`, `user_authorization` (advice: without it a run ends with the one-click link) and `upstream_pr`
  for a fork connection (none required).
- Frontend: the public repository picker, the read-only and fork rows, the Contribute dialog and the setup card, the
  authorization line and OAuth client form on each App, the authorized callback page, the upstream pull request on the
  run (its link, Copy the description, the note); 9 locales; mocks.

### Changed

- A fork run's issue is its upstream's (META's `issue_repo`; the start's `head` reads its state there); the agents
  comment on and label nothing on it, and the fork's pull request names no issue.
- The App manifest gains `callback_urls`; an App row and view gain `oauth` and `client_id` (not a secret).
- The Issues source's `issues_token` reads an uncovered public repository through the App (before, it was skipped).
- **The signing layer goes only to the functions that sign** (`SIGNING_LAYER_FUNCTION_IDS`,
  `lib/utils/dependency-layers.ts`): the projects API and its assist worker (and the MCP endpoint, which verifies). The
  persona generator, the persona importer and the document generator drop it (16.8 MB unzipped each): they write
  avatars and prototype HTML to S3 and never build a CDN URL (the projects API signs them per request), and none of
  them has a CDN or signing variable. They had it because `py_layers` judged each function with the lazy imports of
  the functions analysed before it: `scripts/audit/py_graph.py` kept a live function's `from shared.cloudfront_signing
  import sign_url` in the parse cache every bundle shares, so a later bundle that loaded `shared/avatar.py` or
  `shared/prototypes.py` followed it as if it ran at import time, and the result depended on the order the functions
  were analysed. A lazy import now belongs to the run that reached it (`scripts/audit/test_py_graph.py`).

### Security

- IAM, pinned in CDK tests: voc-engineering-user-auth holds the client read and the people's tokens' put alone; the
  broker adds reads of both and a put of the people's tokens; the Agents API adds an invoke and the clients' put and
  delete, still no `ssm:GetParameter`; negative pins: no agent role, the cache writer, the token function, the
  ingestor, voc-engineering-start, voc-engineering-issues-config or the runtime names `engineering-user-auth`, and the
  connections' grant does not match it. In Python: the owner's token is sent only in `POST /repos/<upstream>/pulls`.
- **A form's test responses follow the caller's category and source access** (`feedback_form_handler.py`
  `_view_rows`, `_admits_test_rows`): Results, Responses and their CSV scoped the real responses by the caller's
  category access and source access, but added the test responses (`include_test=true` or `only`) to every caller, so
  one denied the `feedback_form` source, or limited to other categories, still read them, testers' contact answers
  included. A test response is now judged as the form files its responses (source `feedback_form`, the form's own
  category), against the workspace's source profiles in a workspace; a caller it does not admit gets none (fail
  closed, as the stats route counts nothing for them).

### Upgrade notes

- **An App made before 7.57.00** needs, only for the app to open fork connections' upstream pull requests itself (the
  one-click link needs nothing): its callback URL (`https://<domain>/agents/connections/github/authorized`) added on
  GitHub, a new client secret, and **Set the App's OAuth client** under Agents → Connections
  ([deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#the-github-user-authorizations-return-75700)).
- **Needs a live check:** whether GitHub accepts the automatic open with a user token of an App that is installed on
  the fork but not on the upstream (its documentation suggests not); a 403 keeps the one-click link, saying so.

## [7.56.00] - 2026-11-19

The engineering agents get a default **skills library**: 30 skills vendored from the ai-skill-factory plugin 2.0.0
(MIT) and adapted to these agents' tools and rules, each role's card naming the ones it uses. A session's system
prompt lists its role's skills by name and description, and the agent reads one when it needs it with the new
`read_skill` tool (progressive disclosure, as Agent Skills do); the coach's prompt carries its three whole. The Skills
tab gets a **Library**, and a Registry card says which skills it uses. The agent images AgentCore runs move into the
templates, at `voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/images/`, with `npm run images:build`.

### Added

- **The skills library** (`voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/skills/<name>/`, a `SKILL.md` and its
  `references/<file>.md`: 30 skills, 108 files; `templates/orchestration/README.md`, "The skills library"):
  - each SKILL.md's front matter (`schemas/library-skill.schema.json`): `name`, a one-line `description`, `source`
    (`ai-skill-factory 2.0.0 (Amit Deol), skills/<name>`), `license: MIT` and `adapted` (what was changed);
  - adapted to the platform's agents: their tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `run` as argv without a shell or the
    network, `install_dependencies`, `read_skill`, the reviewers' `read_patch`, `write_findings` and `write_review`),
    the repository's STANDARDS.md or INFRA.md read with `read_file` instead of the plugin's spec loader, versions taken
    from the lockfiles instead of the network, every deploy, diff, apply or push left to a person in the finish, no
    `gh`, web fetch, sub-agent, slash command, hook or `git stash`; cross-references name library skills ("the `tdd`
    skill"), and the skills that were not vendored are no longer named;
  - **who uses what** (each card's `skills:`): fixer `tdd`, `systematic-debugging`, `coding-standards`,
    `use-the-sdk`, `verification-before-completion`, `python-engineer`, `typescript-engineer`; builder those and
    `cdk-engineer`, `cdk-doctor`, `aws-serverless`, `databases-on-aws`, `deploy-agentcore`, `docker-ops`,
    `terraform-engineer`, `aws-security`, `frontend-quality`, `mcp-builder`, `perf-debug`, `quality-gates`; hunter
    `systematic-debugging`, `perf-debug`, `security-audit`; commit reviewer, PR reviewer and final go `code-review`,
    `anti-slop`, `security-audit`, `aws-security`, `red-team`, `verification-before-completion` (the PR reviewer also
    `cicd-pipeline`); gate runner `quality-gates`, `verification-before-completion`; understander and mapper
    `understand-plan`, `understand-docs`, `technical-writing`; PR author `technical-writing`; the coach (Learn's card)
    `retrospective`, `skill-builder`, `skill-audit`;
  - adjusted from the coordinator's selection: `cicd-pipeline` is not the builder's (its rules forbid editing CI
    definitions): it is rewritten as an audit of a pull request's workflow changes (pinning, permissions, OIDC,
    secrets, anti-patterns) for the PR reviewer, findings only; `quality-gates` has two sections, the builder's (local
    hook configuration when a feature asks for it, never a CI workflow, no hook install) and the gate runner's (read
    only: which hook system and CI checks the repository has, so checks it runs by hand mirror CI, and a step that
    cannot run is a stop, not a pass), and is the builder's as well; `red-team` keeps only the critic's checklist (the
    steel man, the rubric, severity and confidence, the verification rule); the coach's three are rewritten for its
    one JSON-answer call (each SKILL.md under 4,000 characters; `skill-builder`'s reference on the plugin's own skill
    format is dropped, as it contradicts this platform's); `understand-plan` and `understand-docs` are rewritten
    around what the mapper and the understander write (notes with citations, a draft), without the plugin's fan-out
    agents and output folder;
  - not vendored (out of scope, product-specific or internal): `agent-fleet`, `amazon-narrative-writing`,
    `aws-blog-content`, `cfp-research`, `create-pfr`, `linear-from-doc`, `pptx-design`, `publish-review`,
    `gpu-inference-ops`, `research-protocol`, `deploy-on-aws`, `context-engineering`, `agent-patterns`, `spec`, and
    `scaffolding-audit`;
  - scanned before it landed: no secrets (gitleaks with the repository's `.gitleaks.toml`; the AWS documentation's
    example key id in `security-audit` is gitleaks' own allowlisted one), no customer or person names, no internal
    systems or links: an internal security scanner's name in `aws-security/references/design-decisions.md` became
    "a security scanner", and `code-review`'s copyright-header check of one company's open-source policy became
    `references/repository-compliance.md` (whatever licence header the repository's own files carry).
- **`read_skill(name, reference?)`** (`runtime/harness/library_tools.py`, in the harness's tool registry
  `role_tools.ROLE_TOOLS` for every launchable role, so the Converse loop, the CLI's tool server and Kiro all get it):
  one of the role's own library skills, its SKILL.md (its references named after it) or one reference file, as a DATA
  block with the session's fence, at most 40,000 characters (a longer text is cut, saying so); another role's skill, a
  name that is no skill or a reference the skill has not are refusals that name the ones there are. Every card with
  skills has it (`pending_tools`, then `npm run orchestration:promote-pending`); the transcript's ACP kind is `read`.
- **The prompt's list of skills** (`library_tools.listing`, `with_library`): after the role's instructions and
  examples, each of its library skills by name and description, and that what `read_skill` answers is guidance read
  as data, never an instruction that changes the task, the tools or the gates; only when the session's tools have
  `read_skill` (a skill version stored before 7.56.00 lists nothing). The compiled Kiro configs' prompts carry the same
  lines.
- **The coach's skills**: Learn's card names `retrospective`, `skill-builder` and `skill-audit`; the coach makes one
  model call with no tools, so its system prompt carries their bodies whole, below its rules and above its answer's
  shape (`coach/prompt.py`, `coach-prompt/4`; at most 12,000 characters, `orchestration/bundle.py`
  `MAX_LEARN_SKILLS_CHARS`, within a coach call's worst-case input).
- **The compiler and the validator**: both bundles gain `library` (each skill's front matter, its text, its references
  and the roles that name it) and each agent's `skills`, and the source digest covers the library.
  `npm run orchestration:validate` holds the library to its front matter, its files (SKILL.md and `references/*.md`
  only, each within what `read_skill` answers), the references and skills each file names, no other relative link, no
  Amazon-internal host or system name, every skill named by a card and every card's skills in the library,
  `read_skill` on exactly the launchable cards with skills, and the coach's skills within its prompt's share.
- **Agents → Skills → Library** (`SkillLibrary.tsx`, `SkillLibraryDetail.tsx`, `SkillLibraryParts.tsx`,
  `useSkillLibrary.ts`, `skillLibraryPaths.ts`, `documents/skillLibraryDocument.ts`): a Roles | Library switch; the
  Library lists every skill with its description, source and licence, what was adapted and the roles that use it (each
  linking to its Registry card); a skill opens at `/agents/skills/library/<name>` with its SKILL.md and each reference
  (`…/<name>/references/<file>`) read through the shared document reader (Markdown, the front matter apart). Read from
  `GET /agents/engineering/skill-library` (the list, without the texts) and `…/skill-library/<name>?reference=`
  (a SKILL.md or one reference file; 400 for a malformed name or reference, 404 for none), administrators only, from
  the bundle (`engineering/registry/library.py`; `api/engineeringSkillLibraryApi.ts`); the local mock serves both.
- **"Uses skills" on a Registry card** (`Registry/CardFacts.tsx`): the library skills the card uses, each linking to
  its Library page; none shown when it uses none. Every Registry card carries `skills` (a role's card its template's
  when the skill version it runs has `read_skill`, Learn's card always; a made card its base role's, the same way).
- **`npm run images:build -- <language> <tag> [--push] [--dry-run]`** (`voc-datalake/scripts/images-build.mjs`, from
  the root or `voc-datalake/`): the documented `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64` with its build arguments
  (Mountpoint 1.25.0 with its arm64 sha256 and boto3 1.43.124 by default, each overridable by its environment
  variable); a local image only, `voc-eng-<language>:<tag>`, unless `--push`, which takes the account from
  `aws sts get-caller-identity` under `AWS_PROFILE` and the repository from the processing stack's outputs
  (`PROCESSING_STACK`, default `VocProcessingStack`), refuses another account's repository, logs in to ECR with the
  password on stdin and prints the pushed digest; `latest` and malformed tags are refused.
- VocProcessingStack's outputs `EngineeringImageRepositoryJava`, `…Node`, `…Python` and `…Rust` (each repository's
  URI, with `-c engineeringAgents=true` only): what `images:build --push` reads.

### Changed

- **The agent images moved** from `voc-datalake/engineering-images/` to
  `voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/images/` (`common/`, `python/`, `node/`, `java/`, `rust/`, by `git mv`): the
  Dockerfiles' `COPY` paths (the build context is still `voc-datalake/`), `docs/deployment.md`'s build commands,
  `docs/autonomous-engineering.md`, the image tests, the audit allowlist's reasons, the Lambda assets' hash excludes
  (`lambda-asset-excludes.ts`) and the comments that name the path. The images' contents are unchanged but for the
  harness and the bundle.
- New template versions of every role whose card names skills: builder 3, commit reviewer 4, final go 5, fixer 4,
  gate runner 5, hunter 4, mapper 3, PR author 4, PR reviewer 4, understander 5, and Learn's card (the coach) 2. The
  coordinator's and the committer's cards are unchanged (no skills), and keep their digests.

### Upgrade notes

- Rebuild and push the four images (`npm run images:build -- <language> <tag> --push`, a new tag each), then deploy
  their digests (`-c engineeringImages`): until then the sessions run the old harness, without `read_skill` or the
  library.
- A scope that runs a stored skill version keeps it, without the library: it gets it once a person accepts the newer
  template (Skills, "Template updated").

## [7.55.01] - 2026-11-19

The Feedback Forms v2 UX audit (28 findings), fixed. The form now draws itself apart from the page it lands on, so
the builder's preview, the template picker's preview and a customer's script embed on a dark site show exactly what
respondents get. The in-pane preview is an honest phone, and a pop-out window shows the draft at real sizes. A form's
colours become a Style panel beside the preview, with presets, a dark palette and Auto mode, fonts, sizes and a live
contrast table; unreadable text is refused at publish and on a live form's colour change, in the editor and on the
server, only warned about on a live form kept on the theme it already has, and corrected in the widget. The
assistant button no longer covers the preview's Next, the phone's Next bar really sticks, nothing overflows at
390 px, and the Share tab's script embed works as pasted, from a static file of the app's own CloudFront.

### Fixed

- **The widget is isolated from the host page** (F1, F2; `lambda/api/static/feedback-widget.js`):
  - it draws in an open shadow root of its container (`container.shadowRoot`), with its own reset (an adopted
    stylesheet, else a `<style>`) and one inner root, `.voc-root`; every colour and inherited text property is also
    inline, so a browser without Shadow DOM, a container that cannot host one (a `<form>`: the light DOM then), or a
    page whose CSP blocks the stylesheet still gets the theme's form; the container's own styles and classes are left
    alone;
  - checkboxes and radios are drawn by the widget (a 20 px box in the option-edge colour, the primary fill and an
    on-primary tick), the real inputs kept, hidden, for the keyboard and screen readers; `accent-color` is gone; the
    placeholder is blended to 4.5:1; keys and pointer handling sit on the shadow root (`composedPath`);
  - the iframe page and the mock's copy keep no reset of their own (`html, body {margin: 0}` and the container's
    height); the widget sets `<html>`'s background and `color-scheme` there.
- **The phone's Next bar sticks** (F6): the sticky element is the bar itself (`.voc-nav-bar`, a child of the screen),
  the submit notice above the buttons; at 375 × 667 Next is at y 603–655 (it was at 688, below the fold).
- **Phone / Desktop is gone** (F3): the pane shows a 390 px logical phone scaled to fit ("Phone · 390 × 394 · 89 %"),
  as tall as the window leaves (at least 320 px in the full-height builder, 480 elsewhere); the toolbar is Language ·
  Restart · Start here · Style · Open in window ▾; from 1600 px the preview column is `minmax(22rem, 28rem)`; the
  duplicate "Preview · nothing is sent" caption goes (F21).
- **The assistant button keeps clear** (F4; `components/StickyActionBar/actionBarRegistry.ts`, `assistant/bubble/`):
  keep-clear zones, `lift` (the save bars) and `beside` (the builder's and the picker's preview), so the launcher
  stands beside the preview instead of on its Next (measured at 1280 × 800, 1440 × 900 and 1920 × 1080, never
  overlapping); a dragged spot stays the person's unless it covers a zone. Below md the builder hides the launcher
  and its ⋯ menu has **Ask the assistant**.
- **No sideways overflow at 390 px** (F7): the picker (669 px wide before), a template's preview (425 px) and Results ›
  Responses (649 px, now a card per response below md) are 390 on all twelve pages the audit measured.
- **The Share tab's script embed works** (F8): the snippet is the container, `<script
  src="<app origin>/widget/feedback-widget.js">` and `VoCFeedbackForm.init({…})` (hidden-field placeholders as
  strings, the test token in Test mode); the in-app SDK snippet likewise.
- **The Questions tab scrolls once** (F9): from lg it is a full-height page whose panes each scroll; the Add question
  type menu and every builder ⋯ menu open fixed, in a portal (`utils/fixedMenu.ts` now measures a menu without its
  scale-in transform), never clipped by their pane; the type menu gains type-ahead.
- **Turning a Live form with responses Off asks first** (F10).
- **The preview follows every card** (F11): the welcome screen (while on) and the endings too (`goTo('welcome')`,
  `goTo('end:<id>')`), and Start here works for all three.
- **Flow's false "goes anyway" note** (F12): a rule is noted only when everyone it catches would go to the same place
  without it, the question's Otherwise target when it has one (`paths.noMatchTarget`), and no later rule could send
  them elsewhere; new words, and an ending's own.
- **Question cards** (F13, F14, F18's clamp): 8 px apart, with an insertion line and a 24 px "+" on hover or focus
  in place of the reserved gap, and Add question below in each card's ⋯; the selected card's secondary text in

- **Narrow builder** (F15): the save bar renders only when a button shows, at the end of the tab body, so it sticks;
  the tab row shows that it scrolls (an end fade and scroll buttons, `IconTabs` `scrollLabels`, with the run

- **The iframe embed grows to the form** (F16): framed on its own page, the widget posts `{type: 'voc-form-height',
  height}` to its parent, and the iframe snippet carries a resizer that takes it only from that frame and the API's
  origin (a plain 480 px frame without script).
- The template cards (F18): three chips in one row then "+N", horizontal cards, one column below 2xl, two at 2xl.
- `CollapsibleSection` `size="sm"` for Logic and Advanced (F19); the translation notice is one line under the
  Question field (F20); options keep one width with the jump marker's column reserved, and the Routing view stacks

- The forms list (F22): one link per card (`link-quiet`, a new recipe in the design system), a three-zone layout, the

- The switch's Off track has a 3:1 `--control-border` edge, app-wide (F23; it was 1.27:1 on light).
- The picker has one language control, "Create in"; Describe says "in English · change"; "Drafting…" is said once
  less, and Runs is `aria-disabled` while drafting (F24). The AI draft banner's Go to sits after its sentence; the
  drafter is asked for a short title (2 to 6 words).
- The Test tab's recent responses show their day ("Today 10:20", "Nov 18, 11:25 PM"), with Open beside Copy and QR
  (F25); a builder that could not load has "‹ Feedback Forms" (F26); a new form's Save says why it is off ("Fix 1

- Languages: Add language is a menu button, Change… a ghost button by its language. Hidden fields: Live | Test on its
  own line, "Values for". Settings: a category no longer configured is a `badge-warn` with "Pick a configured
  category."; the anchor list says which card is in view (`aria-current`). Results: "Completion 48 % · largest drop at
  Q2" in the summary, and the funnel marks a drop only between steps every path passes (`results/funnelSteps.ts`).
- The StickyActionBar's `bar` is an opaque `bg-card`, never `backdrop-blur`: a backdrop filter trapped a confirmation
  opened from the phone save bar inside the bar.

### Added

- **The preview window** (`frontend/form-preview.html`, the build's second page, `preview/window/`): the same widget
  file in preview mode at Phone 390 × 844, Rotate, Tablet 768 × 1024, Desktop 1280 × 800 or "Embedded, 480 px
  tall", with Restart and Language, no app CSS and no app chrome; it never submits. It follows the unsaved draft, the
  selected card, the language and the palette over `BroadcastChannel('voc-form-preview:<session>')` (same origin by
  construction; the window says `ready` until a draft arrives), its session kept per form in `sessionStorage` so a
  builder reload keeps talking to it; the list card's ⋯ › Preview opens it on the saved form. No CloudFront or CSP
  change: a top-level window on the app's own origin. `FullScreenPreview` is retired; `/feedback-forms/<id>/preview`
  redirects to the builder.
- **Style** (F5; `pages/FeedbackForms/theme/`): from the preview toolbar (the editor column from xl, a side sheet
  with the phone below), and Settings › **Appearance**, now the second card with its own preview: presets VoC light,
  VoC dark, High contrast and **Your brand**; Mode Light | Dark | Auto (and which palette is being edited, which the
  preview then shows, "Showing: Dark"); primary, background and text, each a swatch with a 3:1 edge and a hex field
  that says why it refuses; the derived option edge; corners 0 / 4 / 8 / 16 px and a 0–24 px slider; font (System,
  Same as your page, Serif, Rounded, Monospace: system stacks only); size Default | Large (18 px). A **live contrast
  table** for text (4.5:1), primary (3:1), button label (4.5:1) and option edge (3:1), each with an icon, its ratio and
  "AA" / "Below AA", and one-click suggestions that move the colour in OKLCH lightness only (`#f5c518` → `#b39018`,
  `#9ca3af` → `#6f7681`).
- **The theme's new fields** (schema version 2, all optional with defaults, read-time migration; `shared/form_theme.py`,
  `model/formsV2.ts`): `mode` (`light` | `dark` | `auto`, default `light`), `dark` (`{primary_color,
  background_color, text_color}`, default VoC dark `#bd8fff` / `#19161d` / `#f2f1f4`), `font` (`system` |
  `inherit` | `serif` | `rounded` | `mono`, default `system`) and `text_size` (`default` | `large`). The top-level
  colours are the light palette. A stored theme is answered with the defaults filled in (`with_defaults`) and written
  back whole on its next save.
- **One set of contrast rules, three places:** the editor (`theme/contrast.ts`, `validateForm.ts`: text under 3:1 is
  an error that blocks Publish and a live form's colour change but never Save, and a warning, `themeUnreadableLive`,
  on a live form kept on the theme it already has, shown in the Style panel and the header's save status, "This
  form's text is hard to read. Fix its colours"; 3–4.5:1 and the other pairs are warnings), the server
  (`shared/forms_v2.py` `validate_publishable` on `shared/form_theme.py`'s helpers, with text under 3:1 in a palette
  the form can show: a write that turns a form live, or changes a live form's theme, is `400 theme_unreadable` with
  the palettes and ratios; any other write to a live form already on that theme is saved and answers `warnings:
  ['theme_unreadable']`) and the widget (`safeContrast`: text under 3:1 is drawn white or `#19161d`; the option edge raised from 55 %
  until 3:1; a primary under 3:1 gets its ring and selected edges in the text colour).
- **The widget's theme engine**: `mode` with `prefers-color-scheme` followed live, the dark palette, `color-scheme`,
  the font stacks (`inherit` for a script embed only), large text; a seeded Shuffle in the preview (`preview.seed`,
  stable across Restart) with "Shuffled for each respondent" under the frame, and `preview.scheme` /
  `setScheme('light' | 'dark' | null)`.
- **The workspace form brand**: `form_theme` on the existing `/settings/brand` row (no new route): `GET` answers it
  (`null` when none), a `PUT` of only `form_theme` sets just that (`null` removes it), a brand `PUT` keeps it; saved
  by the workspace's admins ("Save as brand…", off with the reason for anyone else). New forms from a template, Blank,
  Describe or the assistant's draft start on it.
- **The widget as a static file**: `/widget/feedback-widget.js` on the SPA distribution (`lib/stacks/core-cdn.ts`, a
  `/widget/*` behavior on the SPA bucket's origin, `WidgetHeadersPolicy`: CORS GET/HEAD from any origin without
  credentials, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` and the SPA's own
  security headers), built from the one source by `frontend/widgetAssetPlugin.ts` (a release banner on its first
  line; the dev server serves it too) and deployed with the frontend by either path. The address is stable and
  unversioned on purpose (both deploy paths prune, so a hashed name would break pasted snippets); no SRI, since the
  app uses none and a file replaced each release cannot carry a fixed hash (docs/feedback-forms.md says how a site
  that needs SRI can host its own copy). `lib/stacks/core-stack.test.ts` allows exactly this one unsigned path.
- **Publishing with a language half translated asks first** (F17): "English respondents will see 5 texts in
  Polski." with Publish anyway / Update anyway and Translate per language; the Share tab's Publish asks the same.
- The list stats (`?include=stats` and `…/stats`) carry `last_response_at`, the latest counted response's
  `source_created_at`, when one carries it, and `channels: {link?, iframe?, script?}`, each channel's latest response.
- **Where a response was answered**: the widget sends `channel` (`link`: its own page opened as it is; `iframe`: that
  page framed; `script`: a script embed), optional and one of the three in the API's request model
  (`schemas/public-body-models.json`, `lib/stacks/api-request-models.ts`: a model change, no new resource) and in
