  stats, so a submit writes nothing more. Test responses never count.

### Changed

- The synth-time frontend freshness check counts the widget source, `form-preview.html` and the widget plugin as
  frontend inputs.
- The design system records `link-quiet`, the switch's Off edge, keep-clear zones, the opaque save bar, the portalled
  builder menus and `IconTabs` `scrollLabels` (docs/kiro-design-system.md); docs/feedback-forms.md the list, the
  builder, the script embed and its asset, isolation, the preview and its window, the theme fields, the contrast rules
  and the brand.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy the frontend and VocCoreStack together: the Share tab's script embed names `/widget/feedback-widget.js`,
  which the new `/widget/*` behavior serves (a deployment adds a response headers policy and a cache behavior to the
  SPA distribution). Rebuild `frontend/dist` first: a widget edit now makes the old build stale for `cdk synth`.
- A live form whose stored theme has text under 3:1 keeps saving: the save answers `warnings: ['theme_unreadable']`
  and the builder says "This form's text is hard to read". Only a colour change that stays unreadable, or publishing
  such a form again after turning it off, is refused; its respondents already get readable text from the widget.
- Deploy VocApiStack before, or with, a frontend-only deploy (`npm run deploy:frontend`): the new widget sends
  `channel`, which an API from before 7.55.01 refuses as an unknown field (the CDK deploy ships both in VocApiStack).

## [7.55.00] - 2026-11-18

Feedback Forms become a form builder. A form is now a flow of questions (schema version 2): a welcome screen, 1 to
30 questions of ten types, logic that jumps forward to a later question or to one of up to five endings, hidden
fields the link or the app fills in, and its texts in any of the app's nine languages. It has a test link whose
responses never count, per-question results with a drop-off funnel, twelve templates, and an AI that drafts a form
from a description, in the builder and from the assistant. A form saved before keeps working: it is migrated when
it is read and written back as version 2 on its next save. The release also carries a customer pilot's fix: a form
without a rating shows its Question.

### Added

- **Schema version 2** (`lambda/shared/forms_v2.py`, the one definition; docs/feedback-forms.md):
  - `language` (the primary) and `languages`; every text is an I18nText `{"<locale>": "…"}`, the primary's required,
    the others falling back to it;
  - `welcome`, `questions` (1–30), `hidden_fields` (at most 20), `endings` (1–5), `settings.test`;
  - the question types `open_text` (short or long, text / email / number / phone / url, max characters),
    `single_select` and `multi_select` (1–50 options with stable codes, Other, an exclusive None of these, shuffle,
    list / dropdown / chips, min and max), `rating` (stars, numbers or faces, 3–10), `nps`, `csat`, `ces`,
    `statement` (an optional https button), `consent` and `contact_info` (name, email, phone, company);
  - **logic**: per question, rules `{when: {op, value?}, then: {jump_to}}`, the first that matches wins; the ops are
    checked per type, a jump only goes forward (no loops) and its target must exist;
  - **revisions**: a save that changes the definition is a new `revision`; the replaced one is kept as a snapshot
    (`FORMREV#…`), so a respondent who opened the form before an edit is checked against what they saw; a question
    id is never reused (`400 question_id_reused`); a save names the revision it read (`expected_revision`) and a stale
    one is a `409 revision_conflict` with who saved it and when; the other fields (name, enabled, theme, routing,
    links, labels, dimension defaults, tags, test settings) still change in place without a revision (a recorded
    TENETS.md D1 gap);
  - **the lock of an answered form**: once a form `has_responses`, a save that drops a question id, or an option code
    from a question it keeps (a rename is a drop plus an add), must name each one in `removes` (`{questions, options:
    {question_id: [codes]}}`), or it is a `409 answers_locked` naming them and nothing is written. A named removal is
    kept as the builder keeps it (the id retires, the answers stay in Results as removed), and the builder sends
    `removes` itself; in a workspace as deployment-wide;
  - each option may carry its own category routing (never published): the first answered option that maps one
    files the response; otherwise the form's routing applies.
- **The public form** (`lambda/api/static/feedback-widget.js`, still one dependency-free file): one question per
  screen with the welcome card, every type, logic, several endings, labelled Back and Next, a sticky bar on phones and
  progress over the longest path left; hidden fields from the link (`hf_<id>=`) or the SDK (`setHiddenFields`); the
  respondent's language from `lang=` or the SDK, then the browser, then the form's (D4), with the widget's own words
  in nine languages and the page's `lang` and title following the form; keys handled only inside the form, never on
  the host page; a refused answer explained in the respondent's language, back at its question. `init` returns a
  handle (`setHiddenFields`, and for the editor's preview `update`, `goTo`, `restart`, `setLanguage`, `destroy`).
- **Responses v2** (`lambda/shared/forms_v2_responses.py`): `{answers, hidden?, form_revision?, language?,
  ending_id?, session?, test?, page_url?, …}`, checked answer by answer against the revision answered (type,
  required, range, codes, characters, min and max, the logic path; unknown keys refused) with a refusal `code` and
  the `question_id` to go back to (`answer_invalid`, `answer_required`, `selection_count`, `hidden_unknown`, …;
  `form_changed` is a 409, `form_off` a 400). The item's text is the open answers under their headlines; the
  structured answers, hidden values, path, revision and language go into its metadata (`form_answers`, `form_hidden`,
  `form_path`, `form_revision`, `form_language`); a hidden value whose id is a dimension's key and whose value is one
  of its values fills that dimension (D5).
- **Test mode** (D2): `POST /feedback-forms/{id}/test-link` (admins) issues or rotates a test token, the only answer
  that carries it; the test link (`…/iframe?test=<token>`) works while the form is Off and shows a TEST strip;
  `record: tag` keeps its responses apart from the form, in their own partition (`FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST`, a workspace's
  `WS#{ws}#FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST`), as `is_test` (never queued, so never processed, counted, in NPS or on a dashboard),
  `drop` checks them and keeps nothing; `GET …/config?test=` answers `test: {valid, record}`.
  **Test responses are kept until an admin or the form's creator deletes them** (the owner's decision):
  `DELETE /feedback-forms/{id}/responses?test=true` is for an admin of the workspace (else of the deployment) or the
  person who created the form, a `403 test_responses_admin_or_creator` for anyone else; `GET /feedback-forms/{id}`
  answers `can_delete_test_responses`, and the Test tab offers Delete all to those people only (the others read who
  can). Every such delete is recorded first (TENETS.md D4): a workspace form's in `AUDIT#WS#{ws}`, a deployment
  form's as an `AUDIT#delete` row (`shared/delete_audit.py` `record_delete_first`), kind
  `feedback_form_test_responses`, the form id, the caller, `count` and the time; a row that cannot be written deletes
  nothing. A tagged test response keeps its contact answer's email (lower-cased) and name, so `voc-retention` reaches
  it: an erasure by email or by name, a whole-source erasure of `feedback_form` and that source's retention period
  delete test responses too, each with a tombstone first, in the scopes they reach feedback items in (by email and by
  the retention period every workspace's forms too; a workspace's own erasure, its own; an erasure that deletes a
  workspace's test response clears that workspace's exports, which hold them as `feedback_form_tests`;
  [docs/source-policies.md](docs/source-policies.md)). They are kept unredacted (a recorded TENETS.md D5 gap).
- **Results** (`lambda/shared/forms_v2_results.py`): `GET /feedback-forms/{id}/results` per question of the current
  revision (shown, answered, skipped, not shown; option counts with the latest Other texts, histograms, NPS, CSAT and
  CES scores, the latest open answers), the endings and hidden fields, answers to removed questions and options, and
  a **drop-off funnel** (D6) `{opened, left: {question_id: n}, completed}`: the widget sends one `opened` beacon per
  page load (`{event: {kind: 'opened', session, revision?}}`), and a respondent who leaves without submitting sends
  one `left` beacon (`{event: {kind: 'left', question_id, session}}`), both by `sendBeacon` on their own public
  route, `POST /feedback-forms/{id}/events`, never an answer. The public config read never writes. The funnel's
  record is one counter row per form per day (`opened`, `left:{question_id}`), kept without expiry (TENETS.md D2) and
  going with the form's delete (the test link's with its test responses'); a visit's own row, which moves its `left`
  to the furthest question and takes it back when the visit submits, expires after 7 days. `GET …/responses` pages
  the responses (filters: dates, language, ending,
  `hidden.<id>`; `include_test=false|true|only`) and `format=csv` exports them (labels and ids as two header rows, no
  spreadsheet formula in any cell, the header's headlines included: they are the author's text). The form list's
  card shows a headline figure (NPS, CSAT % or the average).
- **AI drafts** (`lambda/shared/forms_v2_draft.py`): `POST /settings/form-drafts` `{description, language, channel,
  base_form?, instruction?}` starts an assist job run by the settings API's assist worker (the deployment's model on
  the `utility` surface, metered like every AI feature). Both draft routes are the settings API's
  (`lambda/shared/forms_v2_draft_routes.py`, on its own `/settings/{proxy+}`), not the forms Lambda's, workspace-scoped
  as before (with `X-Workspace-Id` the job, its hourly counter and its model calls are the workspace's). The browser
  reads `GET /settings/form-drafts/{job_id}` when the worker's `job` notice arrives, polling as the fallback (1.5 s
  without push, 10 s with it, 3 minutes at most). The
  person's text travels as data; the server makes the ids and codes itself and drops every address that is not https;
  the answer must pass the same validator (one repair with its errors, then `invalid_draft`); `no_model` when the
  deployment has none. Any signed-in editor of a workspace may draft (and its admins; deployment-wide any signed-in
  user: the owner's decision); 20 drafts per person per hour (`429 rate_limited` with `retry_after`); not gated by the
  way of working (D12). It never saves. While a draft generates, **Stop** (in the picker and in Improve with AI)
  asks "Stop drafting?" and, confirmed, stops the poll at once and drops the draft (the server's job finishes on its
  own: an assist job has no cancel, and nobody reads its result).
- **The builder** (`frontend/src/pages/FeedbackForms`): a picker with "Describe your form" and twelve templates
  grouped by goal (Loyalty: NPS, CSAT after support, CES; Drop-offs: cancellation, switching back to the old UI,
  checkout or signup abandonment; Product: product-market fit, feature request, feature satisfaction, bug report;
  Onboarding: segmentation; Blank), their copy in nine languages; a builder page at `/feedback-forms/<id>/<tab>` with
  Questions, Flow, Languages, Hidden fields, Test, Share, Results and Settings; the choice editor (paste options,
  routing per option), the logic editor with its problems, the hidden fields with their snippets, translations side by
  side, Save, Publish, Update live form and Turn off, the stale-save banner (Compare, Reload, Save mine), and a live
  preview that runs the real widget in the page, never sending anything. "Improve with AI" redrafts the open form from
  an instruction and shows the changes to apply; an AI draft opens unsaved with its notes and the addresses to confirm.
  Option codes and question ids lock once the form has a real response.
- **The assistant's `draft_feedback_form`** (the `forms` pack, any caller): a whole version 2 form on an approval card
  the person edits (its name, a question left out, the suggested addresses checked) before Approve creates it Off, or
  "Open in builder". Card-only, never a plan step.
- `GET /feedback-forms/{id}`: one form with `response_count`; the record says `has_responses` (marked once, by the
  first real response) and `migrated_from: 1` while it is still stored as version 1.
- **Every form delete is recorded** (the owner's decision): a workspace form's in `AUDIT#WS#{ws}` (kind `form_deleted`,
  as before) and now a deployment form's too, as the deployment's other deletes (`shared/delete_audit.py`
  `record_delete_once`: `AUDIT#delete` / `feedback_form#{form_id}` in voc-aggregates, the form id, the actor and the
  time, one row per form); written first, so a delete whose record fails deletes nothing. Both rows carry
  `test_responses_deleted`, the test responses removed with the form, read and counted before anything is deleted
  (`record_delete_once`'s new `counts`; a retried delete keeps the first count).

### Changed

- **Version 1 forms** are served migrated (D15): their rating becomes a `rating` question headed by the Question, the
  text step an `open_text` question headed by the follow-up question when the rating is on and by the Question when it
  is off, `collect_name` / `collect_email` a `contact_info` question, `success_message` the first ending; a form
  without a language gets the deployment's (`-c primaryLanguage`), which the builder asks its author to confirm. The
  first save writes it back as version 2, keeping the version 1 fields in revision 1's snapshot. A version 1 widget's
  body (`text`, `rating`, …) is still accepted.
- The editor (FormEditor, its panels, the template wizard and the submissions dialog) is replaced by the builder; the
  list's cards link into it.
- **The assistant's `update_feedback_form`** takes only what every form takes: `enabled`, `name`, `dimension_defaults`,
  `tags`, and `title` / `description` (the welcome screen), `success_message` (the first ending) and
  `submit_button_text` (the last question's button) in the primary language. `question`, `placeholder`, the rating and
  `collect_*` fields, which a version 2 form refuses, are gone from it; questions and logic change in the builder.
  `list_feedback_forms` reads each form's language, revision, questions (id, type, headline, option codes, rules),
  endings, hidden field ids and test link state.
- The API Gateway model of `POST …/submit` (`FeedbackFormSubmission`) no longer requires `text`: it bounds the
  version 2 body, and the submit takes responses only (a beacon there is `400 submission_invalid`). The beacons'
  route has its own strict model, `FeedbackFormEvent` (`schemas/public-body-models.json` regenerated).
- The processor drops a message marked `is_test` before validation (`TestResponseDropped`) and the aggregator skips
  one, so a test response that reached the queue anyway is never counted; a workspace's delete takes a form's lookup
  row from its form rows only, not from the new rows beside them.
- Results of Feedback Forms: no funnel is shown when the beacon counted no open for the view (Reach instead).

### Fixed

- **A form without a rating shows its Question** (a customer pilot): the widget showed "Tell us more" instead. A
  form with a rating gets an optional follow-up question for the text step (7.54.00's `text_question`, now the
  `open_text` question's headline).
- **The widget speaks the form's language**: its own words (Start, Next, the errors, Thank you) follow the form,
  in the app's nine locales, instead of the visitor's browser.
- Found in the review rounds of the release (they never shipped): a test token with a non-ASCII character
  (`?test=é` on the public config or submit) is a wrong token, never a 500 (the token is compared on its UTF-8
  bytes); a plain save of a version 1 form (the list card's Enable) validates its migration before writing it back
  as version 2, never stores it unchecked; the builder's stale-save banner never prints a Cognito sub as a name: it
  says "You saved this form at 14:02, in another tab or window." when the saver is the person, else "Someone else
  saved this form while you were editing it." (`builder.conflict.messageSelf`, 9 locales).

### Removed

- The version 1 editor: `FormEditor.tsx`, `FormEditorPanels.tsx`, `TemplateWizard.tsx`, `SubmissionsModal.tsx` and
  their specs; the SPA's `api.createFeedbackForm` and `api.getFeedbackFormSubmissions` (the builder creates through
  the v2 client; `GET …/submissions` stays for the assistant's `get_feedback_form_submissions`) with their parser;
  `FormStatsFigures`' `panel` variant (its one user was the submissions dialog).

### IAM

- The Feedback Form API's role, which serves the public routes, gains no AI access: no `lambda:InvokeFunction`, no
  jobs-table action and no model grant (pinned in `lib/stacks/api-stack-feedback-forms-v2.test.ts`). The AI draft runs
  entirely on the settings API, whose role already owns the assist job rows of every scope, its assist worker, the
  Bedrock grant and `UpdateItem` on voc-aggregates (the draft's hourly counter in a forms partition): no grant changes
  there. The forms role's key-scoped `DeleteItem` now covers the forms partitions (`FEEDBACK_FORM`, one workspace
  id's `WS#{ws}#FEEDBACK_FORM`: a form, its snapshots and funnel counters) and the test responses' own partitions
  beside them (`FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST`, `WS#{ws}#FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST`). No other grant changes.
- New routes on the Feedback Form API, all Cognito-authorized but one: `GET` on `/feedback-forms/{form_id}` (one
  form) and one `{proxy+}` under it for `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE` (results, responses, CSV, test responses, test link);
  and one new unauthenticated route, `POST /feedback-forms/{id}/events`, the widget's funnel beacons, public like
  `submit` (the widget runs on customers' sites) with the same form checks and lookup (a disabled form takes none
  without its valid test token; a workspace's form by its lookup row, its rows written in that workspace), its own
  throttle (sized for page views, like the widget's reads; docs/feedback-forms.md), its own strict model and the same
  WAF scope as the widget's reads, so a beacon never spends the submit route's limit, which stays for real responses.
  It writes counters only: never an answer, a hidden value, an address or a user agent. The AI draft's two routes ride
  the settings API's existing `/settings/{proxy+}` (Cognito-authorized). The public config read never writes; the test
  token rides the existing submit. The stack's resource ceiling goes from 415 to 425 (`api-engagement-budget.test.ts`:
  the performance-tier synth is at the 425 gate, which is unchanged).
- `voc-retention` gains `DeleteItem` on voc-aggregates, key-scoped to the test responses' own partitions
  (`FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST` and one workspace id's `WS#{ws}#FEEDBACK_FORM_TEST`, for an erasure or a retention period); it
  cannot delete a form, a revision, a funnel counter or any other row there (pinned in
  `processing-stack-retention.test.ts` and `customer-data-deletes.test.ts`).
- The Feedback Form API's environment adds `PRIMARY_LANGUAGE`.
- The audit-row guard (`lib/utils/audit-row-guard.ts`) names the Feedback Form API's role the writer of `AUDIT#delete`
  in voc-aggregates (a deployment form's delete record and its test responses' delete record; its existing `PutItem`
  there writes them): it may put that partition only, and change or remove no audit row.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy VocApiStack and VocProcessingStack (the retention worker's new grant), then the frontend. No table, index or
  data migration: a version 1 form is migrated when it is read and written as version 2 when someone saves it; its
  responses keep counting under the migrated questions.
- A version 1 form whose texts exceed version 2's limits (a question over 500 characters, for one) keeps being
  served, but its next save, the list's Enable switch included, answers `400` with the field and the rule: shorten
  it in the builder first.
- **Embeds keep working.** Forms embedded or linked before 7.55.00 load the new widget from the API (the iframe page
  and `feedback-widget.js` are served by it); a cached widget that still sends a version 1 body is accepted.
- `has_responses` is marked by the first real response from this release on; a form answered only before reads it
  from its stored responses (`GET /feedback-forms/{id}` counts them), so the builder locks its codes and ids as soon
  as it is opened, and the server's lock (`answers_locked`) holds from its next real response.
- Test links are for administrators: only an admin (of the workspace, else of the deployment) issues, rotates or
  reads the token (Test tab, or `POST …/test-link`), so an editor's Test and Share tabs show no test link. Test
  responses are deleted by an admin or the form's creator only; a form created before 7.55.00 has no recorded creator,
  so its admins only.
- From this release a deployment form's delete leaves an `AUDIT#delete` row in voc-aggregates (deletes before it left
  none; a workspace form's delete was already recorded).
- Stop on an AI draft ends the browser's wait only; the job runs to its end on the settings assist worker and its
  Bedrock call is billed as before.
- The funnel counts from this release on: a view whose dates start before it shows Reach. Its two beacons have their
  own route and rate limit, apart from real responses ([docs/feedback-forms.md](docs/feedback-forms.md#the-funnel));
  a throttled beacon costs one funnel count and nothing the visitor sees.
- The assistant's `update_feedback_form` no longer offers the version 1 fields; an old conversation that proposes them
  gets the card's "invalid request".
- The widget's start word in Polish stays "Rozpocznij", and its de/es/fr/pt/ja/zh/ko words were written without a
  translator: they are worth a review.

## [7.54.00] - 2026-11-17

Administration is redesigned around what an administrator comes to do: it opens on a **home** with search and **Needs
attention**, and its nine tabs are grouped by how often they come up (Everyday: People, Data sources, Logs; Regularly:
Categories, Feedback boards; Set up once: AI models, Brand & appearance; Rare: Privacy, Platform), one page each, at new
paths with no aliases. People is one table with an editor in a side sheet; Data sources has a This workspace |
Deployment switch and an Advanced fold; every card says "Saved" the one way. This release also closes the
7.51.01–7.54.00 batch: it is shipped together, the package versions go from 7.51.0 to 7.54.0, and the settings pages
get 7.51.01's tooltips.

### Added

- **The Administration home** (`/admin`, `SettingsHome.tsx`):
  - search (`SettingsSearch.tsx`, an APG combobox over `settingsIndex.ts`: every tab and card, plus Agents › Spend and
    Connections and Account › Preferences, with each locale's own terms, `settings:search.terms.*`; `/` focuses it on
    Administration pages; "Erase" finds Privacy › Erasure first, "GDPR" finds Privacy);
  - **Needs attention** in a `role="status"`, hidden when empty: sources a breaker paused, enabled people with no way of
    working saved, AI models this account cannot call (from the reads the pages already make: `/sources/status`,
    `/users`, `/settings/model/capacity`; the Logs count from `/logs/summary?days=1`);
  - the Everyday cards with their counts, the other groups as links, Elsewhere, and "Version X · Release notes"
    (`/admin/version`).
- **Navigation** (`adminTabs.ts`, `adminTabLabels.ts`, `adminPaths.ts`, `useAdminLocation.ts`, `AdminNav.tsx`): one page
  per tab with a "← Administration" header, its name and its job; from `lg` a grouped
  `<nav aria-label="Administration">` with `aria-current="page"`. A path that names a section scrolls to and focuses its
  card (`SectionAnchor.tsx`). Paths: `/admin/people[/<username>|/invite]`,
  `/admin/sources[/<source>|/inbox|/radar|/tokens][?scope=deployment]`, `/admin/logs`, `/admin/categories[/dimensions]`,
  `/admin/boards[/<id>|/domains|/participants]`, `/admin/ai`, `/admin/brand[/theme]`, `/admin/privacy[/erasure]`,
  `/admin/platform[/deployment-brand]` (platform admins only), `/admin/version`. `adminPaths.ts` is the one query reader
  (`scope`, pinned in `locationParams.test.ts`).
- **People** (`components/UserAdmin`): one table (Name, Role, Way of working, Flags, Status, Edit) and a person's editor
  on the new **SideSheet** (`components/SideSheet`: `ModalShell` with `placement="end"`, `.sheet-panel`,
  `--animate-slide-in-end`): role, category and source access, way of working (7.50.02's Not set, comparison and
  radiogroup kept), fallback owner, memory reviewer, platform admin, name, reset password, disable or enable, and Delete
  at the foot. **Invite person** is the tab's one primary.
- **Data sources** (`DataSourcesPage.tsx`): the This workspace | Deployment switch for platform admins inside a
  workspace (the deployment's sources are no longer a tab of their own), the two-sentence deployment notice, cards
  health first (paused or failing on top, the order fixed on first read), 7.50.02's GitHub Issues managed view, and
  Advanced with Email inbox, Radar and Design-system tokens (Integrations before), in this workspace's view only.
- **One Saved pattern** (`components/SavedStatus`): every card says "Saved" in a `role="status"` until its next edit;
  the 3 s and 2 s timers and the page-level Save are gone (brand, source credentials, theme, AI models, boards, domains,
  participant email, Radar, Exa, inbox caps, draft editors, categories, People).

### Changed

- Feedback boards takes the Participant email card; Privacy holds Source policies and the erasure panels; Platform the
  workspaces and the deployment brand; Brand & appearance the brand card (its own Save, with the unsaved-changes guard
  on leaving the tab), the default theme and, in dev builds, the API endpoint under Advanced.
- Account opens on Preferences (`/account`; the tab bar keeps Profile first).
- Copy: the tabs', sections', home's, search's and scope's keys in 9 locales; every "Administration → …" pointer, the
  assistant's guidance and tool text, and the backend messages that named the old places (design references, archive
  imports, Radar, failure reasons, alerts) name the new ones; links across the app use the new paths, Agents' included
  (`ReadinessChecks`, the setup guide's prerequisites, `agents:openSources`).
- **Readiness's fixes** (`lambda/engineering/readiness.py`, the batch): "Administration → People" at `/admin/people`,
  and the deployment's GitHub Issues card at `/admin/sources/github_issues?scope=deployment`.
- **One side sheet** (the batch): the shared document component's `sheet` variant (7.52.00) is this release's
  `SideSheet`, with a new `size="wide"` (44rem from `sm`): the sheet's own title, the document's details as its
  description, the decision or Close in its footer. History's Open and Compare open on it (they were a centred dialog).
- **Tooltips on the settings pages** (7.51.01's migration, which waited for this release): their 26 native titles
  (pages/Settings, components/UserAdmin, pages/Account) become `Tooltip` (`label` for the selects and icon buttons,
  `description` for a mode's meaning, a test's model and cost, a raw source id behind its name, a breaker's full error,
  counts and hints), `TruncatedText` (names, ids, messages) and an `InfoTip` (the PR/FAQ and PRD unlocks); the S3 notice's
  title, which only repeated it, is dropped. The admin-gated controls on Settings follow Scrapers: focusable with
  `aria-disabled`, saying why in their tooltip and description, translated (`common:adminOnly`; the English
  `ADMIN_ONLY_TITLE` constant is gone): the Enabled switch, Save to Secrets Manager, the breaker's Reset and the
  validation logs' Clear. The native-title ratchet holds 9 titles in 7 files (the flow canvas and the document editor).
- **Repository code may run read-only git on its checkout** (the batch, the owner's choice; `unit_runner.code_git_env`):
  a repository's gate script, its tests and tools like setuptools-scm can run `git status`, `diff`, `ls-files`, `log`
  and `describe` on `/work/repo` as `code`, where every git command exited 128 ("detected dubious ownership": the
  checkout is the agent's, found in 7.51.03). Repository-code commands only, never the agent's own, get
  `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2` with `safe.directory` set to exactly `/work/repo` and `/work/repo.git` (never a wildcard),
  which git reads as protected command-line configuration, and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; the runner's values win (a
  command's environment holds no other `GIT_*` variable, and an `/exec` call carries none). The git directory stays
  closed to `code` (a commit, an add, a ref, a tag or `git config` fails with "Permission denied"), the agent's git
  still names its git directory and work tree (a `.git` file `code` changes or replaces moves only `code`'s own git),
  and a repository below the working tree stays refused. `CHECKOUT_DIR` and `GIT_DIR` move to `unit_runner`
  (`checkout.py` imports them). Proof: the python image built locally, run with `--network none` and no
  credentials, through its own runner behind the namespace walls: as `code` the five commands exit 0 (128 without
  the runner's keys) and the five writes fail; as `unit` the checkout and the agent's commands exit 0; a nested
  repository is refused; `test_engineering_namespaces.py` 11 passed as root (6 passed, 5 skipped as `unit`).
  [autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#runtime-one-agentcore-session-per-agent).

### Removed

- `DeploymentDataSources.tsx` (its test became `DataSourcesPage.test.tsx`), `SectionSwitch.tsx`, `UserFlagsPanel`,
  `PlatformAdminPanel`, `AiModePanel`, `UserSettingsPanel.tsx`, `useUserSettingSave.ts`, `EditUserModal.tsx`,
  `hooks/useResetAfter.ts` (with their tests); the mobile dropdown, the page-level Save and Header, `BrandConfigSection`;
  the old `tabs.*` / `sections.*` keys and other dead keys in 9 locales; unused props (`SavedStatus.className`,
  `SideSheet.dismissable`, `NameFields.autoFocusFirst`, `RefusalAlert.className`); `constants/admin.ts` (the batch).

### Fixed

- **The run coordinator waits for its agents** (the batch; the first live engineering run, `01M7QNAR1101DZW2A48J24PSN6`
  on b-, 2026-11-18: its coordinator posted the classify task, launched the understander, read "classify running",
  was nudged and called `finish` with the run unfinished, so the run stalled with no live agent). A new coordinator
  tool, `wait_for_agents` (`runtime/harness/waiting.py`, in the harness's own registry, so the Converse loop, the CLI
  and Kiro get it alike): it opens a wait on its lease (a one-line progress step with `waiting`, which
  `board_client.progress` now sends), looks at its inbox every 5 s and at the board each minute, renewing the lease,
  and returns at the first news (a task done, failed or needing a person, an agent that stopped, a question,
  steering, a waited task the board shows ended or re-posted), on a pause (checkpointed, the session paused) or after
  25 minutes ("no news yet: read the flow and the board, then wait again"); it renews the lease, then closes the wait.
  Its `finish` is refused while an agent still works on a run that can go on (its flow running, or none, and no task
  failed twice): "agents are still working on …: call wait_for_agents". It is nudged with "Continue with your tools:
  if agents are working, call wait_for_agents; when the flow has finished, call finish." The coordinator's skill is
  v6 (Steps, a rule and an example; both bundles and its Kiro config compiled), and the board's `tasks` op and
  `read_board` name the `agent` on each task. The wake path it needs: a task's end (`task.done`, `task.failed`,
  `task.needs_human`) and the supervisor's `run.agent_timed_out` and `run.agent_failed` are addressed to the run, so
  they reached no inbox; they now also go to the conductor's inbox and wake the coordinator (`bus/routing.py`
  `CONDUCTOR_NOTICES`, `delivery.py`). A delivery to a coordinator whose wait no tick has seen yet gives it the wake
  grace, which its lease shows (`Supervisor._woken`), so the next tick does not suspend it with its news unread. A
  pause without news leaves the wait open (a long wait is then held without a session until a message continues it),
  a pause with news closes it (the CLI's and Kiro's harness too), and a coordinator's continuation closes a wait its
  last session left open; on Kiro, steering also wakes the tool server's wait. The local fake run's scripted coordinator waits for each agent's `task.done` through the inbox router and the
  delivery function (12/12, to its pull request).
  [autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#the-coordinator-waits-for-its-agents-75400).
- **Reviewers read the submitted patch, and a review that could not review is not a pass** (the batch; the live run
  `01M7QXJN02WSFMG92VWWZ00NKB` on b-, 2026-11-18: its commit reviewer's task named the fixer's patch key in its text
  only, `read_file` refused it as no file of the checkout, the reviewer read the unchanged files, finished "neither an
  approval nor a rejection" with no finding, and the board step passed `review.no_blocking` on zero findings). The
  roles that judge a submitted patch without running code (commit reviewer, PR reviewer, final go) get `read_patch`
  (`runtime/harness/review_tools.py`): the patch the task names, read through the agent's own role, as data, in pages
  of at most 40 000 characters cut at line ends, the first listing the changed files; a task that names none, a key that
  is no submitted patch of the run or an object that cannot be read is a refusal that says so. A reviewer's checkout
  has that patch applied before its first turn (the harness's own git; one that does not apply is told to the model),
  so `read_file` shows the changed files too, and a CLI's or Kiro's tool server is handed the key (`VOC_PATCH_KEY`).
  The coordinator's `post_task` takes `patch` for the reviewers and requires it for a commit reviewer. The reviewers
  record a verdict with `write_review` (`voc-review/1` under `_review/`: `approve` or `request_changes` only after
  every page was read, a request for changes with a blocking finding, an approval with none; `could_not_review`
  always); their `finish` waits for one, and `could_not_review` ends the task needing a person, so the board step
  blocks instead of closing. `review.no_blocking` with a reviewer as `by` fails on no review record, a
  `could_not_review` (or unreadable) one or a request for changes; the board reads `_review/*` for it (its
  `ReadRecordedOutputs` grant). Skills: commit reviewer v3, PR reviewer v3, final go v4 (pending, promote-pending),
  coordinator v7; both bundles and the Kiro configs compiled. The local fake run's reviewer reads the patch through
  `read_patch` and finds the fixed file in its checkout (12/12, to its pull request); a fake run whose reviewer cannot
  read its patch stops at the board, at a person, with `review.no_blocking` failing.
  [autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#the-agent-catalog).
- **The gate installs into its own environment, and a stopped gate goes to a person** (the batch; the same run: its
  gate runner's `py.install` ran `pip install` into the image's `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages`, which
  repository code (`code`, in its own user namespace) cannot write, exited 1 with `Errno 13`, pytest was not run, the
  gate STOPPED, and the coordinator posted "Revise the divide fix after the gate" for a new fixer). The python pack
  makes a virtual environment per root first (`py.venv`: `{base_python} -I -m venv --clear {venv}`, a setup step,
  its pip the standard library's own), under `/home/code/.voc-gate/venvs` in the images (`gate_tools.IMAGE_VENVS`,
  outside the checkout), and `{python}` is that environment's interpreter, so the install (still `-I`, `--isolated`,
  wheels only, PyPI, the one step with the registries) lands there and every later step runs against it
  (`quality_gate/packs.py` `{venv}`, `{base_python}`; a local plan without one keeps the interpreter it was given). The
  node, rust and java packs already write only code-writable places (the checkout, `/opt/voc/cache`). Shown in the
  python image (local tag, `--network none`, the namespace walls, a local wheel index): the old command fails as
  `code` with `Errno 13`; `py.venv`, `py.install` and pytest pass. When no check judged the code, `run_gate` says the
  gate stopped with its own reason (`setup_failed`, `nothing_checked`, `tool_missing`: `packs.STOPS`, the bundle's
  `gates.stops`); the gate runner's record is then STOPPED with that reason (a NO-GO refused), and its `finish` ends
  the task needing a person. Only a NO-GO starts a revision round (gate runner v4, coordinator v7).
  [gates/README.md](voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/gates/README.md).

### Upgrade notes

- **No address of before is aliased.** `/admin/access/users`, `/admin/data-sources[/…]`, `/admin/taxonomy/…`,
  `/admin/system/…` and the other old tabs open the Administration home; an unknown section opens its tab. Update
  bookmarks and runbooks ([account-vs-admin.md](docs/account-vs-admin.md) has the table of old and new paths).
- No routes, IAM or stacks are added or changed by the redesign; deploy the frontend (and, for the batch, the stacks as
  the 7.51.0x–7.53.00 notes below say: VocProcessingStack, then VocApiStack, then the frontend).
- The e2e specs that name Administration's places (inventory, surfaces, boards, workspace admin, modals, …) are updated
  but were not run here (they need a deployment).
- **Rebuild the four engineering images** (python, node, rust, java) for repository code's read-only git: the runner
  they ship sets it. The build arguments are unchanged; push each with a new tag and deploy the digests with
  `-c engineeringImages` ([deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)). Until then sessions run the old runner, where
  repository code's git still exits 128 on the checkout.
- **Rebuild the four engineering images again for the coordinator's wait** (python, node, rust, java): the harness
  and the compiled bundle they ship carry `wait_for_agents`, its finish rule and the v6 skill; until then a
  coordinator runs the old harness and can still finish while its agents work. Deploy VocProcessingStack too: the
  inbox router and the delivery function route a task's end to the conductor's inbox, and the board's `tasks` op
  names each task's agent. No IAM, table or stack resource changes.
- **Rebuild the four engineering images once more for the reviewers and the gate** (python, node, rust, java): the
  harness, the gate packs and the compiled bundle they ship carry `read_patch`, `write_review`, the reviewer's applied
  checkout, the gate's own virtual environment and its stops. Until then a reviewer still cannot read its patch, a
  python gate still installs into the image's site-packages, and a stopped gate is still finished as done. Deploy
  VocProcessingStack too: the board reads the reviewers' verdicts (`ReadRecordedOutputs` gains
  `ws/default/runs/*/*/commits/*/_review/*`, read only), and its `review.no_blocking` fails a board whose reviewer
  recorded none.

## [7.53.00] - 2026-11-17

Agents can run as **Kiro CLI over ACP**, for a whole deployment or for chosen roles, with the native harness still the
default. A **scheduled cross-run Learn pass**, off by default, reads a flow's recent runs once a week and only proposes.
**MCP for runs** lets a local Kiro or Claude agent follow, analyse and steer runs through the global MCP server and ask
for a Run now that an administrator confirms in the app. The harness's shipped skills and platform rules are now read
from the compiled bundle, one source of truth.

### Added

- **The Kiro harness** (`runtime/harness/kiro.py`, `runtime/harness/acp.py`, `runtime/harness_switch.py`,
  `lib/stacks/engineering-kiro.ts`, `engineering-images/common/install-kiro.sh`).
  - `-c engineeringHarness=native|kiro|kiro:<role>,<role>`, `native` by default (`ENGINEERING_HARNESS` on the runtime,
    the start function and readiness). A role on Kiro launches its skill with `--adapter kiro --kiro-version 3.4.0
    --kiro-key-parameter <param>`; the session row keeps that argv, so a continuation stays on the harness it started on
    (skill records still say `harness: converse`).
  - kiro-cli (`kiro-cli acp --agent-engine=v3`) is the harness's child: it runs as `unit` in the harness's namespace,
    its only way out the agent's proxy, with an isolated HOME (`~/.voc/kiro/home`, wiped each start), from an empty work
    directory, never the checkout. Its one MCP server is the harness's own tool server, which serves exactly the
    session's tools from the harness's registry (so 7.52.00's `read_tenets` and `write_tenets` arrive with no edit); no
    Kiro builtin is ever offered. The session's agent config is the compiled `kiro-agents/<role>.json`, now shipped in
    every image and MCP-only (`tools: ["@voc"]`, `allowedTools` and one `mcp` allow rule naming exactly those tools).
  - The ACP mapping: the brief is `initialize` (no fs or terminal capability), `session/new {cwd, mcpServers: []}`,
    `set_config_option mode=<role>` (refused unless Kiro reports that mode), then `session/prompt`; steering and the
    run's direction are a mid-turn `session/prompt` in the `<<<STEERING>>>` fence (the first turn ends `cancelled`, each
    stop reason recorded); a person's Stop, a Shut down or a save-and-stop is `session/cancel`, a 30 s wait for
    `cancelled`, kiro-cli ended, a checkpoint and exit 75; `session/update` maps to progress (coalesced message and
    thought chunks; Kiro's own and refused tool calls as `tool_call` / `tool_result`); `request_permission` answers
    `allow_once` only for an offered `@voc/<tool>`, else `reject_once`, never `allow_always`; `fs/*` and `terminal/*` are
    method-not-found; a resume is `session/load` from the Kiro session saved with each checkpoint
    (`_kiro/attempt-<n>/<seq>-<nonce>.tgz`, named in `position.kiro`; a child run's `seed_restart` copies it as
    `_seed/<task>/kiro.tgz`), falling back to 7.51.00's notes or seed.
  - The key: an operator stores a SecureString at `/[<prefix>-]voc/engineering/_kiro/api-key`; the harness reads it
    just in time and passes it only in kiro-cli's environment (the tool server's environment is blanked).
  - Readiness: an advisory `kiro` check (the key's type only, never its value; its label in 9 locales). The runner
    reports `kiro_cli`.
- **The scheduled cross-run Learn pass** (`learning/cross_run*.py`, `lib/stacks/engineering-cross-run.ts`):
  `-c engineeringCrossRunLearn=weekly|off`, `off` by default (the one Scheduler schedule, Mondays 06:00 UTC, is created
  DISABLED). Once per flow per ISO week (one claim each), within Learn's `budget_share` of the flow's monthly budget, it
  reads the flow's runs of the last 28 days, counts their recurring failures, step times and costs, makes at most one
  model call, and only proposes (lessons as drafts, skill additions as proposed versions behind the benchmark gate).
  The record is `ws/default/learn/<flow>/<week>/v1.json`, read by `GET /agents/engineering/learn`.
- **MCP for runs** (`lambda/shared/mcp_global_tools_engineering.py`, docs/mcp.md): five tools for a write token minted
  by an administrator who still is one, each admitted for its one operation and never as an admin, and audited (the two
  that act at most 20 an hour per token): `engineering_runs_list`, `engineering_run_get`, `engineering_run_analysis`
  (`GET /agents/engineering/<run>/retrospective`, new: Learn's record of the run, with `cross_run` the flow's newest
  weekly record), `engineering_run_steer` (the minter's steering, marked as sent from a local assistant) and
  `engineering_run_request`. A request for a Run now is a row (`engineering/run_requests.py`, `WS#default#RUNREQ#queue`)
  that waits 24 hours for an administrator to confirm or decline it in Agents → Runs (`RunRequests`:
  `GET/POST /agents/engineering/requests`, `GET …/requests/automations`, `POST …/requests/<id>/confirm|decline`); the
  `voc-runs` MCP skill. TENETS.md tenet 4 says how.

### Changed

- **The shipped skills come from the bundle** (`runtime/harness/skills.py`): every shipped skill and the platform rules
  are read from the compiled bundle the image (`/opt/voc/orchestration/bundle.json`) or the Lambda ships; the
  hand-written records are gone (they lagged the templates: the coordinator is now v5 with `relay_steering` and
  `set_direction`, the understander 7.52.00's v4), and a test holds every role to the bundle's record.
- Every image installs kiro-cli 3.4.0 (the musl arm64 build from `prod.download.cli.kiro.dev`, checked against its
  published sha256) and ships the compiled Kiro configs, whatever the harness.
- `kiro` is an artifact kind beside 7.52.00's `tenets` (`workspace/layout.py`, `runtime/checkpoints.py`).

### IAM (pinned in the CDK tests)

- **Roles on Kiro only:** `KiroApiKey` (`ssm:GetParameter` on exactly the key's ARN) and `KiroApiKeyDecrypt`
  (`kms:Decrypt` of the stack's key through SSM only, conditioned on `kms:EncryptionContext:PARAMETER_ARN`).
- **voc-engineering-runtime:** `RestartReadsKiroSessions` (a restart's copy of the saved Kiro session); the cross-run
  pass's `CrossRunListsIndex` (`s3:ListBucket` held to the index's prefix), `CrossRunReadsManifests`, `CrossRunRecords`
  (`s3:PutObject` on `ws/default/learn/*`, create-only) and `CrossRunRows` (GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem on
  `WS#*#LEARN#*`); the schedule's own role invokes the runtime and nothing else.
- **voc-agents-api:** `RunRequests` (PutItem and UpdateItem on `WS#*#RUNREQ#*` by `dynamodb:LeadingKeys`, no delete);
  GetObject and a listing on `ws/default/learn/*`; `ssm:DescribeParameters` only when a role is on Kiro.
- **Egress** (the agent proxy only): `runtime.us-east-1.kiro.dev`, `management.us-east-1.kiro.dev` and
  `ssm.<region>.amazonaws.com`.
- The MCP Lambda and the agent roles gain nothing. cdk-nag acknowledgements 135 → 137 (the learn records' put and read).

### Upgrade notes

- **Rebuild all four engineering images** and deploy their digests (`engineeringImages`), even on the native harness:
  each now carries kiro-cli and the Kiro configs, and readiness's `kiro` check reads the runner's report.
- **The Kiro API key is stored by an operator**, once, before a role runs on Kiro (no stack or function writes it):
  `aws ssm put-parameter --region <region> --name /voc/engineering/_kiro/api-key --type SecureString --key-id
  alias/<the deployment's voc-datalake-key alias> --value "file://<a file holding only the key>"`
  (`/<prefix>-voc/engineering/_kiro/api-key` on a prefixed deployment; `--overwrite` to replace it). The sessions' way
  out must admit the three egress hosts above. Keep `engineeringHarness=native` until a live run on Kiro has been
  checked in a test account: kiro-cli behind the namespaces, the proxy and the NAT on AgentCore, the key read with the
  agent's role, `session/load` across two microVMs and an hour-long tool call have not run live yet.
- Deploy VocProcessingStack (runtime, start function, the schedule), then VocApiStack (the Agents API's routes and
  grants), then the frontend.
- The cross-run pass stays off until `-c engineeringCrossRunLearn=weekly`; it has no UI and no per-automation setting.
- Not built: push notices and watchers (AppSync); a Kiro session's tokens are not counted (Kiro bills its own
  credits).

## [7.52.00] - 2026-11-17

The engineering agents get their **Registry** (every role's card composed on the server, and cards made from an
accepted skill), the **quality gates' and the assertions' data**, flows that **call another flow** at a pinned revision,
**Used by** and the shared-flow guard, an exact **Paused** state, and the **knowledge flows**: an approved knowledge
pack's `docs/agents/**` and the accepted tenets' `TENETS.md` opened as a pull request through the broker, a versioned
tenets store with its flow, and triage held to the accepted tenets. The run workspace's reads gain a run's expansion,
each agent's card, and a gate read with each check's pack and language, the round, the tools' versions and the
final go's decision. A person can write a skill version as a proposal. The web app gets **one document component**
(X1): Projects documents, History and the review page read, edit and compare through `DocumentSurface`, with Compare
and merge on a stale save. The web app gets **Agent orchestration** (Automations with one state each, the Set up
drawer, an automation's page, Spend and Connections rebuilt), **the flow canvas** (each kind its shape, one canvas and
inspector for build, view and run, the shared-flow guard) and **the Registry, Skills, Knowledge and Tenets** screens.

### Added

- **The knowledge docs pull request** (7.52 A).
  - Approving a knowledge pack version records the repository docs it renders to (`knowledge/render_docs.py`: pure;
    `docs/agents/index.md` and one `docs/agents/<package path>.md` per approved package, the root as
    `repository.md`, `index` or `repository` packages as `*-package.md`, two packages on one file refused; the
    `rendering_digest` is the sha256 of the sorted `[(path, sha256)]` JSON). `PackStore.approve` writes the digest
    on the version and its `KPACKLOG` row, with `KDOCS` and a create-only `KDOCSLOG#<n>`, in one transaction (two
    racing approvals: one is 409).
  - Routes (`lambda/shared/agents_engineering_knowledge_routes.py`, administrators acting for themselves, 404 while
    the module is off): `GET /agents/engineering/knowledge/<conn>[/<pkg>/versions/<v>]`, `POST …/approve`;
    `GET /agents/engineering/tenets/<conn>[/versions/<v>]`, `POST …/versions/<v>/accept|reject`;
    `GET /agents/engineering/docs/<conn>/preview?kind=knowledge|tenets` (`{files: [{path, sha256, bytes, text}],
    digest, approved_digest, matches, branch, patch, patch_truncated, texts_truncated}`); `POST …/docs/<conn>/publish`
    `{kind, digest, pr?}` → 202 `{pr: {url, number, branch}, kind, version, digest, draft}`, or 409 `human_driven`
    (the API checks the stored way of working first), `already_published`, `digest_mismatch`, `not_approved`.
  - The broker's `push_approved_docs`, voc-engineering-start's alone (every agent role and the runtime get 403): the
    credential must name the stored repository; the approval is rendered again and the request's, the approval's and
    the rendering's digests must be one; `write_policy.docs_paths` allows `docs/agents/**` for the knowledge and
    exactly `TENETS.md` for the tenets, 4 MB at most; the requester's stored way of working is read again, failing
    closed; the CI attestation and branch rules apply; one bot commit on `voc-agent/docs/<kind>-v<n>` from the
    default branch's head (`RepositoryHost.tree_with`: a Git Data tree on GitHub, worked out from listings on
    GitLab), and a ready or draft pull request (`pr`, else the flow's own). The push and the pull request are claims
    in `WS#default#DOCS#<conn>`: a failed open is retried from the pushed branch, a second publish answers `repeated`.
    voc-engineering-start's `publish_docs` (`runtime/docs_publish.py`) asks it.
- **The tenets** (7.52 A).
  - A versioned store in `WS#default#REPO#<conn>` (`knowledge/tenets.py`): `TENETS` (the counter, the accepted
    version with its `TENETS.md` digest and ids), `TENETS#<v>`, create-only `TENETSLOG#<v>#<event>` and
    `TENETSRUN#<run>` (one draft per run). Accept never moves the accepted version down; reject keeps the version.
  - The **Tenets flow** (`flows/tenets.yaml`, the sixth default flow, after Understand): the understander reads the
    approved pack, the repository's `TENETS.md` and the accepted tenets, and writes `voc-tenets/1` once with
    `write_tenets` under `_tenets/attempt-<n>/`; `runtime/tenets_end.py` drafts it at the run's end. Its draft step
    asserts `tenets.recorded`.
  - The understander's card and skill are v4 (`read_tenets`, `write_tenets`; the shipped Python fallback too).
    `issue-triage` v3 requires `tenets`; `understand-repository` v3 states `pr: ready`.
  - **Triage cites accepted tenets only** (`outputs.unaccepted_tenets`): `write_triage` refuses an id the accepted
    version does not hold and says which are accepted; the triage run's end refuses the trusted row
    (`unaccepted_tenet`); with none accepted only `[]` passes. Readiness's `tenets` check reads the accepted version
    (pass, or warn with none; never blocking), and `pack` names the docs' rendering.
- **The Registry** (7.52 B; `lambda/shared/agents_engineering_registry_routes.py`, `lambda/engineering/registry/`):
  `GET /agents/engineering/registry?connection=&month=` (every role's card composed on the server: its template, the
  skill the scope runs, model, tools, gates, contracts, caps, scorecard and the month's spend; per-connection heads
  without `?connection=`; the contract that every role has a card whose id is the role), `GET …/registry/<card>`,
  and `POST …/registry/cards` `{from_skill: {role, connection?, version}, slug, purpose, title?, model?, caps?,
  expected_version?}` → 201 `{card}` (an accepted skill version's model, tools and harness; caps at most the
  template's; `WS#default#AGENTCARD#<id>` with `HEAD`, `VER#n`, `LOG#n#created` and the listing, in one transaction).
- **The quality gates' data** (7.52 B and the integration): `GET /agents/engineering/gates?connection=` →
  `{packs, aliases, own_gate, briefs, runners, defaults, stops, connection}`: each pack's tools, steps (every manifest
  field, `messages`, `looked_at_nothing`) and briefs; the briefs as `{id, path, packs, digest, bytes}`;
  `stops` `check_failed`, `looked_at_nothing`, `own_gate_changed`, `review_blocked`, `rounds_used_up` (each

  from the connection's newest gate record (null otherwise). `GET …/gates/briefs/<id>` →
  `{id, path, packs, digest, bytes, text}`.
- **The assertions vocabulary** (7.52 B): `GET /agents/engineering/assertions` → `{checks: [{check, asks, label_key,

- **Template sources** (the integration): `GET /agents/engineering/templates/<kind>/<id>/source` →

- **A person's skill version** (the integration): `POST /agents/engineering/skills/<role>/versions?connection=`

- **`call_flow`** (7.52 B; `shared/flow_expand.py`): a step that runs another saved flow at a pinned revision

- **Used by and the shared-flow guard** (7.52 B): `GET /workflows[/<id>]` answer `used_by {automations, flows}`;

- **Paused** (7.52 B): `POST /agents/<id>/pause` and `…/resume` (an automation that is on; audited rows; the
