## [7.51.04] - 2026-11-17

The run workspace now says when a run has stopped, and why. The owner's first real run waited for a person because its orchestrator could not check out the repository (exit 128, "detected dubious ownership"), yet the canvas still showed "Understand and classify" spinning with "You are here", the timeline put coordinator-1 "On no step of the flow" beside an empty "Agents: 0" step, and the thread read "1 booting (tokens 0, cost_usd 0.00)". Now a banner says what happened, the step where the run stopped reads as failed, the orchestrator has its own row, and the supervisor's lines are in plain words.

### Added

- **The end banner** (`RunEndBanner.tsx`, `runEnd.ts`). Shown at the top of the workspace, for an admin, whenever the run waits for a person, failed or was stopped. It says:
  - what happened, in plain words: a checkout that failed, the orchestrator or another agent that failed, the decision point the run waits at (budget, 30 days, checkout cache, a flow step), or a person's Stop;
  - which agent ("Agent: coordinator-1 (the orchestrator)"), at which step, and the cost so far;
  - why: the supervisor's stored reason (7.51.03's `needs_human_detail`), else the flow's reason at a step's decision point, else the agent's `last_failure`, else its last exit code; when nothing records why, it says so and points to the agent's session;
  - the last failed command behind "Show details": where the agent was, the exit code, how long it ran, and the end of its stderr (redacted by the server);
  - what to do next with the run's own controls: Resume (after raising the budget, at a spent one), Stop then Restart run where this deployment can't send Resume, or Restart run once the run has ended. It has a "Go to the run's controls" button (focus moves to the control bar) and a button that opens the failed agent's session. The banner itself acts on nothing.

  It is toned by meaning: danger when something failed, warn when the run waits for a person's decision, muted when a person stopped it.
- **The overview says why** (`engineering/run_overview.py`, `monitor.py`). Each agent gains `last_exit` (`{exit_code, timed_out, duration_seconds, stderr_tail}`, never stdout) and `last_failure`, both from the supervisor's inspection data. The run gains `waiting_detail`, META's `needs_human_detail`, given only while the run is at a person. Each text is redacted and stripped of control characters as the thread is (`views_thread.display`), within 500 characters. The web app also reads the `flow_outcome` the overview already sent. No new IAM.
- **The supervisor's lines in plain words** (`supervisorLines.ts`, `SupervisorLine.tsx`). Each known line maps to an i18n string, with the raw text behind "Details":
  - "1 booting (tokens 0, cost_usd 0.00)" → "Starting… · $0.00";
  - "… continued in a new session (n) … after crash" → "coordinator-1 stopped unexpectedly and was restarted (attempt n + 1 of 3)";
  - "… crashed 3 times." → "coordinator-1 failed 3 times; the run needs a person" (for an agent that isn't the orchestrator: "its task goes to a new agent");
  - "… could not start. <reason>" (7.51.03), "stopped answering", "found no free agent session", and "Stopped: n session(s) ended." each read the same way.

  A run of the same health line one after another becomes one line that shows the latest ("said 3 times"). The supervisor is named as the sender, and an ended thread says how its session ended ("This session has ended: it failed.").
- **Dev mock and shared fixture.** The test world and the fixture gain a run at a person whose orchestrator failed at its checkout (`failed_run_id`, `failed_overview`, `failed_thread`): `checkout_failed`, the stored reason, exit 128 with its stderr, two crash restarts, and the supervisor's lines. The mock serves its overview and its orchestrator's thread, and lists it in Agents → Runs.

### Changed

- **Step state from the run's real state** (`runFlow.ts`, `runLanes.ts`, `runTimelineModel.ts`). Once the run ended or waits for a person, the step where it stopped is marked "Stopped here". It reads as failed (danger) when an agent or the checkout failed, as needing a person (warn) at a decision, or as stopped (muted), and nothing spins. Any other step still under way reads as paused (run at a person) or stopped (ended run). While the run is under way, a step spins only when an agent is at work on it; a step whose turn it is with nobody on it shows a still "ready" mark.
  - Lanes follow their agent's session: held agents read as paused, a task at a person as needing a person (never failed).
  - The run's orchestrator is now the newest coordinator started (a Resume's replacement, not the failed one).
- **The orchestrator is the run's own**, not a stray lane. The timeline opens with an "Orchestrator" row (who, its session's status, its attempts); the canvas shows it as a strip above the steps that opens its session. A step with no agent has no chevron and says "No agents yet", "Not started" or "No agents".
- **Canvas state layers** (UX part 5 N7, N8, N10, N11, the cheap part; the node redesign is 7.52 C).
  - The conductor's `human` reads as waiting for a person, `stopped` as stopped and `skipped` as skipped, each with its own badge (Hand, CirclePause, Square, SkipForward).
  - "You are here" and "Stopped here" are tags, not a ring; the open lane has the selected fill.
  - Neutral outlines answer a hover. Nothing is dimmed by opacity, and lane borders are at full strength.
  - `focusStepId` centres on the marked step first.
- i18n: the new strings are in all 9 locales.

## [7.51.03] - 2026-11-17

The first real engineering run on AWS (`b-`, `01M7MKH4…`) failed at its first command, the coordinator's checkout. Git refused the checkout cache as "dubious ownership" (exit 128). The supervisor took that for a crash, continued the session twice, and the run went to a person with nothing more than "crashed 3 times". The cache's files now show as the agent user's, so the checkout works. A checkout that fails with an error of its own now ends the agent at once and says why.

### Fixed

- **The checkout cache is the agent user's** (`unit_runner.Runner._mount`):
  - **The cause.** Since 7.50.03 every agent command runs in a user and network namespace of its own (`unshare --user --map-root-user --net`, as `unit`), which maps only `unit`, to uid 0 inside. Root makes the cache's Mountpoint mount, so its files were root's, and root is not mapped in the namespace: they showed there as the overflow uid. Git (2.39 on the Debian bookworm images, too old for a `safe.directory` wildcard) refused a repository its user does not own.
  - **The fix.** `mount-s3 --read-only --allow-other --uid 10001 --gid 10000` (`unit`, group `work`; both flags are in Mountpoint 1.25.0's `--help`, checked in the built image). Inside the agent's namespace the cache is then its own (uid 0). It stays read-only. The modes stay Mountpoint's defaults (0755 and 0644), so nothing changes for `code`, and nothing of repository code's reads the cache.
  - **Every fetch is covered.** This covers the clone and every later lazy fetch of a blob from the cache (a `git show` or `checkout` outside the sparse paths), which a `-c safe.directory=<path>` on the clone alone would not have.
  - **Reproduced in the real image** (the python image built locally, run with `--network none`, no credentials and no ports). The image's own runner and checkout commands, against a cache laid out and owned as each mount shows it:
    - root:root gives git exit 128, "detected dubious ownership in repository at '/mnt/voc-cache/<commit>/g1/repo.git'", as on AWS;
    - unit:work: the clone, the sparse checkout, the checkout, both chmod steps and a lazy fetch of a blob outside the sparse paths all succeed.
- **A checkout command that fails with an error of its own is no crash** (`supervisor.Supervisor._checkout_failed`). Such a failure is an exit code above 0 that is neither a timeout nor a kill, such as git's 128, and a new session would only repeat it. The agent ends `failed` at once, with no continuation. Its reason gives the step, the exit code and the start of its stderr, redacted (the runner's `scrub_text`), on one line of at most 300 characters. For example: "The repository checkout failed (git clone, exit 128): fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at …". The reason is kept:
  - in the agent's inspection data (`last_failure`, beside `last_exit`);
  - in a supervisor message in the run's thread ("coordinator-1 could not start. The repository checkout failed …");
  - on the run's new decision point, `checkout_failed`: its `RUNLOG#` row's `detail` and META's `needs_human_detail`, which a Resume removes (`RunControl.needs_human`'s new `detail`, `RunStore.needs_human`).
  - A worker's task is re-posted with the reason. A person's Resume, once the cause is fixed, launches a new coordinator in place of a failed one, as after a crash. A timeout or a kill is still a crash, continued as before, and a Pause or Shut down asked before the failure is kept.
- **The namespace tests had never run, and three failed when they first did** (`test_engineering_namespaces.py`, in the image under Docker). The code was right; the tests were wrong:
  - The first two expected only `lo` in a new network namespace. Docker Desktop's kernel also makes its fallback tunnels there (`tunl0`, `gre0`, …), down and with no underlay, which `walls.sh` already allows for by counting only the interfaces that are up. The tests now check that only the loopback is up and that anything else is a fallback tunnel.
  - The third read a gone socket's refused connection as an empty answer. When the request reaches the forwarder before it closes, the client gets a reset, which is refused all the same.
- Proof: `test_engineering_local_runtime.py::test_the_cache_is_mounted_read_only_with_its_files_shown_as_the_agent_users` (fails without the fix: no `--uid`/`--gid`) and `test_engineering_supervisor.py::test_a_checkout_its_tool_refuses_ends_the_agent_failed_at_once_and_sends_the_run_to_a_person_saying_why` (fails without it: the agent is continued). The Linux-only `test_engineering_namespaces.py` also gains two tests, run in the image: a cache its user owns is cloned, checked out and lazily fetched from inside the namespace; one another uid owns is refused as dubious (exit 128).
- Siblings: the other root-owned paths a namespaced command touches were checked:
  - `/opt/voc` (the runner, the forwarder, the harness) and `/run/voc` (the session files, which are `unit`'s): read by Python, `cat` and botocore, none of which checks owners.
  - `/work/repo` and `/work/repo.git`: `unit`'s, made in its namespace.
  - **Found, not fixed.** Repository code (`code`, in its own namespace) that runs git on the checkout, such as a repository's own gate script with `git diff` or `git ls-files`, or setuptools-scm, is refused as dubious ownership: the working tree and the git directory are `unit`'s. The same was true under the 7.50.00 firewall wall (`code` ≠ `unit`). Opening the git directory to repository code is a design choice (checkout.py keeps it the agent's), not a certain fix.

### Changed

- Docs: docs/autonomous-engineering.md, Runtime: the mount's ownership and why; a checkout's own failure is no crash, and the `checkout_failed` decision point with its reason.

### Upgrade notes

- **Rebuild all four engineering images** (python, node, java, rust) for linux/arm64 with new tags, and deploy their digests with the stacks (docs/deployment.md, `engineeringImages`; the same Mountpoint and boto3 build arguments). The mount's flags live in the images' runner, so until the new digests are deployed every agent's checkout keeps failing.
- Deploy VocProcessingStack for the supervisor's change (the runtime function's code). No table, index, IAM or route change.
- A run waiting at `coordinator` after "crashed 3 times" from this failure, such as `01M7MKH4KGAMAM1TGR1SYH6CHK` on `b-`: after the images and the stacks are deployed, Resume it where its run monitor's Resume reaches the runtime (a Resume launches a new coordinator, whose checkout then works), or Stop it and rerun its issue.
- **Rollback.** An earlier image mounts the cache as root's again, and its checkouts fail as before. An earlier runtime leaves META's `needs_human_detail` unread.

## [7.51.02] - 2026-11-17

A person's run controls now reach the agents. Until now the run workspace's steering composer, an agent question's Reply, and Pause, Resume and Save a checkpoint worked on no deployment: the Agents API named neither the engineering bus nor the runtime's function, so these controls answered 503 and the workspace showed them off. Only Stop worked, through the start function (7.50.03). Each control now has its own path. Steering and replies are published on the bus by the Agents API, under a grant held to their two detail types. The signals go through the start function, as Stop does. The workspace shows each control from its own flag.

### Fixed

- **Steering and Reply reach the run.** The Agents API publishes `msg.steer` (to the run's orchestrator) and `msg.answer` (to an agent or the conductor) from its own source, `voc.engineering/api`. `ENGINEERING_BUS_NAME` names the bus to it wherever `engineeringAgents=true`.
- **Pause, Resume, Save a checkpoint and an agent's signals reach the run, through voc-engineering-start**, like Stop. The runtime function is still never invoked from the API.
  - **The new action.** The start function's `signal_run` (`{run_id, signal, actor, note?, agent_id?, task_id?, attempt?, restart_from?}`, `lambda/engineering/runtime/run_signals.py`) takes Save, Pause and Resume of the whole run, and an agent's Save, Pause, Resume, Shut down, Stop now and Restart (`checkpoint` or `fresh`). A whole run's Shut down and Stop now stay its Stop (`stop_run`). Anything else is refused before anything is read.
  - **Its checks.** The run must exist and must not have ended. It takes no signal while a Stop of it is under way. The agent needs a session row in the run, and must hold its task at the attempt the person saw. That task must not have ended or be open again.
  - **Its record.** The person's create-only `RUNLOG#<at>#signal#<hex>` row records who asked what of whom, when, and why (the note): D4, `RunStore.record_signal`. It is written before the signal is handed on.
  - **The hand-on.** The signal is handed on asynchronously to voc-engineering-runtime's `signal`, as `stop_run` and `finish_stop` are. The runtime keeps its own refusal of a Resume or Restart during a Stop.
  - **The answer.** The API answers `{signal: {signal, target, attempt, status: sent, agents: {}, applied: {}, at}}`. The overview shows what came of it.
- **The overview says what reaches the run, one flag per path.** `steer_available` (the bus is named), `signals_available` (the start function is named) and `stop_available` replace `actions_available`. `board_available` is false (below).
- **The web app shows each control from its own flag**: the composer and Reply, Pause, Resume and Save, an agent's Stop and ⋯, and the Board tab's controls. A control that is off still says why: "Pause, Resume and Save can't reach this run from this deployment: it names no start function", or the composer's "it doesn't name the engineering bus to the Agents API". The dev mock and the shared fixture carry the new flags and the signal's new answer. All 9 locales are updated.

### IAM

- **The Agents API's role (VocApiStack)** gains one statement, `SpeakOnTheEngineeringBus`:
  - `events:PutEvents` on `arn:<partition>:events:<region>:<account>:event-bus/[<prefix>-]voc-engineering-<account>-<region>` only;
  - with `StringEquals` `events:source` = `voc.engineering/api` and `events:detail-type` = `msg.answer` or `msg.steer`.

  It gets no other `events:` action, no other bus, no other source or type, and still no `lambda:InvokeFunction` on voc-engineering-runtime (pinned in `api-engineering-reads.test.ts`). With the module on, the role has a fixed name, `[<prefix>-]voc-agents-api-<account>-<region>`, so the bus's policy in VocProcessingStack can name it (that stack cannot reference VocApiStack). Without the module the role keeps its generated name.
- **The engineering bus's policy (VocProcessingStack)** admits that role as every publisher is admitted:
  - its ARN joins `OnlyTheEngineeringPublishers`;
  - a new `OwnSourceOnlyAgentsApi` denies it every source but `voc.engineering/api`.

  The detail types are not repeated in the bus's policy, which is near EventBridge's 10,240-character limit: 8,897 characters with 17 statements live on `b-` before this change. A test holds the worst case under the limit.
- **The router** (`bus/senders.py` `API_TYPES`) admits `msg.steer` and `msg.answer` from the API's source and nothing else: no `task.*`, `signal.*` or `skill.*` from it any more. It also drops any event whose `detail-type` is not its message's own type, from any source, so a message cannot claim a type its grant was not checked on.
- **voc-engineering-start's role is unchanged.** `signal_run` uses its run rows' GetItem and PutItem (`StartRunRows`) and its invoke of the runtime (`HandTheLaunchOn`). The role's statements are now pinned one by one (`engineering-runtime.test.ts`).

### Changed

- **Nothing else is said on the bus from the API.** A signal's and a Stop's `signal.*` conversation records are gone; their `RUNLOG#` rows are the record. The Stop's unused `note` is no longer read.
- **A person's board actions stay off.** Post, take, block, priority, move and release publish the board's `task.*` from the API's source, which the bus no longer takes. They now answer 503 before the board is asked, so the board never changes what could not be said. The overview says `board_available: false`. A go on a run publishes nothing and still works. Making them reach a run is a decision for later: it would widen the grant and the router to `task.*`.

### Upgrade notes

- **Deploy VocProcessingStack, then VocApiStack, then the frontend.** VocProcessingStack holds the bus's policy, the router and the start function's `signal_run`. VocApiStack holds the Agents API's grant, its environment and its code.
- **The Agents API's IAM role is replaced** on a deployment with `engineeringAgents=true`: it gains a fixed name, and CloudFormation creates the new role before it deletes the old one. Nothing outside VocApiStack names the old role.
- **No image rebuild** is needed: the runtime's `signal` action is unchanged.
- **Older signal records stay as they were.** Runs signalled before this release have no `RUNLOG#…#signal` rows. A `signal.*` conversation record that an earlier release published (none did on `b-`) stays in its conversation.
- **API callers of `POST …/signals`** get `{signal: {status: sent, …}}` with empty `agents` and `applied`, and should read the overview to see the outcome. Callers of the board's actions get 503.
- **Rollback.** Rolling back removes the grant, the bus name and the router's narrowing together, and gives the Agents API's role its generated name again (another replacement). An earlier release ignores the `RUNLOG#…#signal` rows.

## [7.51.01] - 2026-11-17

Hover hints are instant: the app's one **Tooltip** replaces the native `title`, which waited for the browser's own 1–2 s delay and never showed on keyboard focus. It shows 80 ms after the pointer rests, at once when moving between tooltips and on keyboard focus, and closes on Escape. Native titles on DOM elements fell from 253 (154 files) to 45 (24 files): the ones left wait for the releases that rewrite their files, and a lint rule and a ratchet keep the count from rising (UX spec part 3 §3.6, part 4 §4.6; owner decision of 2026-11-17).

### Added

- **`Tooltip`** (`components/Tooltip/`): `<Tooltip kind="label|description" content placement="top|bottom|start|end">` around exactly one element, composing its handlers and ref.
  - `kind="label"` repeats the trigger's `aria-label` (or `sr-only` name) in an `aria-hidden` bubble; `kind="description"` makes the trigger `aria-describedby` the bubble (`role="tooltip"`), which stays in the page while hidden. An empty `content` shows nothing and never remounts the trigger.
  - **Timing** (`tooltipTiming.ts`): 80 ms after a mouse or pen rests on the trigger (a pointer that only crosses it opens nothing); 0 ms while another tooltip is open or less than 300 ms after one closed (the delay group); at once on keyboard focus moved by Tab or an arrow key (`:focus-visible`), not on the focus of a click nor on the focus a dialog gives its first control as it opens (that tooltip would take the dialog's Escape); 100 ms out, and hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13). Escape closes it without moving focus and goes no further, so the dialog or menu under it stays; in a text field the key still reaches the field. One tooltip at a time. Touch never opens one: a tap performs the action and the accessible name is what a screen reader hears.
  - **Placement:** a `popover="manual"` in the top layer, portalled to `document.body` (so no overflow clips it, no z-index competes and no `space-x-*` / `divide-*` / `last:` counts it), placed by `positionFloating.ts` on `@floating-ui/dom` 1.8.0 (pinned; MIT; already in the lock as the editor menus' dependency, now in a `vendor-floating` chunk of its own that the shell loads): flipped when there is no room, shifted 8 px inside the viewport, `start` / `end` by reading direction. A browser without the Popover API shows it with `hidden`.
  - **Look:** the `.tooltip` recipe (`index.css`), `bg-text-strong text-card text-[0.75rem] max-w-64` (12 px that scales with the text size), inverted in both modes, `animate-fade-in` (reduced motion stays global); `theme/tooltip.test.ts` pins it and its contrast in every theme (High contrast at 7:1).
- **`InfoTip`**, a port of KiroCrew's: the ⓘ glyph ("More information", described by its text) that shows like a Tooltip and pins open on a click or a tap until another, a press outside, Escape or blur; never a native `title`. It replaces the Scrapers editor's `HintTip`, and explains the AI coach banner, a built-in dimension, a flagged comment, the untyped-reviews count and the similarity filter.
- **`TruncatedText`**: text cut by `truncate` or `line-clamp-*` whose tooltip shows the whole text only while it is cut (22 places: session and member names, dialog titles, project and persona descriptions, file paths, selectors).
- **Rule 16 and its gate.** An ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` entry (frontend `eslint.config.js`) bans `title` on DOM elements (iframe excepted) and on `Link` / `NavLink`: "Use <Tooltip> (docs/kiro-design-system.md › Tooltips): a native title waits 1–2 s and never shows on focus." It skips the files of the ratchet `scripts/audit/allowlists/native_title.json` (per file, with the release each waits for), and `theme/tooltipUsage.test.ts` fails when a file's count grows, when an unlisted file gains one, or when a count falls without its entry falling too.
- i18n, in the 9 locales: `common:infoTip.label` ("More information") and `common:adminOnly` ("Admin access required", the Scrapers reason that was an English-only literal; `hooks/useAdminOnlyReason`).

### Changed

- **Wave 1 (a codemod, 88 places in 66 files):** every `title` that repeated the element's `aria-label` (icon buttons, `DialogClose`, the sidebar's collapse button, swatches, the document editor's and the flow canvas's icon buttons) is now `<Tooltip kind="label">`.
- **Waves 2 and 3 (by hand, 120 places):** truncated text became `TruncatedText`; dates, who changed it, a raw id or path behind a label, a count's meaning and a button's longer purpose became `kind="description"`; explanations became an InfoTip or visible text; a `title` that only repeated visible text, or a link's address (the browser shows it), was dropped. Agents (§4.6): the row actions are labelled tooltips, the stats hint is gone (the line says "scheduled"), the workflow switcher has a visible "Workflow" label, and Run now stays focusable while a run is under way, with "A run is already in progress." beside it.
- **A control that is off and says why stays focusable** (`aria-disabled`, styled like `disabled` by `.btn` and `.icon-btn`): Run now, View submissions with none yet, Add metric at the limit, and a non-admin's Scrapers controls (an app's Save, Delete, Add and Run, the schedule switch, Generate, Recheck, a source's Run and Delete, the admin-only source tiles), which now say "Admin access required" in their tooltip and description, translated. The scraper editor's Save and Auto-detect keep `disabled`: its read-only notice says why.
- **Design system** (`docs/kiro-design-system.md`): rule 5 is "an `aria-label` and a `<Tooltip kind="label">`"; new rule 16; a **Components › Tooltips** section (API, timing, positioning, content rule, InfoTip, TruncatedText); a Micro-interactions row; an Accessibility bullet; the labels-vs-status rows say "its Tooltip".
- `vendorChunks.json`: `@floating-ui/*` moved from `vendor-editor-menus` to `vendor-floating`.

**Left for later, in the ratchet (45 titles in 24 files):** `pages/Settings/**` (24), `components/UserAdmin/**` (11) and `pages/Account/**` (1) wait for the 7.54 settings redesign (`pages/WorkspaceSettings/**` has none); `components/WorkflowEditor/**` (6) and `components/DocumentCanvas/**` (3) were given wave 1 only, as the 7.52 canvas and the document-component extraction restructure them next (the toolbar's own `ToolbarTip` moves onto Tooltip then).

## [7.51.00] - 2026-11-17

An engineering run's page is now its **run workspace**: one live, Slack-like screen at `/agents/engineering/<run>` (and `…/a/<agent>` for one of its agents), with the flow drawn as lanes, each agent's thread, steering through the run's orchestrator, an inspector with our own diff viewer, and Resume or Restart of an ended run as a child run. Under it, the runtime steers a live run (a versioned run direction every agent reads, relayed instructions in their own fence below the platform rules), writes live transcripts every 15 s with ACP-shaped tool events, restarts one agent of a live run from its checkpoint or afresh, keeps a monthly runs list with cost, and records board-side assertions; the Agents API serves the workspace's reads from the runs' S3 objects. The workspace keeps 7.50.03's Stop: Stop and "Stop now" go through the run's own Stop route and work where the Agents API is not wired to the runtime or the bus, and there the composer and Reply are shown off with the reason.

### Added

- **Steering (runtime).** People steer a live run through its orchestrator, which relays to an agent or a role, or sets a versioned run direction every agent reads.
  - **Bus.** `msg.steer` (from the API to the conductor only, and from the conductor to an agent or a role only) and `signal.restart` (from the API), in `bus/schema.TYPES` and `bus/senders.py`; steering relayed to a role lands in that role's inbox and wakes its live agents.
  - **Coordinator tools** `relay_steering(to, text)` (an agent `<role>-<n>` or a role; never itself, a person or the run; 1 KB at most) and `set_direction(text)`, promoted from pending: the coordinator's card and SKILL.md are v5 (a steering step, a resumed-run step, a rule and an example); both bundles recompiled.
  - **Board.** The `steer` op (coordinator only) publishes `msg.steer` from the board's source as the conductor, the one non-`system` message it sends (agent sessions have no EventBridge egress). `set_direction` writes create-only `DIRECTION#v<nnnnnn>` rows `{version, text, by, at}` and moves META's `direction_version` in the same transaction (a retry with the same text answers the same version). The `direction` op lets any agent of the run read it; inbox pages carry `direction`.
  - **Harness.** A person's steering arrives in its own `<<<STEERING …>>>` fence, "a person's instruction, relayed by the orchestrator, below the platform rules"; the coordinator gets its own wording (relay it or set the direction). The harness reads the direction only when its version moves, and at each session start.
  - **Platform rules.** `_shared/PLATFORM_RULES.md` has a new "## Steering" section: steering never changes the tools, the gates, the dial, the scope or the rules.
- **Live transcripts.** The transcript writes the events it holds every 15 s (`FLUSH_SECONDS`, a clock beside the heartbeat, thread-safe; a failed write keeps the events for the next flush). Each `tool_call`/`tool_result` carries `call_id` (the model's toolUseId), `tool_kind` (ACP kind) and `status` (in_progress, completed, failed); each steering instruction that reaches the model is a `steer` event `{source, text, by}`.
- **Restart an agent of a live run** (the `restart` signal, `restart_from` `checkpoint` or `fresh`, passed through the runtime's signal action): `checkpoint` continues the agent in a new session at once from its newest checkpoint; `fresh` re-posts the task as `restarted` at the next attempt and ends the session as re-posted. Busy and stale answers work as for every signal. Refused for a stopped run, past 30 days or a spent budget, without an agent, for a fresh restart of the coordinator, and while a person's Stop of the run is under way.
- **Resume or Restart an ended run as a child run** (`runtime/restart.py`; D51-3: an ended run is never reopened).
  - voc-engineering-start's `restart_run` (`{run_id: <parent>, child_run_id?, mode, base, agents?, actor}`) writes the child in its start transaction: META `parent {run_id, mode, by, at, base}` and the parent's create-only `CHILD#<child> {mode, by, at}`; the parent's caps, connection, language, goal, issue (no new claim) and flow copy at the same revision; for a Resume, `STEP#<step>#inherited` rows the conductor treats as done. It answers `{run_id, parent_run_id, status}`, refuses a live parent, and a retry with the same child id answers the existing child. `base: head` goes through the broker's `head` op.
  - The runtime's `seed_restart` ends the parent as stopped if it has not ended; for each task the child takes over it writes `_seed/<task>/patch.diff` and `seed.json` (`voc-resume-seed/1`, `runtime/harness/seed.py`: history as excerpts, or a Learn-model summary charged to the child above 40 events or 200 KB, plus the people's steering); then it posts those tasks with their `seed_key` through the flow guard, writes the coordinator's seed and launches the child's coordinator. Any failure sends the child to a person.
  - A fresh start whose task names a `seed_key` under its own run's `_seed/` takes the seed's notes, plan and working tree: `git apply` on the parent's commit, `git apply --3way` on a moved base. A conflict reaches the agent as data (git's words and the files touched), never a crash; a key outside the run, or a bad record, starts the task afresh and the agent is told.
  - A Resume never inherits a quality gate or a fixer's or builder's step (the child's gate judges the child's own patch); gate and committer tasks are never seeded.
- **The monthly runs list.** `WS#default#RUNLIST#<yyyy-mm>` / `RUN#<started_at>#<run>` rows `{run_id, flow, goal, status, started_at, parent?}`, written in the start transaction, updated on each status change; the end (a person's Stop included) adds `ended_at`, `cost_usd` and `learn_cost_usd`.
- **Board-side assertion records**, at the coordinator's `flow` read: create-only `ASSERT#<step>#<attempt>` with `{results: [{check, status pass|fail|unread, detail, on_fail}]}` (`orchestration/assertions.py`). Records only: the conductor does not block on them yet, and checks whose inputs the board does not keep (the PR body or draft, comments, coach proposals) are recorded `unread`.
- **`max_parallel`**, an optional setting (1 to 50) on agent, board and gate steps: in the server rules, the gate PARAMS, the template schema, the compiler and the editor's gate settings; the board's `launch` refuses past it.
- **The Agents API serves the run workspace** (administrators acting for themselves; 404 while the module is off; `lambda/shared/agents_engineering_run_routes.py`, included by `agents_handler.py` before `/agents/engineering/<run_id>`):
  - `GET /agents/engineering/runs?month=&flow=&status=&cursor=&limit=`: a month's runs from the RUNLIST rows, `{runs, next}`;
  - `GET …/<run>/agents/<agent>/thread?after=&limit≤200` (`{items, next, done}`; `after` can be the overview's `transcript_cursor`, which opens the thread at its tail) and `…/thread/<ref>` (the whole event, a tool call with its result, or the conversation message). Refs are `<attempt>.<chunk>.<byte offset>[.1]` or `c<seq>`; a long attempt's tail is read with a range read that drops a partial leading line (the idea of kiro-flock's `parseTail`, `engineering/views_thread.py`);
  - `GET …/changes?source=submitted|checkpoint&attempt=&key=` (`{source, key, commit, attempt, files, truncated, patches, commit_url, pr_url}`, from the exact patches the gate judged) and `…/changes/file?key=&path=` (`{path, key, patch ≤1 MB, truncated}`);
  - `GET …/files`, `…/gate` and `…/memory` (the files an agent read and wrote, its gate checks with output, its recalled lessons and what Learn made of them), and `GET …/<run>/assertions` (a bare list);
  - `POST …/steer {text, about?, thread_id?}` (202): `msg.steer` from the person to the conductor; the conversation records it and the API logs who sent it. `about` goes in the summary as `About <agent>: <text>`, 1 KB covering both;
  - `POST …/restart {mode, agents?, base, confirm}` (202 `{run: {run_id, parent_run_id, status}}`; 409 while the run is live).
  - The overview gains `lanes`, `gates` (`{step: verdict}`), `children`, per-agent `cost_usd`, `attempt`, `commit`, `skill_label`, `model` and `transcript_cursor`, and the run's `cost_usd`, `learn_cost_usd`, `cost_cap_usd`, `parent` and `manifest` (an ended run's). The signals take `restart {from: checkpoint|fresh, task_id, attempt, confirm}`.
  - New engineering modules: `views_thread.py`, `views_inspector.py`, `run_objects.py`, `run_overview.py`; `views.py` and `monitor.py` extended. The shared fixture `frontend/src/test/engineeringRunWorkspace.json` holds the server's answers, checked by a Python test; the dev mock serves the workspace from it (`frontend/mock-engineering-run-workspace.js`, wired by `mock-engineering-runs.js`).
- **The run workspace (web app)**, under `frontend/src/pages/Agents/RunWorkspace/`. `RunWorkspace.tsx` replaces `EngineeringRun.tsx` at the same route, now `agents/engineering/:runId/*`, so no redirect is needed; the agent open is the path segment `/a/<agent>` (`runWorkspacePaths.ts`), and the address without it shows the orchestrator (the coordinator's session).
  - **Canvas:** the flow with each step's agents as lanes (`runLanes.ts`, a `LaneNode` in `CanvasNodes.tsx` on the read-only `WorkflowCanvas`, which now accepts `lanes`), a gate's pass or fail, "You are here" and a spinner on agents at work; planned lanes and steps dashed. Inert: a click opens that agent's session and never acts. A toggle switches to a timeline of steps, agents and attempts (`RunTimeline.tsx`, `runTimelineModel.ts`).
  - **Threads:** each agent's thread in time order (`SessionThread`, `ThreadItem`, `threadModel`): its words, its thinking (collapsed), each tool call on one line that opens into its result, the harness's messages folded, and steering, gates, findings and signals inline. Items are kept by ref, so a later item replaces the earlier one; Markdown renders with `skipHtml`, no images, 4 KB at most per item. An agent's own question has **Reply** (`QuestionReply.tsx`), which answers it on its own thread.
  - **Several agents** as tabs (the app's `IconTabs`, the close button beside them, an overflow menu) or a grid of 1, 2 or 4 panes with keyboard- and pointer-resizable dividers (`AgentTabs`, `AgentGrid`, `agentGridModel.ts`); the layout is kept per run in sessionStorage (a new `voc-run-workspace` store in `workspaceStorage`). On a narrow screen the sessions come first.
  - **Composer** (`SteerComposer`): steering goes to the orchestrator only (`POST …/steer {text, about?}`); "About <agent>" is ticked by default and the placeholder says where it goes.
  - **Inspector:** Changes (our own `unifiedDiff.ts` and `FileDiff.tsx`, unified or side by side, long context folded, each file read when opened, with links to the change and the pull request on GitHub), Files, Gate (the run's gate agents offered when the open agent ran none), Assertions, Cost, Memory and Learn, and the run's Board and Reports.
  - **Header** (`RunHeader`): the budget used against the cap with a meter, Learn's cost, an ended run's manifest, and links to the parent and child runs.
  - **Run controls** (`RunControlBar.tsx`): one bar with the run's toned status chip, Pause or Resume (one toggle), Stop with "Stop now, without saving" in its menu, Save a checkpoint under ⋯, and **Restart run** once the run has ended (`RestartRunDialog`: resume or restart, which agents, the same commit or the head; a 503 shows an "Open the run" link). Each agent has Stop, and under ⋯ Save, Stop now and Restart (from its checkpoint or afresh) (`AgentControls`). Stop means the same for a run and for an agent.
  - **Agents → Runs** (`RunsView`, `/agents/runs`): the month's runs with month, flow and status filters in the query; each opens its workspace. A flow's "See the flow's runs" link goes there instead of Spend, and the "engineering" breadcrumb is now "Runs".
  - **Data** (`useRunWorkspace.ts`): the existing 5 s overview poll, and the open thread read by cursor every 5 s (after 0.5 s when the last page was full). The workspace's schemas and calls are in a new `api/engineeringRunWorkspaceApi.ts`.
  - **Status chips** are toned by meaning (`agentStatus.ts`): at work accent, waiting or paused or waiting for a person warn, done ok, failed danger, stopped and unknown neutral.
  - The parts adapted from KiroCrew (Apache-2.0) are listed in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`, and each adapted file says so in its header.
  - `runWorkspace.*` strings in all nine languages.

### Changed

- **The run workspace keeps 7.50.03's Stop.**
  - The bar's **Stop** and **Stop now** are the run's Stop (`POST …/stop`, voc-engineering-start's `stop_run`), never the `shutdown`/`stop_now` signals. They are offered wherever the deployment names the start function (`stop_available`); where it does not, one line says so.
  - **Pause, Resume and Save** show only where the runtime and the bus are connected (`actions_available`); where not, one line says "Pause, Resume and Save need the engineering runtime and bus, which this deployment doesn't connect yet." Resume is offered for a run waiting for a person and once every agent at work is paused.
  - **While a Stop is under way** (the run's `stop`): the chip reads Stopping…, Stop is inert (`aria-disabled`), Pause, Resume and Save are gone, a status line gives each agent's part ("Stop sent · fixer-2 saving a checkpoint…"), and no agent is signalled, restarted or steered. What the Stop did stays said, on the ended run too ("Stopped. 1 open task was closed. Its automation's run is cancelled, so the automation can run again.").
  - The Stop's parts live once, in `frontend/src/pages/Agents/RunStop.tsx` (`StopControl`, `StopOutcome`, `StopProgress`; 7.50.03's `RunControlBar.tsx` in `pages/Agents/`, whose bar the workspace's replaced). An engineering agent's **Runs** tab uses the same Stop for its live run.
  - `assistant/components/MoreMenu.tsx` drops the trigger icon and class 7.50.03 added for its split button: the split button's menu is the workspace's `ActionsMenu`.
- **An agent's Restart is refused while a person's Stop of the run is under way**, as a Resume is (`runtime/handler.py` `_refuse_while_stopping`).
- **Steering and replies where the Agents API is not wired to the bus.** Steering (`POST …/steer`) and an answer to an agent (`POST …/messages`) are published on the engineering bus, so they need `ENGINEERING_BUS_NAME` on the Agents API and answer 503 without it (as on `b-`, whose API names neither the runtime nor the bus). The workspace now shows the composer off, with the reason ("Steering and replies can't be sent from this deployment yet: it doesn't connect the Agents API to the engineering runtime and bus."), and offers no Reply. The API's grants are not widened.
- **Answers to an agent go only on the thread its own question opened** (D51-4): `POST …/messages` with `to: agent` needs a `thread_id` (400 without one), and that thread must have been opened by the agent's own `msg.question` (404 otherwise). Anything else for an agent is steering, through the orchestrator.
- **The run monitor's panels are folded into the workspace.** `EngineeringRun.tsx`, `EngineeringSignals.tsx`, `EngineeringConversation.tsx` and the interim `RunControls.tsx`/`RunPanels.tsx` are gone; the Board and Reports are inspector tabs, an agent's facts are its Cost tab, and its question's Reply sits under the question.
- **Doubles folded into one.**
  - The overview hook: `useEngineeringOverview` keeps 7.50.03's failed-read handling (the last good read and its controls kept, `refreshFailed`, polling backed off up to a minute, only a 404 stops it), which the workspace reads; `useRunReadable` is exported for the workspace's reads, and `monthOf` from `spendView.ts`.
  - The status tones: `RunWorkspace/agentStatus.ts` (7.50.03's `agentTone`, `runState` and its toned run chip are gone; `engineeringRunText.ts` keeps `isStopping`).
  - The menus: the workspace's `ActionsMenu` (see above).
  - The ASSERT rows' reader: the assertions view's (`engineering/views.py`); `flow/assertion_record.py` `assertion_rows`, which only its test reached, is gone, with the two audit allowlist entries that waited for B's views.
  - The start role's run-partition reads: one `RUN_PARTITIONS` constant for 7.50.03's `StopRunReads` and 7.51.00's `RestartReadsTheParent`.
- **One set of run-control strings**, the clearer copy kept, in all nine languages: the bar's `runWorkspace.controls.*` (`more` now "More run controls", `limited` names the runtime and the bus) and the Stop's own `engineeringRun.stop.*` (`unavailable`, `agentSaving`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `fellBack`, `agentRunEnded`, `already`); `runWorkspace.composer.unavailable` is new; an agent's Stop now asks with `engineeringRun.stopNowAgentMessage`. Gone, as doubles or unreached: `engineeringRun.actionsUnavailable`, `moreRun`, `moreFor`, `saveCheckpoint`, `refreshFailed`, `retry`, `runState.*`, and `stop.group`, `stop.more`, `stop.nowItem`, `stop.stoppingButton`, `stop.sent`; the run's state reads `runWorkspace.runs.statuses.*`.
- **IAM** (each pinned in the CDK tests):
  - `voc-engineering-start`: `RestartReadsTheParent` (Query of `WS#*#RUN#*`, beside 7.50.03's `StopRunReads` on the same partitions); the RUNLIST partitions added to its Get/Put/Update. The `seed_restart` invoke uses its existing grant.
  - `voc-engineering-runtime`: `RunsListRows` (Get/Update), `RestartReadsPatches` (`ws/default/runs/*/*/commits/*/_patches/*`) and `WriteRestartSeeds` (`ws/default/runs/*/_seed/*`, create-only). Checkpoint reads, transcript reads and Learn's Bedrock grant already existed.
  - The board function: `ReadRecordedOutputs` (findings `.jsonl`, `_patches`, `_triage`) and an explicit Deny on `_transcripts` and `_checkpoints`; the DIRECTION and ASSERT rows use its existing table grant (pinned).
  - `voc-agents-api` (`lib/stacks/api-engineering-run-reads.ts`): `s3:GetObject` on `ws/default/runs/*/*/commits/*/{_transcripts,_patches,_gate}/*` and `ws/default/runs/*/_manifest/*`, and `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket only, with `s3:prefix` held to the transcript and patch patterns. No Put or Delete, nothing on checkpoints or seeds, nothing while the module is off.

- **Inventories:** the run workspace's routes are in `test_route_admin_gates.py` and the cross-workspace pending list; the RUNLIST, DIRECTION, ASSERT, CHILD and `_seed/` rows and prefixes are in docs/multi-workspace.md's engineering row and the 3g3 inventory; `mock-coverage.json` lists the workspace's calls beside 7.50.03's `…/stop`.

### Upgrade notes

- **Rebuild the four engineering images and deploy their digests with the stacks**, as for 7.50.03 (docs/deployment.md, `engineeringImages`): the harness inside them changed (the 15 s flush, the ACP-shaped events, the steering fence and the direction, the seeds), and the workspace's live threads, steering and Resume or Restart need it.
- Deploy VocProcessingStack (the runtime's, the start function's and the board's code and grants), VocApiStack (the workspace's routes and the Agents API's S3 reads) and the frontend.
- **Runs started before 7.51.00 have no runs-list row**: Agents → Runs does not list them. Their workspace opens from their address, an agent's run row or the flow's page as before.
- **API callers that answer an agent** (`POST …/messages` with `to: agent`) must now send the `thread_id` of the agent's own question; anything else for an agent is steering (`POST …/steer`).
- **Where the Agents API names neither the runtime nor the bus** (as on `b-`): Stop and Stop now work; Pause, Resume, Save, an agent's controls, steering and Reply are off, and the workspace says why; Restart run on an ended run works (it goes through the start function too). Wiring them is a deployment decision (the bus and the runtime named on the Agents API, with their grants); this release widens no grant for them.
- **Rollback.** An earlier release ignores the RUNLIST, DIRECTION, ASSERT, CHILD and `STEP#…#inherited` rows and the `_seed/` objects; a child run started on 7.51.00 then runs without its inherited steps and seeds.

## [7.50.03] - 2026-11-17

The first real engineering run on the `b-` deployment found two problems, and both are fixed. The run monitor could stop nothing: the run sat waiting for a person, and its engineering agent's run stayed locked. A person's **Stop** now ends any run that has not ended, through the start function, with or without a live session, and the monitor always shows it. The coordinator's session never started, because AgentCore Runtime refuses the images' in-container iptables firewall (no CAP_NET_ADMIN, a read-only `/proc/sys`). The images now choose **whichever wall the container supports**: the firewall where iptables works, else a user and network namespace of its own for every command of the agent's and of repository code's, bridged by a forwarder to its own proxy over a Unix socket. They still fail closed when neither holds.

### Fixed

- **The run monitor could stop nothing.** The live run (`01M7KVTD…`) was waiting for a person (`needs_human` = `coordinator`): its coordinator's session never started, its `coordinate` task was open with `launched_agent` `coordinator-1`, and that agent's launch hold had run out. Its monitor offered no Stop, and the Bug fixer's agent run stayed locked behind it. There were two causes, found in the code and the deployed function's configuration (read-only):
  - **The signals never reached the run.** By design the Agents API's role may invoke `voc-engineering-start`, never `voc-engineering-runtime`, so the API is not wired to the runtime or the bus (no `ENGINEERING_RUNTIME_FUNCTION`, no `ENGINEERING_BUS_NAME`). The overview therefore said `actions_available: false`, and the page showed one sentence where the signals would be. No signal was ever sent (the API logged none).
  - **A whole-run stop ended nothing.** Where signals do reach the runtime, a whole run's **Shut down** or **Stop now** only moved its agents' sessions (`Supervisor.signal_detailed`). A run with no session answered "no agent yet" and stayed as it was, since only `end_run` ends a run and nothing calls it.
- **A person's Stop now always ends a run that has not ended**, with or without a session or a reachable supervisor:
  - **The route.** `POST /agents/engineering/<run_id>/stop` `{now?, confirm?, note?}` is for administrators acting for themselves. It goes through `voc-engineering-start`'s new `stop_run`, so the API needs neither the runtime nor the bus (the overview's new `stop_available`).
  - **Stop.** The agents that have a session save a checkpoint and stop (the Shut down signal, handed on to the runtime's new `stop_run`), and the answer is `stopping`. The run ends once none has a session left, or at the latest 10 minutes after the request (each tick, `_finish_stops`). With no agent that has a session, it ends at once.
  - **Stop now.** `now: true` with `confirm: true` ends the run at once.
  - **While a Stop is under way**, the run launches no agent (`SessionStore.create` refuses it) and takes no Resume.
  - **What ending the run does** (`lambda/engineering/runtime/stop.py`):
    - writes META `stopped` with its `RUNLOG#` row naming the person and how (D4);
    - closes every task that has not ended, as `failed` with a `stop` history row naming the person (`BoardStore.close_for_stop`). The retrospective reads it as handed back, never as an agent's failure for the coach;
    - runs out every live launch hold, ends the run's sessions and releases it.
  - **The issue's `ISSUE_RUN#` claim is kept**, as the design says: one run per issue, ever, and Run now `{issue}` reruns it.
  - **The agent's run ends too.** Once the run has ended, the API ends its engineering agent's run at once: cancelled, its lock released (`shared/engineering_agent_runs.py` `end_agent_run`, which the heartbeat's lock heal now uses too). The agent can run again without waiting up to 15 minutes for the heartbeat.
  - **A whole run's `shutdown` or `stop_now` sent as a signal is this Stop**, both through `/signals` where the start function is named and in the runtime's own `signal` action.
- **The run monitor's controls** (the UX spec's "run monitor" part). For an administrator on any run that has not ended, one **Run controls** bar always has **Stop**:
  - **Stop is a split button.** Stop saves first; its menu holds **Stop now, without saving…**, which asks first.
  - **Where the signals reach the run**, the bar also has one **Pause/Resume** toggle by the run's state, and **Save a checkpoint** under ⋯. Where they do not, one line beside Stop says so.
  - **While a Stop is under way**, the run's chip and the disabled Stop say **Stopping…** (`aria-disabled`), and a status line gives each agent's part ("fixer-2 saving a checkpoint…").
  - **The answer says what happened**, for example "Stopped. 1 open task was closed. Its automation's run is cancelled, so the automation can run again." The run is read again, and the line stays once the run has ended.
  - **Toned chips.** The run's status is a toned chip: running accent, waiting for a person warn, stopping warn, done ok, failed danger, stopped muted. Each agent's status is toned too.
  - **Agent cards.** Each card's five buttons are now its **Stop** and a ⋯ menu: Save a checkpoint, Pause or Resume, Stop now.
  - **Runs tab.** An engineering agent's **Runs** tab shows the same Stop for its live run; "stop it on its run monitor" is gone.
  - **Files:** `frontend/src/pages/Agents/RunControlBar.tsx` (new), `EngineeringSignals.tsx`, `EngineeringRun.tsx`, `EngineeringRunHeader.tsx`, `EngineeringRunPanels.tsx`, `RunsTab.tsx` and `engineeringRunText.ts`. `assistant/components/MoreMenu.tsx` takes a trigger icon and class, for the split button's menu half. There are new strings in all nine languages.
- **An idle session lived to its 8 hours.** The runner's `/ping` set `time_of_last_update` to the current time on every ping. The HTTP protocol contract says not to: "Do not set `time_of_last_update` to the current time on every ping. A timestamp that advances on every ping signals a continuous status change, which prevents the idle session timeout from ever firing — sessions then persist until `MaxLifetime` and can exhaust your session quota."
  - The field is now when the runner last did real work: the status's last change (a command starting or the last one ending, a hold), an invocation that starts, hands over, holds or wakes the agent (`WORK_OPS`), or a command's start.
  - A ping, a `status` read or a poll of a command's result never moves it.
  - `HealthyBusy` stays as it was: only while a command runs and is not held.
  - An idle or held session now ends at the runtime's idle timeout (an hour), never at its maximum lifetime (`unit_runner.Runner.ping`). The images carry the runner, so this ships with their rebuild.
- **One failed read hid the controls.** `live` was false after a single failed overview read, so the controls disappeared and polling stopped while the run went on. `live` now comes from the last good read. After a failed read the page keeps that read and its controls, says "Couldn't refresh: this is the last read." with **Retry**, and keeps polling with a backoff (doubling, at most a minute). Only a 404 stops it (`useEngineeringRun.ts`).
- **AgentCore Runtime refused the agents' egress firewall, so no session could start.** The coordinator's container refused `start`, and InvokeAgentRuntime got a 400 from the runtime.
  - **What failed.** The 7.50.0 entry point could not install its iptables rules ("Permission denied (you must be root)"), nor write `/proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks` ("Read-only file system"). The runner, started without `--egress-firewall`, fails closed by design.
  - **What a probe showed** (one throwaway session, which the owner approved; dated in docs/autonomous-engineering.md "Runtime"):
    - the container runs as root, with Docker's default capabilities plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN and no CAP_NET_ADMIN, so iptables is refused (nft is absent);
    - `NoNewPrivs` is 1 and there is no seccomp filter;
    - unprivileged user and network namespaces work, for `unit` and `code` too;
    - `/proc/sys` is read-only, but `protected_hardlinks` already reads 1, and the tmpfs `/run/voc` sits on its own device;
    - `/dev/fuse` is present;
    - the session's way out is link-local.
  - **The entry point** (`engineering-images/common/walls.sh`, new) now chooses the wall:
    - it tries iptables first, as before (`--egress-firewall --code-firewall`);
    - otherwise it checks, for `unit` and for `code`, the chain the runner will use: drop to the user, take a user and network namespace of its own, bring its loopback up, see no other interface, drop every capability. It then passes `--egress-namespaces` and `--code-namespaces`;
    - it passes `--hardlink-guard` with each guard that holds (`own_device`, `protected_hardlinks`). It reads these, and no longer writes `/proc/sys`.
  - **The runner starts an agent only behind an egress wall**, takes the dependency step only behind a code wall, and runs repository code only with a hard-link guard. With none, it still refuses (`unit_runner.py`).
  - **In namespace mode, every command runs in its own namespaces.** Every command of the agent's (as `unit`) and of repository code's (as `code`) runs in its own user and network namespace, with only a loopback and no capability.
    - A forwarder inside (`unit_runner.py forward`) bridges `127.0.0.1:8081`/`3128` (the agent) and `3129` (the dependency step only) to Unix sockets that the root runner serves in `/run/voc-net`. The sockets are made at `start`, never in a V2 snapshot.
    - Each socket is mode 0600, owned by its user, and uid-checked with `SO_PEERCRED` on every connection. The code proxy's socket is removed for good once other repository code runs.
    - Link-local, credential and metadata endpoints and DNS are unreachable by construction: the namespace has no eth0.
  - **The runner reports its walls.** Its `start` and `status` answers say which walls hold (`sandbox: {egress, code, hardlink_guard}`). The runtime keeps each language's last record (`WS#default#SANDBOX` / `LANG#<language>`, `runtime/sandbox.py`, wired through `AgentCoreRuntime`'s new `on_walls`).
  - **Readiness has a new `sandbox` check**, which is advice, not required. It answers "unknown until the first session" with nothing recorded, never a pass; pass once a session's walls all held; fail when one did not. Its fix names the four images to rebuild.
  - **The VPC fallback is not built.** The namespaces hold, and a security-group and DNS-firewall wall would be weaker: it cannot tell the agent from repository code, nor keep either off the link-local resolver.
- **Tests:**
  - `lambda/engineering/runtime/test/test_engineering_run_stop.py` (new) covers:
    - the stuck run's own shape: started, its launch handed on and run out, sent to a person. Stop and Stop now end it: RUNLOG, the closed task and its history row, the hand-on of `finish_stop` (the runtime's `end_run` as stopped) that releases it;
    - an active run with no session and a live launch hold, whose late launch is then refused;
    - runs that ended done, failed or stopped: changed by nothing;
    - a retried Stop;
    - a working agent: saves, then the run ends at the next tick. A Resume and a new agent are refused meanwhile;
    - an agent that never saves: stopped at the grace;
    - Stop now with an agent at work, through the runtime's own signal;
    - a whole run's Shut down with no session;
    - a hand-on that fails, which stops the run at once;
    - bad requests.
  - `lambda/engineering/test/test_monitor.py`: Stop and Stop now parsed; the Stop reaching the run without the runtime or the bus; whole-run signals as the Stop; the conversation's record where the bus is named; an ended run; the overview's `stop` and `waiting_at`; `LambdaStopper`; the run's origin.
  - `lambda/api/test/test_agents_engineering_stop.py` (new): the route, the engineering agent's run cancelled and its lock released, a Stop still saving, the gates, 409, 503.
  - The lock release: `lambda/shared/test/test_engineering_agent_runs.py` (`end_agent_run` ends the agent's run once, frees the lock and keeps the issue's claim), and through the heartbeat `test_heartbeat_engineering.py` (stopped → cancelled).
  - `test_engineering_runtime_handler.py`: the deployed runtime keeps each started session's walls as its language's last.
  - `test_retrospective.py`: a stop-closed task is no failure.
  - Sandbox tests:
    - `test_engineering_walls.py` (new): the entry point's decision tree, as a harness of `walls.sh`;
    - `test_engineering_local_runtime.py` and `test_engineering_images.py`: the runner refusing `start` with no wall and accepting each kind; the guards; pings alone never move the idle clock, a command is busy while it runs and the idle clock runs from its end, an invocation that does work moves it and a held agent is idle;
    - `test_engineering_namespaces.py` (new, Linux only): the namespace wrapper and forwarder, run where `unshare -Urn` works, else skipped with the reason;
    - `test_engineering_sandbox_record.py` (new): the record;
    - `test_engineering_agentcore_runtime.py`;
    - `test_readiness.py` and `test_readiness_aws.py`: the `sandbox` check.
  - CDK: `engineering-runtime.test.ts`.
  - Frontend: `EngineeringRun.test.tsx`, `RunsTab.engineering.test.tsx`, `engineeringRunsApi.test.ts`.

### Changed

- IAM:
  - `voc-engineering-start`'s role gains `dynamodb:Query` of the runs' own partitions only (`StopRunReads`, LeadingKeys `WS#*#RUN#*`, never the registry): a Stop reads the run's tasks and agents.
  - The supervisor's and the delivery function's roles gain `dynamodb:PutItem` of `WS#*#SANDBOX` only (`SandboxRecord`, `engineering-runtime-grants.ts` `grantLauncherRows`).

- Docs:

    - the run monitor and its Stop;
    - Trust and safety (the Stop built);
    - Runtime: the "unchecked" list replaced by what the probe showed, dated, what the AgentCore guide does and does not say, the walls design with its socket table and its guarantees against the firewall's, whole-run stops and `end_run`;
    - Readiness: the `sandbox` row.
  - `docs/autonomous-agents.md`: the engineering agents' runs, the run monitor's actions, the `…/stop` route.
  - `docs/deployment.md`: `engineeringImages`, which must all be rebuilt for 7.50.03.
- `lib/test-support/baseline.json` regenerated (the IAM statements above and the version).

### Upgrade notes

- **Rebuild all four engineering images and deploy their digests with the stacks, in the same deploy.**
  - Build and push python, node, java and rust for linux/arm64 from `voc-datalake/`, with new tags. The commands are in docs/deployment.md, `engineeringImages`; use the same Mountpoint and boto3 build arguments as 7.50.00.
  - Read each digest, then deploy the stacks with `-c engineeringImages='{"python":"sha256:…","node":"sha256:…","java":"sha256:…","rust":"sha256:…"}'` and every other `-c` setting of the deployment. Then deploy the frontend.

With no session it ends at once, its open task is closed and its engineering agent's run is cancelled, so the agent can run again. Rerun its issue with the agent's Run now `{issue}`.
- **MMDSv2, checked.** The guide says AgentCore Runtime requires MMDSv2 from 2026-06-30 and rejects invocations of a runtime without `metadataConfiguration.requireMMDSV2`. The stacks cannot set it: neither aws-cdk-lib 2.275.0's `CfnRuntime` nor CloudFormation's `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime` schema (us-west-2, 2026-11-17) has the property. The `b-` python runtime made by these stacks already reads `requireMMDSV2: true` (`get-agent-runtime`, read-only), so nothing is to do now; docs/autonomous-engineering.md (Runtime, "MMDSv2") says to set and pin it once the property exists.
