## [7.50.02] - 2026-11-17

The deployment's GitHub Issues source configures itself from Agents → Connections: connecting a repository through the deployment's GitHub App (the two-click **Connect GitHub**) is what makes its issues read, with no Data sources step, no token to paste and no repository webhook. The installation, and every **Check installation**, adds each connected repository to the source (merged, never overwritten: an administrator's own repositories stay, a source set to a token stays on the token), signs it in with the App, turns its schedule on, and creates the `voc-agent` label on each repository when it is missing; each connection has a **Read this repository's issues** switch (on by default), and removing a connection takes out only what its automation added. The Data sources card becomes the advanced view ("Managed by your GitHub connection"), App-first, and `/admin/data-sources/github_issues` opens it. The setup guide's first step is just Connect GitHub and Confirm CI, with the Issues source and the label as automatic ticks, and readiness passes them from that state. A live check also found every user shown as AI-driven on the Users page while the engineering dial, which takes only an explicitly saved choice, refused them: a person with nothing saved now shows **Not set**, readiness tells "Not set yet" from a saved Human-driven, and the Set up dialog offers **Set mine to AI-driven**. The pull request copy now says agents open pull requests for review and merging stays with a person.

### Added

- **The Issues source follows the connections** (`lambda/engineering/connectors/issues_sync.py`; [docs/github-issues.md](docs/github-issues.md#configured-by-your-github-connection-75002)). A pure rule (`plan`) over the source's stored settings: a connection's repository is added to `github_issues_repos` (up to 20; past it, skipped as `limit`) and recorded in a new key, `github_issues_repos_managed` (the repositories the automation added, one `owner/name` per line); one already listed (an administrator's entry, a GitHub URL included) is left as it is and never claimed; a source with no sign-in gets the connection's App as `github_app_id`; a source signed in with a token is untouched (`token`), one signed in with another App keeps it (`other_app`); a removal takes a repository out only when `repos_managed` names it. `IssuesFollow` (the Agents API's side) asks `voc-engineering-issues-config` (below), which applies it and turns the source's schedule rule on when it added a repository and the rule was off, after an installation saves its connections and on Check installation (the answers' new `issues` block: `signs_in`, `added`, `reading`, `skipped`, `labels`, `schedule`, `error`), on a connection's switch and on a connection's removal, and never fails the step that called it (the connections are saved; the block says what went wrong). Each connection's switch and label state is a row of the connections' partition (`CONNECTIONS#default` / `ISSUES#<connection_id>`), and every change an audit row of the connections' `LOG#` shape (`issues_source_added`, `issues_source_removed`, `issues_schedule_enabled`, `issues_read_on`, `issues_read_off`, `issues_label_created`), never a secret.
- `GET /agents/engineering/issues-source` (`{deployed, signs_in, app_id, repositories, managed, schedule, label, connections: [{connection_id, repository, read, reading, reason, label}]}`; `reason` one of `off`, `token`, `other_app`, `limit`, `not_app`, `not_deployed`, `pending`) and `PUT /agents/engineering/connections/<connection_id>/issues` (`{read: boolean}`, answering the same view; 409 for a connection not made through the deployment's App turned on, or where the source is not deployed). Both the connections' gate: 404 while the engineering agents are off, then administrators acting for themselves; deployment-wide.
- `ensure_label`, a third action of the GitHub Apps' token function (`app_tokens.py`): `{app_id, installation_id, repository, label}`, where `label` must be exactly `voc-agent` (any other name is refused before anything is read), the installation the one GitHub says covers the repository (another App's, another installation or a suspended one is `InstallationRefused`), and the token exactly `{issues: write}` with `repositories` narrowed to that one repository; it reads the label, creates it only on a 404 (color `5319e7`, "Picked up by the VoC agents"; a 422 from a concurrent create is "present"), revokes the token and answers `{repository, label, created}`, never the token. The Agents API asks it for each connection whose label is not recorded yet, up to eight at once.
- **Agents → Connections**: on each connection made through the deployment's App, the **Read this repository's issues** switch and a status line (read automatically; or why not, with the token note linking to the GitHub Issues card; **Read its issues now** for a connection not synced yet) and the label's state; Check installation and the installation's return page say what the source now reads and which labels were created. The layout is unchanged (its redesign is 7.52's).
- `PUT /users/me/ai-mode` (`{ai_mode}`): an administrator saves their own way of working, for the caller's subject from the token, never another person's (a delegated credential is refused); the engineering Set up dialog's **Set mine to AI-driven** uses it, after an inline confirmation that it also lets AI write their PR/FAQs and PRDs, then reads the readiness again.
- `/admin/data-sources/<source>`: the deployment's Data sources opened at one card, expanded and scrolled into view (an unknown source is replaced by `/admin/data-sources`); readiness's `issues_source` fix and the setup guide link to `/admin/data-sources/github_issues`.

### Changed

- **The deployment's GitHub Issues card is the advanced view.** When the stored `github_app_id` is an App and `repos_managed` lists a repository it says "Managed by your GitHub connection: issues from N repositories", with a link to Agents → Connections, and the fields sit under **Configure manually (advanced)**. The manual path signs in App-first: with an App, the App is chosen (the only one preselected, a select for several) under "Signs in with your GitHub App: no token to paste. Issues and comments are read with short-lived, read-only tokens.", and the token field is behind **Use a fine-grained token instead**; a stored choice wins (a source saved with a token, `github_app_id: none` or repositories without an App, stays on the token); with no App, **Connect GitHub** links to Agents → Connections. The "Sign in with" select is gone. Saving writes the same `repos` and `github_app_id`.
- **Setup guide, step 0**: just **Connect GitHub** and **Confirm CI**; the Issues source and the label are automatic ticks read from the issues-source view ("Issues: read automatically from N repositories", "Label voc-agent: created"; a source on a token links to its card). The 7.50.01 integration-status read is gone.
- **Readiness**: `issues_source` passes as soon as the source's settings name the repository with a sign-in ("Issues: read automatically from <repo> …"), before its first poll, else on its watermark as before; its fix names the connection's switch and `/admin/data-sources/github_issues`. `issue_label` passes for `voc-agent` once its connection recorded it created or present ("Label voc-agent: created"); a label that could not be created says Check installation tries again; another label stays `unknown`. `dial` tells nothing saved ("Not set yet: choose AI-assisted or AI-driven for <name>. With nothing saved, a run pushes nothing (documents default to AI-driven).") from a saved Human-driven; a flow that pushes nothing still passes with nothing saved; its fix names `/admin/access/users`.
- **Ways of working** (Administration → Users): the `ai_mode` block of `GET /users`, `PUT /users/{username}/flags` and `GET /users/me/ai-mode` carries `saved` (`shared/ai_mode.py`; `connectors/dial.py` `stored` reads the same row). A person with nothing saved shows **Not set** ("Documents use AI-driven · automations won't push until you choose") with no option selected, so one click on AI-driven saves it; the description says the setting also decides whether the automations a person enables may push and open pull requests, a **How the modes differ** disclosure compares the three modes (your PR/FAQs and PRDs, the automations you enable) instead of hover tooltips only, and the control is a radio group with arrow keys (moving saves nothing; Space, Enter or a click saves). The server rule is unchanged: documents default to AI-driven, the engineering dial needs an explicit AI-assisted or AI-driven.
- Copy, in all nine languages: a connection's CI attestation now says "the agents may push to voc-agent/* branches and open pull requests for review; merging stays with a person", and so do the Bug fixer's and Feature builder's Run now confirmations and Build from this PRD (since 7.50 a pull request opens ready for review unless its flow says `pr: draft`).
- **`voc-engineering-issues-config`**, a new function (VocProcessingStack, `lib/stacks/engineering-issues-config.ts`, `lambda/engineering/connectors/issues_config.py`; only where the engineering agents and github_issues are both deployed), the one writer of the source's settings for the connections, so the Agents API gets no grant on the shared secret. It takes `follow {connection_id, repository, app_id}`, `unfollow {connection_id, repositories}` and `status {}` and refuses any other action or key before anything is read (the Agents API's 400); writes only `github_issues_repos`, `github_issues_repos_managed` and `github_issues_github_app_id` (every other key written back as read); never loses a concurrent save of the Integrations API (the version read checked again before the write, each write with its own `ClientRequestToken`, and a save that landed in between kept, the change applied again on top of it); and answers only `{repos, repos_managed, github_app_id, sign_in, token_set, schedule_enabled}`. Its own role: exactly `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` and `PutSecretValue` on the shared API-credentials secret's ARN (Secrets Manager's own key: no KMS grant) and `events:DescribeRule` and `EnableRule` on the github_issues schedule rule (never DisableRule); no function URL, no resource policy, no table, no bucket. The Agents API's role gains only `lambda:InvokeFunction` on it by name (`ENGINEERING_ISSUES_CONFIG_FUNCTION`; pinned: no `secretsmanager:*`, no `events:EnableRule`), and maps its errors as it maps the token function's. VocProcessingStack takes VocIngestionStack's `secretsArn` for it. The label needs nothing new: the role already invokes the token function, whose role is unchanged.
- Docs: docs/github-issues.md ("Configured by your GitHub connection (7.50.02)", the App-first card), docs/autonomous-engineering.md (the token function's `ensure_label`, the Agents API's IAM, the `issues_source`, `issue_label` and `dial` rows), docs/ways-of-working.md ("Not set").
- Tests: `lambda/engineering/connectors/test/test_issues_sync.py` (add, merge, remove only what was managed, a token-configured source untouched, another App's kept, the 20 limit, the entry parse pinned to the ingestor's, the schedule turned on with its audit row and left off by a later check, labels ensured once and retried after a refusal, the switch, a removal, a pending connection, a source that cannot be read, not deployed), `lambda/api/test/test_agents_engineering_issues_source.py` (the routes, the installation's `issues` block, the gate, 404 off), `lambda/engineering/connectors/test/test_issues_config.py` (the three actions alone, refused before any read; only the three keys written; a token source untouched; a save between the read and the write read again, one landing between the check and the write kept; settings that keep changing unavailable; answers of exactly six fields, and no answer or log line carrying a value of the secret), `test_app_tokens.py` (`ensure_label`: exactly `voc-agent`, `{issues: write}` for one repository, created only when missing, refused for another installation, revoked on failure), the github_issues webhook (an App delivery for a repository its connection configured is ingested), `test_readiness.py` and `test_dial.py` (the managed state, the label, "Not set yet"), `test_users_ai_mode_routes.py` (`saved`, `PUT /users/me/ai-mode`), `lib/stacks/engineering-issues-config.test.ts` (the function's exact grants, only with both flags) and `lib/stacks/api-engineering-issues-sync.test.ts` (the Agents API's invoke by name, no `secretsmanager:*`, no `events:EnableRule`), and the frontend's switch, card, path, guide, Users page and dialog tests (no `X-Workspace-Id` in the deployment scope); the route inventories list the new routes.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy the stacks, then the frontend (`npm run deploy:infra`, then `npm run deploy:frontend`; or `npm run deploy:all`). VocProcessingStack adds `voc-engineering-issues-config` where the engineering agents and github_issues are both deployed (its role, its log group) and changes the token function's code (`ensure_label`); VocApiStack changes the Agents API's code and there its role (`lambda:InvokeFunction` on that function by name) and environment, and the Users API's code (`PUT /users/me/ai-mode`, `saved`). Deploy VocProcessingStack before VocApiStack (`deploy:infra` keeps that order). No table, index or image change.
- A connection made before 7.50.02 is not added by itself: open Agents → Connections and use **Check installation** on its App once (or **Read its issues now** on the connection). That adds its repository to the source, signs the source in with the App if it had no sign-in, turns its schedule on and creates the `voc-agent` label. A source already set to a token stays on the token: switch it to the App on its card (Configure manually) if you want the connections to manage it.
- The App must hold Issues read and write on the repository (every App made since 7.45.00 does); a label that cannot be created shows on the connection, and Check installation tries again.
- People with nothing saved now show **Not set** on the Users page; the engineering dial refused them before too. Choose AI-assisted or AI-driven for each administrator who enables an engineering agent, or use **Set mine to AI-driven** in its Set up dialog.

## [7.50.01] - 2026-11-17

Fixes from a live check of 7.50.00's engineering Set up dialog and readiness, two of which blocked a first real run: the Set up dialog was taller than the window and could not scroll (Save and Cancel out of reach), and on a first set-up **Save and enable** could never be clicked, because the dialog showed the readiness of the stored agent (no connection yet: "No stored connection to attest") instead of what it had selected. The readiness now answers for a selection (`&connection=&language=`, read-only), the dialog reads it again as the selection changes, the checks are compact, the way-of-working check says who and how in plain words, the Issues source's fix names the page the app has, the setup guide keeps the deployment's facts apart from each automation's readiness and says when the deployment's GitHub Issues source is not configured, "Start from a template" counts its five flows, and the Agents list orders the loop's automations as the loop runs.

### Fixed

- The engineering agent's **Set up** dialog is held to the window (`max-h-[90vh]`): its body scrolls between the title and **Cancel** / **Save and enable**, which stay in view (in a 1440×1000 window it was 2,415 px tall, top at −707 px, and the wheel did not move it). Its readiness is compact: the summary line (Failing · Unknown · Warnings · Passed), the checks that do not pass with the ones a run needs first, and those that passed folded under one line ("Checks that passed (n)"), as wherever the readiness shows open (the setup guide's automation steps too). The same height limit for the Agents pages' other dialogs: **Start a run**, a flow's **History** and every confirmation (`ConfirmModal`, whose content now scrolls: a skill's benchmark form was as tall). `frontend/src/pages/Agents/AgentEngineering.tsx`, `ReadinessChecks.tsx`, `StartRunDialog.tsx`, `components/WorkflowEditor/WorkflowHistory.tsx`, `components/ConfirmModal/ConfirmModal.tsx`.
- On a first set-up **Save and enable** never became clickable: the dialog showed the stored agent's readiness, which has no connection yet, so `ci_attestation` failed ("No stored connection to attest") although the selected connection was attested; it only overlooked the checks it sets itself (the connection, the image, the budget). `GET /agents/engineering/readiness?automation=<agent id>` now takes `&connection=<id>&language=<language>` and answers for the agent as if it were set up with them, read-only (`engineering/readiness.py` `preview`: nothing is saved, Enable still evaluates what is stored). The connection must be stored and not removed and the language one with an agent image (400 otherwise, 503 when the connection cannot be read), for `?flow=` too. The dialog reads it for its selection and again whenever the connection or the language changes, so the App installation, the CI attestation, the branch rules, the Issues source and the image are the selection's; Save and enable waits while a required check fails for it, the enabling administrator's way of working included, and only the budget, which the dialog saves and checks itself, does not hold it. Still administrators acting for themselves only, REST only; no route is added. [docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#readiness-before-enable)
- The `dial` check's words: it nested a broken parenthetical and showed raw ids ("ai-assisted, ai-driven"). It now says, for example, "The runs follow alice, whose way of working is Human-driven, so a run would push nothing. This flow needs AI-assisted or AI-driven.", and its fix names the person and the ways of working the flow runs in, under Administration → Privacy & access → Users (`readiness.MODE_NAMES`, `mode_names`; the subject carries the enabling administrator's username, else the asker's).
- The `issues_source` check's fix named "Settings → Data sources (deployment)"; the app calls it **Administration → Data sources** (`/admin/data-sources`), and so does the fix now (and docs/autonomous-engineering.md's table).
- "Start from a template" said "Six default engineering flows" and listed five (7.50.00 took Self-improvement out of the list), in all nine languages; so did the library's and the dialog's docstrings and docs/autonomous-engineering.md ("Default flows", whose table drops the Self-improvement row).
- The setup guide's prerequisites contradicted themselves: "CI attested: Done" (the deployment's connection) above an automation's readiness failing the CI attestation (the automation had no connection yet). The step now shows **This deployment**'s facts apart (GitHub connected through an App, naming the connections; the CI attested, naming the connections it is attested for; the issues ingested) and then each automation's prerequisite checks under its own heading, "Readiness for <automation>, once set up" (as on its own step). While an automation names no connection and the deployment has one it could use, the guide asks its readiness of that connection (the preview). The Issues line said "Not known yet" while the deployment's GitHub Issues source was not configured: it reads the deployment's integration status (`GET /integrations/status`, no workspace header) and says **Not configured**, with the link to Administration → Data sources, and the step is not done while it is so. New strings in all nine languages (`readiness.passedFolded`, `passedLabel`; `setupGuide.readinessFor`; `setupGuide.prerequisites.deploymentTitle`, `connectedAs`, `ciFor`, `notConfigured`; `checksTitle` is gone).
- The Agents list put Issue triage last (by name). `GET /agents` lists the agents that are not engineering agents by name, then the engineering ones: the seeded automations first, in the loop's order (Issue triage, Bug fixer, Feature builder, as the setup guide and the docs have them; each found by its seeded name), then any other by name (`shared/agent_seed.py` `list_order`). The dev mock lists them the same way, and answers the readiness preview as the server does.
