## [7.50.00] - 2026-11-17

The autonomous bug loop runs from templates kept in the repository: `voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/` holds each engineering role's card and skill, the flows, the seeded automations, the gate packs and the eval cases, compiled into one bundle that the Lambdas, the images and the web app read, with a validator, a compiler and a local runner (`npm run orchestration:*`). An agent runs the skill its launch resolved (the skills store's version, else its role's bundled template) behind the platform's rules and a per-session fence, and can read its run's issue; a new seeded **Issue triage** agent classifies and labels each labelled issue on a claim of its own, and Bug fixer and Feature builder act on an issue once its trusted triage says their kind. The gate runner runs the deterministic gate (`run_gate`), which the engineering images now ship with their toolchains pinned to the gate packs, and the final go reads the gate records and the findings. Model tokens are priced into a run's spend, every session's transcript and each run's manifest are kept, Learn is every flow's last step, and a run's pull request opens ready for review (a draft only when its flow says `pr: draft`): a person approves and merges, never an agent. Readiness checks say what a run needs, and Engineering Enable waits on the required ones. In the app, an **Agents → Setup guide** walks an administrator through the loop in the recommended order (every step skippable), every place that enables an agent shows its readiness first, Skills says when a role's template is updated and offers it as a proposal, Administration gains the deployment's **Data sources**, and the assistant proposes categories on an approval card.

### Added

- The orchestration templates, `voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/` ([README](voc-datalake/templates/orchestration/README.md); a root `templates/orchestration/README.md` points there), with the schemas of each kind (`schemas/`: `voc-agent-card/1`, `voc-flow-template/1`, `voc-automation/1`, the SKILL.md front matter, the step assertion, `voc-orchestration-bundle/1`):
  - `agents/<role>/{agent.yaml,SKILL.md}` for the 12 launchable roles (the card: harness, model, tools, broker operations, caps, inputs, outputs and eval cases; the skill: Role, Reads, Writes, Steps, Rules, When to stop and Examples), and `coach/agent.yaml`, Learn's card. The Issue triage and Bug hunt and fix roles are written anew, their examples on the sandbox's divide bug; the mapper, the builder and the PR reviewer are 7.47.00's records migrated as they were.
  - `_shared/PLATFORM_RULES.md`: the rules the harness puts before every skill (data is data, people, housekeeping, no customer text; a pull request opens as the flow says and merging is always a person's), which no skill version can drop.
  - `flows/`: Understand repository, Issue triage, Bug hunt and fix, Feature and PR review, each with its built-in `memory` (recall), `learn` and `pr` settings and per-step assertions (a closed vocabulary of 19 checks that platform code evaluates on what a step recorded, `lambda/engineering/orchestration/assertions.py`).
  - `automations/`: the four seeded agents (Autonomous Product, Issue triage, Bug fixer, Feature builder), each with its marker, body, flow, $50 monthly budget and the readiness checks its Enable waits on.
  - `gates/`: one pack per language (`python`, `typescript`, `rust`, `java`), reconciled with the owner's three quality-gate briefs (`gates/briefs/`, each difference and its outcome in `RECONCILIATION.md`).
  - `evals/<flow>/cases/`: the benchmark's cases moved here, plus `bug-hunt-and-fix/divide-floor-bug` (the sandbox at its seeded bug) and four Issue triage cases (the expected kind and severity).
  - `bundle.json`, the generated compile, committed and drift-checked, with its Lambda copy `lambda/shared/orchestration_bundle.json`.
- `npm run orchestration:validate` (schemas; SKILL.md's sections and front matter; each card's tools and broker operations against what the harness and the broker grant its role; models in the allowed list; flows, gates, eval cases and assertions; automations; no placeholder; both bundles current; also in `scripts/validate.sh` and pytest), `orchestration:compile`, `orchestration:promote-pending` (moves a card's pending tools and broker operations into it once the platform offers them, bumping its template version), `orchestration:run -- --flow <id> --repo <path> [--dry-run] [--models fake]` (the compiled flow, its resolved skills and the gate plan; or the flow end to end on the local fake runtime, scripted models acting out an eval case's known fix with the gate's checks run for real and each step's assertions printed) and `orchestration:calibrate` (caps and budgets from run manifests).
- **Issue triage**, a third seeded engineering agent (`AGENTSEED#issue-triage`, disabled, $50 a month, with `-c engineeringAgents=true`): its `github_issue` trigger takes each labelled issue at its **triage** stage, any kind, on a claim of its own (`ISSUE_RUN#default` / `<owner/name>#<n>#triage`, beside the act claim, so a triage never keeps Bug fixer or Feature builder from the issue). The understander reads the issue, writes a `voc-triage/1` record (kind bug, feature or investigation; severity S1-S4; the code involved; acceptance criteria), comments on the issue and labels it; the run's end copies the record, create-only, to the issue's trusted row `ISSUE_TRIAGE#default` / `<owner/name>#<n>` (written by `voc-engineering-runtime` alone; every other writer of `voc-agents` is denied it).
- `requires_triage` on an act `github_issue` trigger (`bug` for Bug fixer, `feature` for Feature builder, as seeded): while an enabled Issue triage agent watches the same connection, the trigger takes an issue only once its trusted triage row says that kind; with none enabled there, 7.47.00's rule (the issue's feedback type) holds. GitHub labels are informative only. [docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md)
- The broker's `label_issue`: the understander's triage labels on its run's own issue only (`voc-triage/<kind>`, `voc-severity/s<n>`, from a fixed allowlist; one kind and one severity, once per attempt; no way-of-working check, as it pushes nothing).
- New agent tools (`lambda/engineering/runtime/harness/`): `read_issue` (the understander, hunter, fixer, committer, PR author and coordinator: the run's issue, fenced as data), `write_triage`, the understander's `post_comment` on its issue and `label_issue`, `run_gate` (the gate runner: the packs detect the checkout's languages, plan their checks and run each in the sandbox; the gate record's checks are the harness's record of them, so a GO is the packs' and never a model's word), and the final go's `read_gate_record` and `read_findings`.
- Which skill an agent runs: at launch, the flow step's pinned version (accepted only), else the skills store's current version for the run's connection, else its role's bundled template (`<role>@template-<n>`); the session row records the label, and the agent's model and harness follow it. The board's `skill` operation serves that record (and the bundle's platform rules) by the session's label, never one the agent names; a store that cannot be read refuses the launch, never a template in its place. The skills store seeds a role's shared skill from its template at an administrator's Skills visit, every version names its provenance, and a role's history says when a newer template is bundled. [docs/autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#which-skill-an-agent-runs-75000)
- Memory recall: the board's `memory` operation gives a task's brief the approved lessons of its repository and role, as the flow's `memory` setting asks.
- Transcripts: every agent session's whole transcript, redacted, under its own create-only keys (`ws/default/runs/<run>/<agent>/commits/<sha>/_transcripts/attempt-<n>/<chunk>.jsonl`), flushed at each checkpoint and at the end; the runtime writes each run's manifest (`ws/default/runs/<run>/_manifest/v<n>.json`: flow and revision, agents, sessions, models, tokens, cost) and an index by flow and day (`ws/default/transcripts-index/<flow>/<day>/<run>.json`). Kept forever. [docs/autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#transcripts-and-the-runs-manifest-75000)
- Learn, every flow's last step: the run-end retrospective runs on done, failed and stopped, and by the supervisor's sweep on a run at a person past the flow's `after_needs_human_hours` (72 by default); it reads the failed attempt's transcript as excerpts, its coach's tokens count in the run's spend within the flow's `budget_share` of the run's cost cap, and `learn.enabled: false` turns it off. Its lessons and skill proposals still wait for an administrator.
- Readiness: `GET /agents/engineering/readiness?automation=<agent id>` or `?flow=<template id>[&connection=&language=]` (administrators acting for themselves, REST only; 404 with the module off) answers each check, `{id, status, detail, fix, docs, required}`: the connection and its App installation, the CI attestation and branch protection, an image for the language, the knowledge pack and tenets where the flow requires them, the Issues source and the label, the enabling administrator's stored way of working, the budget and the hard cap, Bedrock access to every model the flow runs on, AgentCore's sessions quota, the memory setting, the network and a probe of the workspace bucket. Engineering Enable runs the required ones and answers 409 with those that fail. [docs/autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#readiness-75000)
- A flow's `pr` setting, `ready` (the default) or `draft`, recorded on the run (`pull_request`) and honoured by the broker at the open.
- **Agents → Setup guide** (`/agents/setup[/<step>]`, administrators with the engineering agents on): prerequisites (GitHub through the deployment's App, the CI attestation, the issues ingested), Understand the repository and Tenets (their flows arrive in a later release), Issue triage, Bug fixer, Feature builder and Ready to go (**Run on an issue now**; every run learns, its proposals wait in Skills), in the recommended order. Every step but the last is **Skip for now**, saying plainly what skipping costs; none is locked, and Enable is gated by readiness only. What is set up is read from the existing routes; the person's choices are `GET`/`PUT /agents/engineering/setup` (one `voc-agents` row, `SETTINGS#engineering_setup`, with a create-only audit row per save; 409 when another administrator saved meanwhile). While nothing is set up, the Agents list offers **Help me set up** or **Skip** once for the deployment. [docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#setup-guide)
- Readiness before Enable in the web app: the Set up dialog, the agents list's card, an agent's Enabled switch and the setup guide show each check (passed, failing, warning or unknown; required or advice), the server's finding, its fix and its doc link, and Enable waits while a required check does not pass; Enable's 409 shows its failing checks. The way-of-working check links to Administration → Users. [docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#readiness-before-enable)
- Skills → **Template updated (vN)**: a role whose bundled template is newer than every version of the scope seeded from one says so on its panel, shows what the template changes (`GET /agents/engineering/skills/<role>/template?connection=`: the template, its record and its diff from the version the scope runs) and **Adopt as a proposal** (`POST …/skills/<role>/template/adopt?connection=` `{expected_current, template_version}`): a new version proposed by that administrator (provenance `template`), which runs only once an administrator accepts it like any proposal; 409 when what the screen showed moved or that template is proposed already. Administrators acting for themselves only. [docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#template-updated)
- **Administration → Data sources** (`/admin/data-sources`, platform admins only): the Data sources page in the deployment's scope (no workspace header), the sources that feed the deployment and so the engineering automations (the GitHub Issues source among them).
- The assistant's `save_categories` (administrators): the categories it proposes, 1 to 10 with an optional product and up to 5 subcategories each, on an approval card where each is edited (renamed, its product, subcategories added or removed, a category left out) before **Approve**, which adds the edited set to the current workspace's categories (the deployment's outside one) and changes or removes nothing configured; a stored list that changed since the card read it saves nothing. A card-only write: a plan never names it. In all nine languages. [docs/categories.md](docs/categories.md)
- `-c engineeringModelPrices`: each model's token price over the runtime's defaults (the AWS Price List's us-west-2 figures for the global inference profiles, standard tier). [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)

### Changed

- Changed: a run's spend counts model tokens: each model's tokens are priced and added to the session's `cost_usd`, its ledger row and the flow's month in the same transaction as the session time, so a run's cost cap, its flow's budget alerts and the hard cap bound model spend (a model with no price is priced at the dearest listed). Agents → Spend and the hard cap's hints say so, in all nine languages.
- Changed: a run's pull request opens ready for review unless its flow says `pr: draft`; an update never changes it either way, every body ends with the line that the merge is a person's, and there is still no merge, approval or ready operation anywhere (tenet 3 and the broker's docs say so). The Bug hunt and fix and Feature templates' descriptions say "a pull request ready for review", in all nine languages.
- Changed: every tool result an agent reads is fenced with a per-session random marker (was a fixed `<data>` tag), and the platform's rules come before every skill with the session's fence in them.
- Changed: the engineering images ship the deterministic gate (the standard-library gate modules, the orchestration loader and bundle, the packs at `/opt/voc/gates`) and pin their toolchains to the packs' `[image]`: Python 3.12.16, Node 24.22.3, Rust 1.99.1, Temurin 25.0.5+8 with Maven 3.9.16 and Gradle 9.8.0, each checksum-checked; the Python and Rust images add Node 24 for a repository's TypeScript half, and their dependency step reaches npm's registry (Rust's `static.rust-lang.org` too).
- Changed: the gate packs are one per language, `python`, `typescript`, `rust` and `java` (`python-ts` and `rust-ts` stay as aliases, so a stored flow's packs list stays valid): a TypeScript-only repository gets only `typescript`, a Rust-only one only `rust`. Python also detects `requirements-dev.txt`, and a root of test files with no marker (whose dependency step installs pytest).
- Changed: `GET /workflows/templates`, the web app's flow templates and the seeded agents are read from the bundle, in the same shapes. A new deployment's Bug fixer gets the plain Bug hunt and fix flow (Issue triage is its own agent); a Bug fixer seeded before keeps its flow, and no stored row is rewritten.
- Changed: the web app keeps a `github_issue` trigger's `stage` and `requires_triage` as the agent has them, so saving an agent's settings never turns Issue triage into an act trigger or drops Bug fixer's and Feature builder's required triage; the dev mock seeds the three agents with their triggers.
- Changed: a flow's `memory`, `learn` and `pr` settings ride on its start step's params and each step's assertions on `params.assert`, both optional, so a flow saved before stays valid and the editor and the assistant keep them as written.
- Changed: IAM, with `-c engineeringAgents=true`: the runtime's role reads the understanders' `_triage/` records and the agents' `_transcripts/` (listing that prefix only), writes only the runs' manifests and the transcripts' index, and puts `ISSUE_TRIAGE#*` rows create-only (every other writer of `voc-agents` is denied them); the board's role is denied every write of the skills', the memory's and the scorecards' rows; the Agents API's role gains the readiness checks' reads (`bedrock:GetFoundationModelAvailability`, `servicequotas:GetServiceQuota` on AgentCore's sessions quota, `GetItem` of the Issues source's watermarks) and one create-only `PutObject` under `ws/default/_readiness/*`. Each grant is pinned by its stack test, with negative pins (no agent writes beyond its own keys).
- Docs: docs/autonomous-engineering.md (which skill an agent runs, the fences and the new tools, transcripts and the manifest, Learn, readiness, the role catalog's tools), docs/autonomous-agents.md (the seeded agents, Issue triage, claims per stage, `requires_triage`, the setup guide, readiness before Enable, Template updated), docs/categories.md, docs/scrapers.md and docs/assistant-plan-mode.md (`save_categories`), docs/github-issues.md and docs/account-vs-admin.md (the deployment's Data sources), docs/deployment.md (the image rebuild and digests, `engineeringModelPrices`), docs/multi-workspace.md (the transcripts, manifests, index, triage claim and trusted triage row in the deployment-wide list and the 3g3 inventory; the deployment's Data sources).

### Removed

- The Self-improvement flow template leaves the templates list (its steps stay valid in stored flows). `voc-datalake/engineering-gates/` (now `templates/orchestration/gates/`) and `voc-datalake/engineering-benchmark/` (its cases now under `templates/orchestration/evals/`) are gone; so is `lambda/shared/engineering_flow_templates.json`, which the bundle replaces.

### Fixed

- The checkout's `chmod` is found in the system's own directories (`/usr/bin:/bin`; macOS has `/bin/chmod` only), so the checkout's commands and the checkout cache's git tests run on macOS too.

### Upgrade notes

- With `-c engineeringAgents=true`, rebuild and push all four engineering images for linux/arm64 from `voc-datalake/` (Java: Temurin 25 with Maven 3.9.16 and Gradle 9.8.0; Python: Python 3.12 with Node 24; Rust: Rust 1.99.1 with Node 24; Node: Node 24), read each new digest and deploy them with the stacks in the same deploy, `-c engineeringImages='{"python":"sha256:…","node":"sha256:…","rust":"sha256:…","java":"sha256:…"}'` ([deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)). A runtime keeps running the image its digest names: on the old digests its sessions run the old harness, without `run_gate`, the new tools or the bundled skills.
- Model tokens are priced from this deploy on (earlier tokens stay unpriced), so a run's cost cap is reached sooner than before; set `-c engineeringModelPrices` only to override the list prices. For a first run on a small sandbox repository, `-c engineeringRunTokenCap=3000000` keeps it well under the run cap (optional; 10 million by default).
- The setup guide's progress is one new `voc-agents` row (`SETTINGS#engineering_setup`, with its audit rows), written by the Agents API's existing grants; the template routes use the skills store's existing grants. No new route is public: every new one is an administrator's, REST only.
- Transcripts, run manifests and the transcripts' index are kept forever in `voc-eng-workspace` (no expiry, no lifecycle deletion of current versions): only the multi-workspace hard delete (3g3) and an erasure of a person's data where it requires one remove them. A transcript holds repository, issue and model text, redacted when written, and may hold a handle a person wrote on an issue.
- The first admin listing of the agents after the deploy seeds Issue triage, disabled. Enable it on the connection Bug fixer and Feature builder use for them to act on triaged issues only; until then they keep 7.47.00's rule. Engineering Enable now answers 409 naming the failing required checks (the connection, the CI attestation where the flow pushes, an image, Bedrock access to the Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 global profiles, the budget, and the enabling administrator's stored AI-assisted or AI-driven way of working): `GET /agents/engineering/readiness?automation=<agent id>` lists each with its fix.
- A pull request now opens ready for review. A flow that should keep opening drafts needs `pr: draft` on its start step (the templates set `pr: ready`); with branch protection's required approval, a person still approves and merges.
- Rollback: disable Issue triage first (an earlier release does not read a trigger's stage, so it would run triage on the issue's one act claim). Runs started under 7.50.00 are best left to end first. The `ISSUE_TRIAGE#` rows, the triage claims and the transcripts stay and are inert to an earlier release.

## [7.49.00] - 2026-11-16

Every in-app place is a path, across the whole app: where a person is (a page, its tab and section, the item open on it, a sub-view, a mode) is the path, so Back and Forward walk tabs and sections, a copied link opens the same place and the assistant's page context reads the tab from the path; only what combines freely (filters, search, a sort, a window, a scope picker) stays in the query. 7.46.00 did this for a project page; this release does it for Administration, Account, Company, Memory, Participants, the Data Explorer, the Agents list and an agent's tabs, the feedback boards (in the app and standalone, their sign-in included) and the expired-session sign-in. A workspace's addresses move from `/w/<slug>/…` to `/workspace/<slug>/…`. There are no redirects from the forms of before (`/w/…`, `?tab=`, `&section=`, `?doc=`, `?view=`, `?request=`, 7.46.00's project query links included): a pre-release change, nobody has an older build installed. Also: GitHub's return from the deployment's GitHub App lands in the workspace the flow started in (never the workspace picker), a new App is named `VoC Autonomous Agent <hex4>` and **Check installation** records the slug of an App renamed on GitHub, an App-created connection's **Edit** dialog fits the viewport and offers only what can change, a platform admin's direct link into a workspace takes the console's own (checked, audited) entry, the conversations list answers such a platform admin instead of 404, no dialog inherits its trigger's text alignment, and the e2e users script gets `create`.

### Added

- Paths (`frontend/src/routes.tsx`; each area's builders and readers beside its page, the shared parts in `utils/pathPlace.ts` and `utils/tabPaths.ts`), inside a workspace after its `/workspace/<slug>`:
  - Administration (`pages/Settings/adminPaths.ts`, route `admin/*`): `/admin/<tab>[/<section>]` (`/admin` is General), the Boards section's open editor `/admin/access/boards/<boardId>`.
  - Account, Company, Memory, Participants (`accountSections.ts`, `companyPaths.ts`, `memoryPaths.ts`, `participantsPaths.ts`; routes `account/*`, `company/*`, `memory/*`, `participants/*`): `/<page>/<tab>`, the page's own path being its first tab.
  - The Data Explorer (`dataExplorerPaths.ts`, route `data-explorer/*`): `/data-explorer/raw` (`/data-explorer`) and `/data-explorer/processed`.
  - The Agents list's views (`pages/Agents/agentsPaths.ts`): `/agents/workflows`, `/agents/spend`, `/agents/connections`, `/agents/skills`, and on Skills a role's history `/agents/skills/<role>` and a version `/agents/skills/<role>/v/<n>`. Each view is a route of its own (`agents/<view>/*`), so it ranks above `agents/:id/*`; an agent's id is never a view's name (`ag_<12 hex>`). `/agents/workflows` is the Workflows view itself (it redirected to `?tab=workflows`).
  - An agent's tabs: `/agents/<id>/<tab>` (`/agents/<id>` is Settings; route `agents/:id/*`).
  - The feedback boards (`pages/FeatureRequests/boardContext.ts`, `boardPaths.ts`): `/feature-requests/insights`; a request open on its board `/feature-requests/<slug>/<requestId>` and `/board/<slug>/<requestId>` (Back closes it); a request known only by its id (a document's `[FR:<id>]` citation, Insights' most-supported list) `/feature-requests/requests/<requestId>` and `/board/requests/<requestId>`, looked up and opened on its board; the standalone sign-in `/board/login/<slug>[/<requestId>]`, which lands back there.
  - `/login/expired`, the sign-in page saying the session ended (`services/sessionExpiry.ts`).
- `frontend/src/locationParams.test.ts`: every production module that reads the query (`useSearchParams`, a `.get` / `.getAll` / `.has` on a URLSearchParams, `api/` included) is listed with the keys it reads, their kind and why; no module reads a location key (`tab`, `section`, `doc`, `view`, `request`, `role`, `version`, `expired`). A new reader, a new key, a key read through a name the scan cannot resolve (an imported constant, a loop variable; a helper's parameter is named in its entry), a location key read anywhere, or an in-app link written with a location query (`/admin?tab=…`, `?view=`) fails it. The Agents views and the tab pages are read from their path modules by the breadcrumbs and the page context (`agentsPaths.ts` `AGENTS_PATH_VIEWS`, `pages/tabPathPages.ts`).
- GitHub's return into the flow's workspace (`frontend/src/workspace/returnWorkspace.ts`, `gateDecision.ts`, `pages/Agents/githubReturn.ts`): the manifest request names the workspace the flow starts in (`{account, org?, workspace?}`, a slug as the platform makes one, `lambda/engineering/connectors/github_apps.py` `parse_workspace`), and the manifest's `redirect_url` comes back into it, `…/workspace/<slug>/agents/connections/github/created`. The `setup_url` stays top-level (it is fixed when the App is made, and an install can start in any workspace); opened outside a workspace, either return page goes straight into the workspace the flow started in (remembered in the tab when the manifest is posted or an install link opened, whether or not the caller's list names it: a platform admin who entered from the console comes back to it, and the gate decides again there; else the workspace last entered; else the caller's first), its query carried through, in place of the top-level address (`location.replace`: Back never lands on GitHub's query again), and never shows the workspace picker. The pages then take their query out of the address as before.
- **Check installation** (`POST /agents/engineering/github-apps/<app_id>/check`) records the App's slug as its installation reports it (`app_slug`, which the token function's `inspect_installation` now answers) when it differs, with the App's page and a `github_app_renamed` audit row (an App renamed on GitHub can get a new slug), so **Install more** keeps working; the App's row reads it again at once. The slug is learned from an installation, so an App renamed before its first install keeps the slug it was made with (docs/autonomous-engineering.md says what to do).
- The edit dialog of a connection the GitHub App saved (`pages/Agents/ConnectionDialog.tsx`): its App and installation and its repository read only, the default branch and an optional reason (kept with the connection's audit row) as the only fields; no host choice, no pasted-key fields, no key guidance.
- A platform admin's direct link into a workspace they are not a member of (`/workspace/<slug>/…` pasted or shared: with every place a path, every shared link is one): the gate takes the console's own entry, never a bypass (`frontend/src/workspace/platformDirectEntry.ts`, `WorkspaceGate.tsx`). For a token that names `platform-admins`, on a slug outside the caller's list with no entry recorded in the tab, it reads the workspace's id from the console's list (`GET /platform/workspaces`, platform admins only, page by page), records it as **Enter** does (`platformEntry.ts`), and asks `GET /me/workspaces/current` with it, which live-checks the platform admin and audits the entry (`lambda/shared/workspace.py`), as for the console's Enter. Anyone else gets the same "Workspace not found" as for any slug that is not theirs, and the console's list is not even asked; a server refusal drops the record.
- `bash e2e/scripts/e2e-users.sh create` (`voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/scripts/e2e-users.sh`): makes the e2e suite's two Cognito test users when they are missing (`e2e-admin` in `admins`, `e2e-viewer` in `users`, both in `e2e`; their emails from `E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `E2E_USER_EMAIL`, marked verified), with no invitation and no password printed, disabled until `enable`; a user that exists is left as it is and only its groups made sure of, so it is idempotent. The usage line, the e2e README and docs/deployment.md say so.
- In all nine languages: `common:breadcrumbs.insights`, `.skills`, `.spend` (the route table's new segments) and `agents:connections.dialog.appCreatedTitle`, `.appCreatedHint`, `.repositoryFixed`, `.reason`, `.reasonHint`.

### Changed

- Changed: a workspace's addresses are `/workspace/<slug>/…` (were `/w/<slug>/…`): the router's base path (`frontend/src/workspace/workspacePath.ts`), every link built from it (`workspaceUrl`, `pageHref`), the platform console's and Workspace settings' shown address, the GitHub App manifest's `redirect_url`, the mocks and the e2e suite. `workspace` is reserved: no top-level page and no agent id is named so (`routes.paramNames.test.ts`). A `/w/…` address is now a plain unknown page.
- Removed: every query-to-path redirect, for a pre-release change nobody has installed: 7.46.00's project links (`?tab=`, `?doc=`, `?view=focus`: `projectPaths.ts` `legacyPlace`), and none is added for the other pages (`?tab=`, `&section=`, `&board=`, `?view=processed`, `?request=`, `?board=` on the board sign-in, `/login?expired=1`); Administration's pre-5.09 tab ids, Account's 5.09–5.11 `?section=` ids and Company's `?tab=mine` go with them. Such a link opens the page's first tab. A path that does not name its place as it should (an unknown tab, a tab without its section) is still replaced by its own path, in place. `/settings` and `/feedback` stay route aliases (the assistant's navigation links `/settings`).

- Changed: a tab, section, view or item switch is a history entry (Memory's, Participants', Account's and the Agents pages' tabs used to replace theirs, and Company's were page state), so Back and Forward walk them; moving to the place already shown adds none. The rest of the query stays on a move (an open review's `?review=`), except where a view owns its options: leaving Agents → Spend drops its month, grouping and workflow, leaving Insights its board and window, as before.
- Changed: every in-app link names the path (`adminPath`, `accountTabPath`, `companyTabPath`, `agentPath`, `agentsPath`, `flowRunsPath`, `boardRequestPath`, `requestLookupPath`, …): the assistant's result links (Users, Radar settings), Home's onboarding step and agent decision cards, the breadcrumbs (the Workflows and Connections crumbs link `/agents/workflows` and `/agents/connections`), Radar's Configure, Data sources' and the design system's links, a board card's Edit, the share link of a request, the `[FR:<id>]` citations and the GitHub return pages' way back (`GitHubReturnFrame.tsx`: `/agents/connections`).
- Changed: the breadcrumb trail ends at the page for a page's own places (its tab, section, view, open request or version), at the agent for an agent's tab, as it already did at the project (`components/Breadcrumbs/routeCrumbs.ts` `trailSegments`).
- Changed: the assistant's page context names the tab from the path (`/admin/<tab>/…`, `/memory/<tab>`, an Agents view, an agent's tab, the boards' Insights); its route table follows the new routes (`assistant/page/pageContext.ts`). The stream contract's `page.tab` note says so (`lambda/stream/src/assistant/contract.ts`, a comment only).
- Changed: the unsaved-changes guards follow the paths: Administration's brand draft asks only on leaving `/admin` (`isLeavingAdmin`), the default theme's pick on leaving General, an agent's config draft on leaving its six config tabs.
- Changed: the board slugs `insights` and `requests` are reserved (`lambda/shared/feature_boards_store.py` `RESERVED_SLUGS`, with `login` and `boards`), so no board shadows `/feature-requests/insights` or a request lookup. A reserved slug is refused when it is new (a create, or a rename to one); a board stored with one before keeps it through its other edits (the editor sends the slug with every save).
- Changed: a request's copied link (**Copy link** on its dialog) carries the page's `/workspace/<slug>` (`boardContext.ts` `shareLinkFor`, as a review's copied link), so it opens the same place in the same workspace; the request lookup is `RequestLookup.tsx` (was `OldRequestLink.tsx`).
- Changed: `bash e2e/scripts/e2e-users.sh create` stops, saying so, when it made a user it could not disable (a rerun would leave it as it is), so a test user is never left enabled unseen.
- Changed: a workspace's slug rule has one home, `lambda/shared/workspace_ids.py` (`WORKSPACE_SLUG`, `RESERVED_WORKSPACE_SLUGS`, `is_workspace_slug`), which `shared/platform_workspaces.py` and the GitHub App manifest (`github_apps.py` `parse_workspace`) both read.
- Changed: a new GitHub App is named `VoC Autonomous Agent <hex4>` (25 characters; GitHub takes at most 34, and an App's name is unique on all of GitHub, hence the suffix), was `VoC agents <hex6>` (`github_apps.py` `app_name`).
- Fixed: `GET /chat/conversations/_list` (and a conversation by id) answered a platform admin inside a workspace they are not a member of the one 404 "Workspace not found", so the assistant's sessions list failed there while every other route answered. It now answers 200 and an empty list (a conversation by id: its own 404), as the assistant's stream Lambda, the other writer of these rows, answers their runs and saves nothing for them (`session/workspace-member.ts` `resolveSessionOwner`, LOCKSTEP); nothing is elevated, read or written, and the writes stay a member's (`lambda/api/chat_handler.py` `_reading_caller`). A malformed id, a service subject and anyone else keep the 404. No IAM change.
- Fixed: a platform admin's direct-link lookup that failed (a fault or a throttle of `GET /platform/workspaces`, not its 403) showed "Workspace not found" for a workspace that may exist: it is the gate's "could not load" page with **Try again** now, and a warning in the console; the lookup reads 100 workspaces a page (`platformDirectEntry.ts`, `platformWorkspacesApi.list`'s `limit`).
- Fixed: the agents list did not show 7.47.00's **Set up**, so an administrator had to open each engineering agent to find it. An engineering agent that is not set up now shows, on its list card and to an administrator, the same **Set up** (the same dialog) or **Connect a repository first** (to Agents → Connections) with the reason, and no state badge of its own (the row shows the agent's); nothing once it is set up or to a user (`pages/Agents/AgentEngineering.tsx` `EngineeringSetUpCard`, `Agents.tsx`). Its link to Connections, 7.47.00's `/agents?tab=connections`, is `/agents/connections`.
- Fixed: a dialog rendered inside a right-aligned (or centred) wrapper inherited its alignment, so every title, label and hint sat on the right (7.47.00's agent **Set up** dialog, inside its control's `text-right` wrapper): the shared dialog shell starts its text from the start (`components/ModalShell/ModalShell.tsx` `text-start`), for every dialog of the app.
- Fixed: an App-created connection's **Edit** dialog was taller than the viewport with nothing to scroll: every connection dialog is now at most the viewport's height (`max-h-[90vh]`, as the other long dialogs), its body scrolling between a fixed header and footer, on a phone too (`ConnectionModals.tsx`).
- What stays a query, and why (each module in `locationParams.test.ts`): filters and search (Categories', Problem Analysis' and the Dashboard's facets, Radar's `brand` and `days`, a board list's `q`, `status`, `sort`, Insights' `board`, `days`, Agents → Spend's `month`, `by`, `workflow`, Agents → Skills' scope `connection`); the review modal (`review`, `reviewBrand`: it opens over any page, so no one page's path); a form's prefill read once (Connect's `project`, a project's decision draft); and external callbacks (GitHub's App returns `?code=&state=` and `?installation_id=&setup_action=&state=`, the MCP OAuth consent's authorize request, the emailed board sign-in link's `email`, `code`, the unsubscribe link's `t`), which are the other party's by design and stripped once read.
- Mock (`frontend/mock-github-apps.js`): the manifest takes `workspace` and answers the new name and the workspace's `redirect_url`.
- Tests: the production e2e suite opens every page by its path and asserts paths and `/workspace/<slug>` (`frontend/e2e/`: the screen inventory, surfaces, every project, agent, Account, Administration, Company, Memory, Participants, Data Explorer and board spec, and document-canvas's `/focus`, left on `?view=focus` by 7.46.00; its COVERAGE.md and README follow). Its checks of the query redirects of before are gone with them (`/company?tab=mine`, Account's `?section=mcp`, `/agents?tab=workflows`); Company's **My objectives** link is checked in their place, and `/projects/<id>/mcp` (was `?tab=mcp`) still lands on Overview.
- Docs: docs/document-canvas.md's "Addresses" (every address, what stays a query and why, the GitHub return, CloudFront), docs/multi-workspace.md (the direct link, the conversations list), docs/deployment.md (`create`), docs/account-vs-admin.md, docs/feature-requests.md, docs/memory.md, docs/briefing.md, docs/company-context.md, docs/project-workspace.md, docs/participants.md, docs/radar.md, docs/categories.md, docs/github-issues.md, docs/autonomous-engineering.md (Skills, Spend, the GitHub App's name, the workspace return, renaming an App on GitHub: Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → the App → **Edit**), docs/autonomous-agents.md, docs/assistant-plan-mode.md, docs/processing-pipeline.md.

### Upgrade notes

- No stack, route or stored data changes beyond the Lambdas' code: a normal deploy (`npm run deploy:all`). CloudFront already serves every new path: an unknown path is S3's 404, which the distribution answers with `index.html` (`lib/stacks/core-cdn.ts`), and no app path starts with `/avatars/` or `/prototypes/`, its only other behaviours.
- No redirects (a pre-release change: nobody has an earlier build installed): a `/w/<slug>/…` address, and a link that names its place in the query (`?tab=`, `&section=`, `&board=`, `?doc=`, `?view=`, `?request=`, `/login?expired=1`), are not rewritten. `/w/<slug>/…` is an unknown page; a query link opens its page's first tab. Bookmarks of a test deployment are made again from the new paths.
- A board whose slug is `insights` or `requests` (none is made by the app's own slug rule, but an administrator could type one) is shadowed by the new paths in the app: it stays reachable by its id (`/feature-requests/<board_id>`), and a new slug can be given in Administration → Privacy & access → Boards.
- The assistant's `suggest_navigation` still takes the page paths it took (no query, no new tab path): unchanged.
- GitHub Apps made before this release keep their name and their `setup_url`; their returns outside a workspace now go straight into the workspace the flow started in. To rename one, do it on GitHub (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → the App → **Edit**), then press **Check installation** on Agents → Connections so the stored slug follows.
- A platform admin's direct link needs nothing new on the server: it reads the console's list (`GET /platform/workspaces`) and enters through `GET /me/workspaces/current` as the console's Enter does (same live check, same audit row).
- Rollback: an earlier release reads `/w/<slug>` and the query links, not the new paths: a link copied from this release (`/workspace/acme/admin/access/users`) does not open there.

## [7.48.00] - 2026-11-16

Multi-workspace, phase 3g-d: an erasure reaches the deployment's own projects, where every real reviewer address is today. An erasure by email removes the address from the deployment's review link audiences (a revoked link's too), its comment threads and replies (a deleted project's too), its projects' owner and member fields and their personas' research notes (a deleted or half-deleted project's too, for both), by the same code as a workspace's, and lists for review the product documents whose extracted text, or its filename, holds it. The deployment now keeps a registry of its projects, of its review links and of its commented series, written by the project create, the link create, a series' first thread and the project bundle's import; a backfill lists what was made before (run it once after upgrading: see the upgrade notes). The deployment's erasure job's row now says whether it walked the deployment's projects, so an admin can tell from the data which jobs to submit again. The lineage marks no longer scan the whole projects table once the backfill has run. 3h, the switch, no longer waits for 3g-d (it still waits for 3g2, 3g3, the erasure panel's review list and 3g-d2, the removal of the erasure's Scan fallback) ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md#the-project-plan-phase-3)).

### Changed

- Changed: the deployment's erasure by email without a source walks the deployment's own projects first in its `workspace_projects` phase, then every listed workspace as before (`voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/retention/project_people.py`, one walker for both scopes): every review link (an audience scrubbed before the threads are read), every commented series' threads, then every project its registry lists (a deleted or half-deleted project too: the delete's fence takes its `META` off `gsi1-by-type`, never off the registry) with its `META`, product documents and personas, then the company persona library. The same de-identification as in a workspace (7.43.00): a link's audience loses the address (a list link left admitting nobody is revoked), a reviewer's author fields go, a name that is the address becomes "Team member", a `META` loses `owner_email` and the matching `members` entries' email and name. Each change is recorded before and after under `AUDIT#tombstone#deployment_projects` (never the address, a link's id or a workspace) and counted in `project_rows_deidentified`. The phase now runs when voc-workspaces is not configured too (the deployment's projects alone). A workspace's own erasure never walks the deployment's projects, and a hand-over that carries them fails it. The cursor says `deployment_done` once they are walked; a walk that began with the job then takes the workspace listing's start time again (the hours the deployment's walk took are not counted as the listing's window), and a deployment job's cursor that says neither (a cursor of 7.43.00 to 7.47.00 carried across the upgrade) walks them first, then goes on where it was, its listing state kept as it is. The deployment's walk refuses to write a row whose key is a workspace's.
- Added: the deployment's erasure by email without a source says on its job row and its audit row `deployment_projects_walked` (true or false) and `deployment_rows_found` (`registry` or `scan`, once it walked them), and the erasure job's API view (`GET /settings/erasure`, `voc-datalake/lambda/api/settings_handler.py` `erasure_job_view`) returns both, so the jobs that never reached the deployment's projects can be found (the Administration panel shows them with 3g-ui). No other job writes either field.
- Changed: a deployment project's delete (`api/projects.py` `delete_project`) sweeps its S3 objects (prototypes, product documents, owned avatars) before its rows, so a delete stopped in between leaves a product document's record without its objects (listed as not checked) rather than its extracted text without a record. An object S3 refuses to delete is still only logged, and the delete still finishes `deleted`; so an erasure by email lists a deleted or half-deleted deployment project's product documents folder in `files_not_checked`.
- Changed: a prototype pin's reply names its writer by their username, else "Team member", never their address (`api/projects_handler.py` `_pin_actor`; the rule a member's thread author follows since 7.43.00). Replies written before keep theirs (a D5 gap, docs/multi-workspace.md 3g-pin).
- Changed: an erasure job whose `workspace_id` is present but not a workspace id fails, instead of running as the deployment's job; and the Scan counts a link's routing row that names no workspace id as malformed.
- Changed: a deployment product document (`projects/<id>/product_docs/`) is judged by its extracted text, whatever its kind (the extractor writes text for every kind there: a PDF's, an image's description): a document whose filename or text holds the address is listed in `files_needing_review`; one with no text (pending, failed, never uploaded, a key the role cannot read) in `files_not_checked`. Its upload is never read. Nothing there is changed or deleted.
- Added: the deployment's registries in voc-projects (`voc-datalake/lambda/shared/project_keys.py`): `PROJECT_IDS` / `<project id>` for every deployment project (with its `created_at`), `DOCSHARE_IDS` / `<share id>` for every deployment review link (with its `project_id`, `series_id`, `created_at`) and `COMMENT_SERIES_IDS` / `<project>#<series>` for every commented series, one partition each, no `ttl`. A deployment project's create puts its registry row (if absent) before its `META` (`shared/project_writes.py` `register_deployment_project`; one more write per create), and its delete never removes it. A deployment link's create puts the link's and the series' rows in the transaction that writes the link (`shared/document_share.py`); a deployment thread first reads its series' row and puts it if absent only when it is not there (`shared/document_comments.py` `put_thread`: one more read per new thread, one write per series), and a persona review lists its series once for all the threads it files (`shared/document_review.py`); the project bundle's import (`voc-datalake/scripts/project_bundle/importer.py`) lists the imported project and each imported comment partition's series before its objects and rows, with boto3 alone (a plain import still needs only Python 3.12 and boto3, docs/project-export.md; the rows are the shared builders', and a test holds them to the stores' and runs the plain path without the Lambda dependencies). A test holds every module that writes a comment partition to listing its series, and every module that makes a project to listing it (`lambda/shared/test/test_comment_series_listed.py`; the verification fixture's project, which holds no person's data and expires by its own `ttl`, is the one exception, named there). The series registry is deployment-wide, not in the project's partition, because a deployment project's delete empties that partition but leaves its comment threads, which keep their reviewers' addresses. `put_thread` refuses, without a workspace too, a thread whose partition is not its series' (a workspace's refused it already).
- Added: `voc-datalake/scripts/projects/backfill_review_registries.py`, which lists the projects, links and series made before this release (see the upgrade notes), and `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/review_registries.py`, its Scan pages (strongly consistent, projected to six attributes; a series judged by the walker's own rule, a malformed comment partition counted once and never failing anything), which the erasure and the lineage pass also use until the backfill has run: they read the backfill's marker first, then walk the registries by Query, or, without a complete marker (its `completed_at`, its three counts and a `release` of 7.48.0 or later), find the same links, series and projects by Scans of voc-projects (one per pass: three per erasure by email, one per lineage pass). Either way they find the rows the stores had written when they read that part, provided every writer since the backfill ran 7.48.00 or later: a VocApiStack-only rollback below 7.48.00, or a bundle imported from an older checkout, breaks this until `--unmark`; a row written after (a new thread on a series already walked) is the next erasure's. The marker records the release it was taken under, and the backfill writes it only if there is exactly one projects API and one assist twin (now given `APP_VERSION`), each on 7.48.0 or later, its last update applied (`LastUpdateStatus` `Successful`) and older, when the walk began, than the longer of their timeouts plus 5 minutes; its progress is kept in a row of its own (`MIGRATION#review-registries#progress`, each update conditioned on its run's id), resumed with `--resume` under a new run id; the marker's put and the progress row's delete are one transaction on the same condition; `--unmark` deletes the marker.
- Changed: the deployment's lineage pass (`lineage`) reads the deployment's projects through `PROJECT_IDS` (or its Scan of the projects' `META` rows until the backfill has run) and its persona library, each project's own partition by filtered Query pages, as the workspace pass does (`voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/retention/lineage.py` `deployment_step`), instead of a Scan of the whole of voc-projects, whose cost would grow with every workspace's rows; it now runs as steps under the job's time budget and page cap. A lineage hand-over carrying the old Scan's cursor starts the pass again (every mark is idempotent).
- Changed (IAM, VocProcessingStack): the retention worker's role may Query voc-projects in the deployment's `PROJECT#*`, `DCOMMENTS#*`, `DOCSHARE#*`, `PROJECT_IDS`, `DOCSHARE_IDS` and `COMMENT_SERIES_IDS` partitions only, of the attributes its reads project only (`dynamodb:Attributes`, with `dynamodb:Select` `SPECIFIC_ATTRIBUTES` required, so a Query naming no attribute cannot read whole rows; every such Query now sends it), and no index; its attribute-limited UpdateItems (the two on voc-projects and the membership one) may ask for no returned values (`dynamodb:ReturnValues` `NONE` when named); and GetObject `projects/*/product_docs/extracted/*` (in the statement of a workspace's product documents). Its lineage UpdateItem is pinned to `PROJECT#*` and one workspace id's `PROJECT#*` (any partition before), and its de-identification UpdateItem now also reaches the deployment's `PROJECT#*`, `DCOMMENTS#*` and `DOCSHARE#*`, each still held to its attributes. Its Scan of voc-projects stays, used only to find the deployment's links, series and projects until the backfill has run, and is narrowed from the table and its indexes to the table alone and to the six attributes it projects (`dynamodb:Select` `SPECIFIC_ATTRIBUTES`, `dynamodb:Attributes`).
- Added (VocApiStack): the projects API and its assist twin get `APP_VERSION`. Added (VocCoreStack): a custom resource (`voc-datalake/lib/stacks/review-registries-marker.ts`, with CDK's AwsCustomResource provider, its role and its log group) deletes the backfill's marker when it is created (this upgrade) and when it is deleted (a rollback to a release without it), its policy allowed DeleteItem in voc-projects' `DOCSHARE_IDS` partition only (IAM cannot pin the sort key; the call names the marker's), the table key's Decrypt, and denied every audit row; the policy is on CDK's singleton AwsCustomResource role, and it is the stack's only AwsCustomResource. It is in VocCoreStack, beside the table, because VocApiStack's resource count is at its release ceiling, so it does not fire on a VocApiStack-only deploy (see the rollback note). It deletes the marker only, never the backfill's progress row: a walk resumed after any later deploy is voided by the backfill itself, which judges the writers against when the walk began.
- Docs: docs/multi-workspace.md's 7.48.00 row and the plan's 3g-d marked done (3h waits for 3g-ui, 3g2, 3g3 and 3g-d2, and its upgrade check refuses without the marker); the plan gains six entries: 3g-d2 (the Scan fallback and its grant removed, with its two guards), 3g-p (a deployment project's delete reaching its comment partitions and links), 3g-lin1 (the ids inside a document's `derivation`), 3g-lin2 (a persona job's `result`), 3g-pin (prototype pin replies written before) and 3g-bundle (the project bundles' files); TENETS.md D5's gaps (the deployment's projects are reached; an erasure that finished before this release must be run again; a deployment project's delete leaves its threads and links, the project bundles' files copy reviewer addresses no erasure reaches, a prototype pin's reply written before may name a member by address, and two older gaps of the lineage marks: an id cited inside a document's `derivation` and a persona job's `result` in voc-jobs, kept until its 7-day `ttl`; each now a plan entry: 3g-p, 3g-bundle, 3g-pin, 3g-lin1, 3g-lin2) and tenet 6's grants (the Scan's sensitive keys, the reset's shared role); docs/deployment.md's note on `--unmark` (a single-stack rollback, an import from an older checkout); docs/project-export.md's; docs/document-review.md's storage table (the two registries); docs/source-policies.md's erasure sections and grants; `.kiro/steering/tech.md`'s retention role and its load.
- Internal: `lib/test-support/baseline.json` regenerated (VocApiStack's, VocCoreStack's and VocProcessingStack's template hashes). `lambda/shared/persona_copy_routes.py`'s `_created` is renamed `_created_response`: the stored-attributes audit keys its write helpers by name, so the persona routes' helper, which only builds a 201 answer, keeps a name no writing helper shares (7.47.00 renamed the GitHub Apps' writing `_created` to `_conversion_answer` for the same reason).

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:all`). VocProcessingStack changes the retention worker (its code and grants); VocApiStack gives the projects API and its assist twin `APP_VERSION`; VocCoreStack adds the marker's reset (a custom resource: on this deploy it deletes any marker already there); VocApiStack, VocCoreStack and VocProcessingStack give every function whose bundle holds `lambda/shared/` new code (`shared/project_keys.py`, `shared/project_walk.py`, `shared/project_writes.py`, `shared/document_share.py`, `shared/document_comments.py` and `shared/document_review.py` change, and `shared/review_registries.py` is new). No table or index changes; the erasure job's API view gains two fields.
- Then run the backfill once from `voc-datalake/`: `.venv/bin/python scripts/projects/backfill_review_registries.py` for a dry run (it reads and prints what it would list), then again with `--apply` (`--projects-table NAME`, else the `PROJECTS_TABLE` environment, else the core stack's `ProjectsTableName` output; `--api-stack`, default `VocApiStack`; `--region`). It needs Scan, GetItem, PutItem, DeleteItem and TransactWriteItems on voc-projects and the KMS key's use, and, read-only, `cloudformation:DescribeStacks` on the core stack (only when the table is not named), `cloudformation:ListStackResources` on the API stack and `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` on its functions (which answers each function's environment variables, their names and values, ARNs among them; the script reads only `APP_VERSION`). It scans voc-projects three times (the links, the comment partitions, then the projects' `META` rows, a deleted project's too), puts each missing registry row if absent, and at the end of one applied walk nobody took over writes the marker `DOCSHARE_IDS` / `MIGRATION#review-registries` (with when, the counts and the release), but only if there is exactly one projects API and one assist twin in the API stack, each reporting `APP_VERSION` 7.48.0 or later, its last update applied (`LastUpdateStatus` `Successful`), and last updated, when the walk began, longer ago than the longer of their timeouts plus 5 minutes (20 minutes today), so no container of the older release could write a link, a thread or a project behind the Scans. An applied walk does not start otherwise (it says why: wait, and run it again), and one during which a writer is updated again (another deploy) writes no marker and drops its progress: run `--apply` again, a new walk. It changes no link, thread or project. It is safe to run again at any time: every put is conditional, so a second run lists nothing and only rewrites the marker. A long run can be split: `--max-pages N` stops after N Scan pages, and `--apply --resume` goes on from the progress row the stopped run left (`MIGRATION#review-registries#progress`), under a new run id, so the run it resumes stops if it is still alive; a second `--apply` started meanwhile takes the walk over the same way, and a run taken over writes nothing more and says so. A dry run keeps no progress. Until the marker is there, the deployment's erasures by email without a source find its links, series and projects by three Scans of voc-projects themselves (and each lineage pass by one): they reach the same rows, at a higher cost. A fresh deployment has nothing to list; running the backfill there just writes the marker.
- Import project bundles only from a 7.48.00 or later checkout: an older importer lists neither the imported project nor its comment series in the deployment's registries, so once the marker is there, in registry mode a project imported by an older checkout is missed whole (its `META`, personas and product documents, live or deleted) and so are its series' threads. If you must import from an older checkout, run `--unmark` first, then the backfill again after the import (docs/project-export.md).
- Run again the erasures that did not reach the deployment's projects: every erasure by email without a source created before the 7.48.00 deploy finished, or whose row does not say `deployment_projects_walked: true` (in Administration's erasure list for the first part, the job's API view, `GET /settings/erasure`, for the second). The job keeps only the address's hash, so an admin submits the erasure again, with its address and legal basis. One handed over while the release deploys walks the deployment's projects when it resumes (a cursor of 7.43.00 to 7.47.00 names neither `deployment` nor `deployment_done`) and says so on its row; one already past its `workspace_projects` phase when the new code takes it over finishes with `deployment_projects_walked: false`, and is run again the same way.
- Rollback: rolling the release back (every stack, from the earlier release's checkout) deletes the marker (VocCoreStack's custom resource is deleted), so the next upgrade's erasures fall back to their own Scans until the backfill runs again: an earlier release writes no registry row, and a marker kept across a rollback and the next upgrade would vouch for registries that miss what was made in between. Deploying one stack alone is routine (docs/deployment.md, "Deploy Individual Stacks"), and an older VocApiStack deployed alone does not delete it: before that, delete it yourself (`.venv/bin/python scripts/projects/backfill_review_registries.py --unmark`, as docs/deployment.md says there); a check of the registries against the live projects and the reset's move into VocApiStack are 3g-d2's; an erasure also ignores a marker that names no release of 7.48.0 or later. An earlier release ignores the registry rows (they stay, harmless) and goes back to its lineage Scan; tombstones under `AUDIT#tombstone#deployment_projects` and the job rows' new fields stay. An erasure handed over mid-way to an earlier release carries this release's cursor, which the earlier one may fail on (the lineage pass's) or step past (the deployment's projects), so roll back when no erasure is running, and run again one that failed (every step is idempotent).

## [7.47.00] - 2026-11-16

Engineering agents are autonomous agents: an agent with engineering settings runs an engineering flow on a repository connection, from its triggers or Run now, as the administrator who enabled it. With `-c engineeringAgents=true` every deployment gets two ready-made ones, **Bug fixer** and **Feature builder**, seeded disabled with their workflows built from the engineering flow templates and a $50 starting monthly budget; a labelled GitHub issue starts one run, ever, whose draft pull request says `Fixes #N`. The agents and their runs are still the deployment's (multi-workspace phase 3g3): their runs take only the deployment's own feedback ([docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#engineering-agents)).

### Added

- An agent's `engineering` settings, `{connection, language, feedback_type}` (`voc-datalake/lambda/shared/agents_store.py`): a stored repository connection, a toolchain with an agent image (`python`, `node`, `rust`, `java`) and what it works on, `bug` or `feature_request`. Refused with 400 while the module is off, for a connection that is not stored (or removed) and a language without an image; an engineering agent runs an engineering flow only and an agents workflow's agent none (400). Its instructions are at most 300 characters (the trusted start of its run's goal, 500 at most, refused never cut), its runs per day 0-5 (default 1). Enabling it (`POST /agents/{id}/enable`, or a save with `enabled`) needs the connection, the language and its flow's `budget.monthly_usd` (400 "set the agent up first"), and records who it runs as from then (`owner_sub`, `owner_username`: the enabling administrator; `owner_sub` is never set by hand on one). Engineering agents are listed and read by administrators acting for themselves only (404 for anyone else), and only where the module is on.

Both disabled, scope all reviews, one run a day, their flows (editable in the Workflows tab) with `budget.monthly_usd` 50 (`SEEDED_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD`, the owner's starting budget, which their Set up shows and an administrator may change); they still need a connection and a language before they can be enabled.
- The `github_issue` trigger (`voc-datalake/lambda/agents/heartbeat/issues.py`): `{label (default voc-agent, at most 50), trusted_authors, lookback_days 1-30 (default 7)}`, an engineering agent's with a GitHub connection, at most one. The heartbeat reads the deployment's `CHANNEL#issue` partition of the channel index, items first ingested within the look-back, newest first, at most 500 a tick, and keeps an open issue of the connection's repository from the GitHub Issues connector, of the agent's kind (`dimensions.feedback_type`), in scope, carrying the label; on a private repository (a connection with `repository_private`, 7.45.00) a trusted author (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`) may stand in, or, with no label set, any issue. On a public repository the label is mandatory (400 when empty). A label added after the look-back is missed.
- One run per GitHub issue, ever: the run's start transaction puts `ISSUE_RUN#default` / `<owner/name>#<n>` create-only (which agent, run, engineering run and feedback item took it), for every agent; a start refused later keeps it (never retried), and only an administrator's Run now `{issue}` reruns an issue (taking the claim only when it is free).
- `scope.sources` for every agent: the `source_platform` ids its reviews come from, at most 20 (`item_in_scope`); refused with a `threshold` trigger, whose counters have no source.
- An engineering agent's runs (`voc-datalake/lambda/agents/heartbeat/engineering.py`, `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/engineering_agent_runs.py`): its `new_reviews` counts only in-scope reviews of its kind and its runs carry up to 50 of their ids (ids, top category and count; never text); a `threshold` with none of its kind in its window skips (`no_bug_reports`, `no_feature_requests`) and moves its baseline; a `schedule` goes ahead with what it finds. Before each start the owner is re-checked in Cognito, as a plan's approver is (`voc-datalake/lambda/agents/plan_identity.py` `is_current_admin`: still enabled, the same account, in `admins`; else `owner_not_admin`; a directory that cannot answer starts nothing); an agent whose connection or flow budget went away skips with `not_set_up`. The run row gets `kind: engineering`, `engineering_run_id`, `issue`, `prd`, `feedback_count`; the lock is held while the engineering run is live (active or waiting for a person) and freed when the heartbeat reads its `META` ended (done → completed, failed, stopped → cancelled), for a disabled agent too; a run whose engineering run was never written fails after 15 minutes.
- Run now of an engineering agent (`POST /agents/{id}/run`, an administrator acting for themselves; a delegated credential gets 403): `{issue}` (rerun an issue), `{prd: {project_id, document_id}}` (a feature agent's), or nothing (a bug agent's hunt); a feature agent needs one of the two. 409 until it is set up; the start's refusal is 409 in its words, a start known not written 503, one that may have been written 503 naming its engineering run (`run_id`). Cancelling an engineering agent's run from its page answers 409: stop it from its run monitor.
- The goal of an engineering agent's run is trusted text only: its instructions and one sentence of numbers and names ("Fix the bug reported in issue #7 of owner/name.", "Hunt the defects behind 12 bug reports in all reviews.", "Build the feature the PRD … of project … describes."), credential-shaped text redacted; never an issue's, a review's or a PRD's text.

- The broker (`voc-datalake/lambda/engineering/connectors/`): `head {connection, repository, branch, issue?}`, voc-engineering-start's operation alone (its role in the session named after its function, `identity.START_ROLE`; an agent's or the runtime's call is 403, and the start may make no other operation), read only: the branch's head commit and the issue's state (`GitHubHost`/`GitLabHost` `head_commit`, `issue_state`; a GitHub pull request's number is no issue). The run record's `issue_number` is META's issue (its own repository's only), so the run's understander comments on that issue alone, and a draft pull request's body names it, `Fixes #N` (GitLab `Closes #N`) added when the agent's body does not reference `#N` (`broker.closing_body`).

No behaviour changes.

### Upgrade notes

- With `-c engineeringAgents=true`, the first admin listing of the agents after the deploy seeds Bug fixer and Feature builder, disabled, beside any agent the deployment has. To use Bug fixer: connect the repository with the deployment's GitHub App (Agents → Connections, 7.45.00; an App-created connection carries `repository_private`, so a private repository may also take a trusted author's issue, while a public one, or a connection saved with a pasted token, needs the label), attest its CI, ingest its issues with the GitHub Issues source signed in with that App (**Sign in with** → GitHub App, in place of a fine-grained token), open Bug fixer, Set up (connection, language, the $50 budget or another), Enable; label an issue `voc-agent` (docs/autonomous-agents.md, "To enable Bug fixer"). ## [7.46.00] - 2026-11-16

The document page gets an icon toolbar beside its menus (versions, History, AI review, AI rewrite, Comments with its open count, Contents, Full width, Full screen, then Share), opens with the full width and Contents on and the comment panel closed, and shows a PR/FAQ or PRD as one document across its versions: one entry in the Documents list, opened on its latest version, with a version picker that reads any earlier one read-only and restores it as a new version. A project page's tab, document, version and full screen are now paths (`/projects/<id>/documents/<docId>/v/<n>/focus`); old `?tab=` / `?doc=` / `?view=focus` links still work ([docs/document-canvas.md](docs/document-canvas.md#the-toolbar)).

### Added

- The document page's toolbar (`frontend/src/components/DocumentCanvas/actions/DocumentToolbar.tsx`, `toolbarItems.ts`, `toolbarControls.tsx`, `useRovingToolbar.ts`), at the end of its top bar: the version picker, **History**, **AI review** (Ask personas to review), **AI rewrite** (Revise from comments), **Comments** (the open threads as a badge and in its name), **Contents**, **Full width**, **Full screen**, and **Share** (the review link) as the row's one prominent button. A WAI-ARIA `toolbar`: one Tab stop, ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (wrapping), Home and End; every icon named, with a tooltip shown on hover and on keyboard focus and given as its description; the switches `aria-pressed`; a disabled AI flow stays focusable and says why (no personas; no thread answered yet; accepted changes waiting for their save); the running flow said in a polite status. A viewer gets no Share, AI review or AI rewrite, as the menus offer them only to an editor. Below 768 px History, the AI flows, Contents and Full width move into a **⋯** menu. The toolbar and the View menu switch one state.
- The version picker (`VersionPicker.tsx`, `versionChoices.ts`): v1 … vN newest first (the History list's 25), the latest marked **Latest**, the one on screen checked (`menuitemradio`). Choosing an older version shows it read-only under a banner (`page/OlderVersion.tsx`: "Viewing v2 of 4 · read only", **Back to latest**, and for an editor **Restore**, asked first, History's restore: a new version), the page's own canvas, its unsaved draft and its comment rail kept mounted out of sight. It reads `GET /projects/{id}/documents/{document_id}/versions` (any member; the History list), when the picker opens or an older version is asked for: no route was added, nothing stored is rewritten or merged.
- The Documents list shows a PR/FAQ or PRD series once, as its latest version, counted once and selected while any of its versions is open (`pages/ProjectDetail/documentEdit.ts` `seriesHeads`, `listedIdOf`); a prototype keeps one entry per version. The series card's menu (7.44.01) acts on the version it shows, the latest: **Open** opens it, **Delete** deletes that one version (`DELETE /projects/{id}/documents/{document_id}`, as the page's own Delete does; the version before it is then the series' card), and it has no **Rename** (`documentKinds.isRenamedInPlace`). A link to an older version's own row opens the series' latest with that version under the banner, checked once per address, so a version saved by a teammate while you edit never moves your canvas.
- A click in a commented passage makes its thread the active one and opens the comment panel (`DocumentComments/CommentedDocument.tsx`); a persona review opens it to say what it filed.
- Paths for a project page (`pages/ProjectDetail/projectPaths.ts`, `useProjectPlace.ts`; the route is `projects/:id/*`): `/projects/<id>/<tab>` (`overview`, `personas`, `product`, `documents`, `decisions`, `participants`; `/projects/<id>` is the Overview), `/projects/<id>/documents/<docId>`, `…/v/<n>` (an older version; the version on the page has no `/v/`), `…/focus`. A tab, a document, a version or full screen chosen is a history entry, so Back and Forward walk them; a save, a restore or the latest loaded moves in place. The breadcrumb trail ends at the project; the assistant's page context reads the tab and the open document from the path.

### Changed

The three switches are your preferences in this browser (`voc-document-view` in localStorage, version 1, the same on every document), not the address, and only an explicit switch stores one (the toolbar's button, the View menu's entry, its shortcut); before this release they lived only as long as the page, so there is no stored choice to migrate and everyone starts on the new defaults. A comment started on a selection (Comment, Ctrl/⌘+Alt+M), a link to a thread, a click in a commented passage and a persona review's result open the panel for that visit only: the stored choice stays, and another document or a reload shows it again.

In-app links use the paths (a run's document, the Decisions card's "PR/FAQ ready", a brief card's "Decide": `projectDocumentPath`, `decisionDeepLink`); the server builds none of these links (searched: emails, notifications, review-share links, the assistant's navigation chips, MCP), so nothing changed there.

## [7.45.00] - 2026-11-16

The in-app GitHub connect flow, on a GitHub App manifest (only with `-c engineeringAgents=true`). An administrator makes the deployment's own private GitHub App from Agents → Connections in two clicks, without copying a key: the browser posts the server's manifest to github.com, GitHub sends it back with a one-hour code, and the Agents API exchanges the code at once and puts the App's private key and webhook secret straight into SSM; installing the App on repositories saves each one as a connection whose credential references the App's key, stored once. A new function, `voc-engineering-app-tokens` (the broker's code under its own role), is the only one besides the broker that signs with an App's key: it reads an installation for the Agents API without ever answering a token, and gives the github_issues source's deployment-wide runs read-only Issues tokens narrowed to their repositories, which the run revokes when it ends. The github_issues webhook verifies an App's deliveries against that App's own secret. No new unauthenticated endpoint; the web app's `form-action` admits `https://github.com` alone, only with the module ([docs/autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md#a-github-app-in-two-clicks-74500)).

### Added

- Added: the Agents API's GitHub App routes (`voc-datalake/lambda/api/agents_handler.py`, `voc-datalake/lambda/engineering/connectors/github_apps.py`), the connections' gate (404 while the module is off, then an administrator acting for themselves; a delegated MCP credential gets 403), all behind Cognito on `/agents/{proxy+}`: `GET /agents/engineering/github-apps` → `{apps: [{app_id, slug, owner, owner_type, html_url, webhook, connections, created_at, created_by, version}], limit: 5}`; `POST …/github-apps/manifest` `{account: user | organization, org?}` → `{action_url, manifest, expires_at}` (a private App, no OAuth on install, `setup_on_update`, Contents, Pull requests and Issues read and write and Metadata read, named `VoC agents <hex6>`; where the github_issues webhook is deployed, its hook on `<API>/webhooks/github_issues` with the issues and issue_comment events; the return addresses on the deployment's own CloudFront domain; an organization's login checked as GitHub spells one; 409 past 5 Apps); `POST …/github-apps/conversions` `{code, state}` → 201 `{app, install_url, expires_at}` (the code exchanged with `POST https://api.github.com/app-manifests/<code>/conversions` over the broker's crypto-free transport; 409 when GitHub no longer takes it, saying the App may exist on GitHub without its key here); `POST …/github-apps/installations` `{installation_id, setup_action, state}` → `{app, account, connections, skipped}` (every installed repository saved as a connection up to the 20, its id the repository's name with `-2`… on a collision; archived, already connected, past the limit and unsaveable ones reported; 409 for another App's installation or a suspended one; `setup_action: request` refused, the state kept); `POST …/github-apps/<app_id>/install` (a new install link), `POST …/github-apps/<app_id>/check` → `{repositories, missing}`, and `DELETE …/github-apps/<app_id>` `{reason?}` (409 while a connection uses it).
- Added: single-use setup states (`CONNECTIONS#default#SETUP` / `STATE#<sha256>` in voc-agents): the raw state (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`) is handed to the browser and never stored; each row names its purpose, the administrator's subject, the account and the App, expires in 30 minutes and carries a `ttl` of a day. One conditional UpdateItem claims it; a failure before anything is stored (GitHub unreachable, rate limited, failing, or its answer lost) gives it back, and a code GitHub already spent then answers the 409; the same administrator posting it again gets the stored outcome; anything else is one uniform 400.
- Added: the deployment's GitHub Apps in SSM: `/[<prefix>-]voc/engineering/_github-app/<app_id>/key` (`{app_id, slug, private_key}`) and, with a hook, `…/webhook` (`{webhook_secret}`), SecureString, standard tier, the stack's key, never overwritten, written before the App's row (`CONNECTIONS#default` / `GITHUB_APP#<id>`), with `github_app_created` and `github_app_removed` audit rows of the connections' `LOG#` shape. GitHub's client id and secret are discarded; the key, the secrets and any token are never answered, logged or put in an error.
