## [7.44.00] - 2026-11-16

Web Reviews pages read themselves the best way by default: **Automatic** tries the signed browser, then the Amazon Bedrock web index, then AgentCore web search snippets (stored as excerpts), and each workspace learns, from its own runs only, which method reads each site; the card, the run row and the AI assistant say how a page was read and what is known.

### Added

- A Web Reviews page's `method` **`auto`** (Automatic (recommended)), the default for a new page and for one saved without a method (`lambda/shared/web_review_targets.py`; a stored `browser` or `bedrock_web_search` is kept). Per target per run (`plugins/web_reviews/ingestor/handler.py`, `cascade.py`): (a) the signed browser; when it is blocked (a bot wall, an HTTP 4xx/5xx document, a redirect to an error page such as `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`), the page did not load, or it read no review on a page that has some (its JSON-LD declares a review count, the target or the site read reviews before, or it was never read), (b) Amazon Bedrock web search with the 7.42.00 surface model and fallback and the same attribution; when that also gets nothing, (c) AgentCore Web Search (`InvokeWebSearch` of the managed tool `web-search.v1`, SigV4 for `bedrock-agentcore`, the page's title or name plus "reviews" held to its domain, only the results on the page itself read), whose snippets the `enrichment` model reads, a review kept only when its body is in one snippet (`plugins/web_reviews/ingestor/snippet_reader.py`). A redirect to another site's page ends the read. A later step is skipped, and reported, when the Lambda has too little time left for it. A run reads in three phases (the learned steps before the browser, one browser session, the steps after it).
- Every Web Reviews item carries `method_used` (`browser`, `bedrock_web_search`, `agentcore_web_search`); an AgentCore item is an excerpt: `excerpt: true`, `snippet_cut`, `snippet`, `snippet_url`, `snippet_title`, `snippet_published_date`, `query`, `site`, `source_url`, `fetched_at`. The run row gains `reads`, one entry per target: `method`, `method_used`, `reviews`, `plan` (`known`, `reprobe`, `cascade`), `known_method`, `learned_at`, `excerpt` and every step with its outcome (`readable`, `blocked` with its vendor, `no_reviews`, `error`, `skipped_time`, `not_offered`), answered by `GET /sources/status?run_status=web_reviews`. An `auto` page is reported in the run's errors only when no step read it, as one line naming every step.
- Learning which method works (`lambda/shared/web_review_methods.py`): one record per workspace and site in voc-aggregates, `WS#{ws}#WEB_REVIEWS#METHODS` / `{domain}` (`WEB_REVIEWS#METHODS` for a deployment-wide run), with the best method, when it was learned and each method's last outcome, time and counts, no review content. A best method that read the site within 30 days goes first, the cascade from the top is its fallback; a method blocked within 7 days is left out; a site whose best method is not the browser gets the browser tried again first every 14 days. Each workspace starts empty: nothing is shared or seeded. The workspace hard delete sweeps the records (`web_review_methods`, `lib/utils/workspace-delete-grants.ts`); the export lists them as not exported.
- `GET /integrations/web_reviews/methods` (any member) and `DELETE /integrations/web_reviews/methods/{domain}` ("Re-check methods": the workspace's admins, audited in `AUDIT#WS#{ws}` as `web_review_methods_cleared`; the deployment's admins without `X-Workspace-Id`), both on the request's own workspace's records; `GET /scrapers/review-methods` answers the same list for the AI assistant.
- Data sources: the Review page form's **Read with** select (Automatic (recommended), Browser only, Bedrock web index only; the Bedrock web search index source presets Bedrock web index only); the card's last-run line says how the page was read ("Browser blocked by Cloudflare → read via Bedrock web index (11 reviews)", "Known: … (learned …)", "Re-checked the browser: …") with an **Excerpts** badge, and an Automatic page shows the method its workspace learned with **Re-check methods** (administrators). In all nine languages; dev mocks for the new routes and run rows.
- The AI assistant's `list_review_site_methods` (scrapers pack): what this workspace learned of each review site. The guidance has it called before a review page is proposed, says what is recorded or that the first run will learn it, never claims a method the workspace has not recorded, and does not propose Yelp or Reddit pages (their official APIs only).
- The site eval: an `auto` method (what `auto` picks on a first run, reusing the run's signed, Bedrock web search and AgentCore rows); `official_api_only` sites (Yelp: the Yelp Fusion API; Reddit: the Reddit Data API) get that outcome from every method instead of being read; the by-site table names the vendors this run met.

### Changed

- The web_reviews ingestor role gains `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch` on `arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:aws:tool/web-search.v1` only (`lib/stacks/ingestion-roles.ts`, pinned in `lib/stacks/ingestion-web-search.test.ts`). It writes the learned records with its existing voc-aggregates grant, its workspace view refusing any other workspace's key. The integrations API role gains `dynamodb:DeleteItem` on `WEB_REVIEWS#METHODS` and `WS#{ws}#WEB_REVIEWS#METHODS` only, while the plugin is enabled (`lib/customer-data-deletes.test.ts`).
- `plugins/web_reviews/evals/sites.json` holds inputs only (each page, its subject, its documented `expect` and feeds or APIs; no vendor, baseline or evidence of a run); the eval compares with `expect` only and writes its reports only under the git-ignored `voc-datalake/web-reviews-eval/` (`--out` elsewhere is refused). The eval's AgentCore method is the ingestor's snippet step.

- Docs: docs/web-reviews.md (Methods with `auto`, Learning which method works, Blocked sites, Evaluating sites without any run's results, Cost, IAM), docs/scrapers.md, docs/plugin-architecture.md, docs/data-lake-structure.md, docs/multi-workspace.md (a 7.44.00 row, the delete's sweeps), `.kiro/steering/tech.md`, `.kiro/steering/structure.md`.

Multi-workspace, phase 3g-b: an erasure reaches a workspace's projects. An erasure by email removes the address (and a name that is the address) from the workspaces' review link audiences, comments and project owner and member fields, lists for review the product documents that hold it, and deletes the exports of each workspace it changed or where a document holds the address; an erasure that deletes a workspace's feedback, or de-identifies a board request, marks the workspace personas, research and documents that cite it, found through the project registries instead of a scan of every project. A team member or reviewer without a name is no longer named by their address in comments and links, and a walk of every workspace reaches one renamed or created while it runs. Nothing changes for the deployment's own projects: existing deployment rows wait for slice 3g-d (planned); and no workspace project exists until the switch (3h), which is no longer blocked by 3g-b (it still waits for 3g2, 3g3, 3g-d and the erasure panel's review list) ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md#the-project-plan-phase-3)).

### Changed

In each walked workspace it reads, first, every review link its link registry lists, then every project its registry lists (a deleted one too: its rows stay until its delete sweeps them) and the company persona library, by strongly consistent Query pages only, through the workspace layer, and de-identifies what holds the address (compared case-insensitively): a review link's audience loses the address (its domains stay, and a domain may still admit the person; a list audience left with no address and no domain is also revoked, by `erasure`, so the next share makes a new link); an author whose email is the address loses email and email digest (a reviewer its name too), and an author of any kind whose name is the address loses that name (a member's becomes "Team member"); a thread's `status_by`, a link's `created_by_name` and `revoked_by` and a persona research note's `author` that are the address become "Team member"; a project `META` loses `owner_email` when it is the address, and each `members` entry whose email or name is the address loses both (subs, roles and usernames stay: only the sub decides access). A page of threads, personas or documents is cut after a row when the invocation's time runs low. The comment text stays, as a board request's does, and is not searched for the person. Each row is written by one UpdateItem conditioned on every attribute read; a row changed meanwhile is read again, whole, its changes worked out again, at most three times, then the job fails (an admin reruns it: every step is idempotent). Before the write an attempt record is put (`AUDIT#tombstone#workspace_projects`, `deidentifying`), after it the outcome (`#done`, `deidentified`): never the address or a link's id. The workspace's exports are closed before its first change and deleted by the `exports` phase, as for a matched feedback item. The model that reads a Web Reviews page from the Amazon Bedrock web search index is chosen in Administration → AI models like every other AI model, with its Test button and its capacity fallback, from a list of OpenAI GPT models of its own; the deploy accepts those models' Marketplace agreements.

### Added

- Administration → AI models: a **Review pages: Bedrock web search** row (surface `web_reviews_search`, `lambda/shared/model_config.py`), listed while the `web_reviews` plugin is enabled. It picks from its own allowlist, the OpenAI GPT models of the `bedrock-mantle` Responses API: `openai.gpt-5.6-luna` (Automatic), `openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `openai.gpt-5.5`, `openai.gpt-5.4` (`WEB_SEARCH_MODELS`, in lockstep with `lib/utils/web-search-models.ts`). The GPT family is not in the Claude allowlist: `PUT /settings/model` refuses a GPT model for any other surface and for all surfaces, and a Claude model for this one (400 naming the surface's models); the pick for all surfaces, the deployment's default and the `e2e` profile never reach it. `GET /settings/model` names each surface's list (`allowlist`: `claude` or `web_search`) and carries `web_search_models` (empty while the surface is not offered).
- Its **Test**: `POST /settings/model/test` with a GPT model sends ONE Responses request to exactly that model (`"Reply with OK"`, 16 output tokens, no tool, no fallback, `lambda/shared/web_search_model_probe.py`) and answers in the Claude test's shape: Available, No access, No capacity, Throttled, Not in this region, Unavailable or Error, read from the HTTP answer.
- The web search read's capacity fallback: when the model is throttled or has no capacity (HTTP 429 / 503, or a refusal naming the model's availability), the page is read by the next model of the surface's chain, Luna → Terra → Sol → GPT-5.5 → GPT-5.4 after the resolved model, with the shared cooldown and `ModelFallback` metric (`shared/model_fallback.py` `run_with_fallback`, now with a pluggable failure test). The SigV4 Responses call is shared by the reader and the Test (`lambda/shared/mantle_responses.py`).
- The deploy accepts the GPT models' agreements while the `web_reviews` plugin is enabled: five more best-effort `BedrockModelAgreements` resources in VocCoreStack (`WebSearchModelAgreement0`-`4`, the app's region; their Marketplace offers are listed in us-west-2, us-east-1 and us-east-2), retried with `-c modelAgreementRetry` like the others.

### Changed

- Internal: `lambda/shared/run_rows.py` reads an app's newest run through the shared pager (`iter_partition`, at most 200 rows, newest first, the first match answered) instead of its own loop, and exports only its functions; the document canvas's format bar reuses `commands.ts`'s `toggleMark`; the canvas hook's `setTitle` is allowlisted as the draft-title test seam (a failed inline rename leaves that draft); `scripts/workspaces/enable_all_plugins.py` tolerates a missing docstring (pyright). `npm run audit:code` reports no finding.
- A Web Reviews page read from the Bedrock web search index uses the surface's model (its pick, else Luna), never its own: the review page and Bedrock web search index forms no longer ask for a model (the manifest's `model` field is gone), and a `model` sent to `POST /integrations/web_reviews/apps` (7.41.00 clients) is accepted and dropped like any unknown field. Every stored review's `model` is the model that read it.
- The settings role gains `bedrock-mantle:CreateInference` on the account's default mantle project, only while the plugin is enabled, and nothing of `bedrock-websearch:*`; the settings Lambda gets `WEB_SEARCH_MODELS_OFFERED`. The web_reviews ingestor role keeps its 7.41.00 grants.
- Docs: docs/web-reviews.md (Methods: the model, the fallback, the agreements), docs/deployment.md (Model agreements, the new AI models section, Model Capacity Fallback), docs/processing-pipeline.md, docs/plugin-architecture.md, `.kiro/steering/tech.md`.
- Internal: the Web Reviews handler's attribution helper is `_citation`, so the usage meter's pin (`lambda/shared/test/test_usage_meter.py`: no `_attribution` outside `shared/usage_meter.py`) holds again; it had tripped on 7.41.00's `_attribution`. A comment of `TemplateSelector.test.tsx` names the test that exists (`BedrockWebSearch.test.tsx`, the `ts_stale_refs` detector), and the reader's code-fence pattern ends on `\Z`, not `$` (`test_regex_end_anchor.py`).

### Upgrade notes

- The next deploy of VocCoreStack attempts the five GPT agreements (best effort); a refused one leaves that model's Test at No access until it is accepted (`-c modelAgreementRetry=<new value>`, or the Bedrock console). A page saved in 7.41.00 with a `model` now reads with the surface's model; pick one in Administration → AI models to keep another.

## [7.41.00] - 2026-11-15

Web Reviews reads more sites while identifying itself honestly: its browser signs every request with Web Bot Auth (Preview), keeps a browser profile between runs and recovers from a dropped connection, and a page that blocks the browser can be read from the Amazon Bedrock web search cache instead; a repeatable site eval measures which method reads which site. Data sources show each page's own last run; a project's documents open as a blank canvas in a wiki-style editor; the assistant searches the web by default.

### Added

- Project documents without a modal: **Documents → New** creates a blank custom document at once under the first free name ("Untitled document", "Untitled document 2"…, every locale), opens its page and selects the title for an inline rename (Enter saves and moves into the text, leaving the field saves, Esc restores; an empty name is refused; a rename is one PUT of `{title, expected_revision, edit_id}`). **PRD → New** and **PR/FAQ → New** are a menu: **With the wizard** (today's flow) or **Blank**, a draft pane with "Untitled PRD" / "Untitled PR/FAQ" selected in the large title, filed through the hand-written route on Enter or Start writing (a PRD's or PR/FAQ's title is its series identity, so it is set once, before filing; an existing series' name is refused).
- The document page as an editing canvas: a top bar with the menus **Document · Edit · Format · Insert · View** (WAI-ARIA menu buttons, arrow keys between menus; every item an action the editor already had, with its shortcut; Edit, Format and Insert only on an editable canvas), the save status, a comments button with the open-thread count and full screen; under it the large inline-editable title and chips (author or owner, edited, words and minutes to read, type); a wide centred sheet with a ~70ch reading column; a hideable comments panel whose thread cards show the author's initial. The menu formerly labelled "File" is **Document**.
- Web Bot Auth for Web Reviews (on by default, Preview): while a browser plugin is enabled, VocIngestionStack creates the deployment's own AgentCore browser `voc_web_reviews` (`<prefix>_voc_web_reviews`), on the public network with browser signing on; its execution role is trusted by AgentCore for this account's resources in the region and has no permissions. Every request carries the `Signature`, `Signature-Agent` and `Signature-Input` headers, which Cloudflare, HUMAN, Akamai, DataDome and F5 can verify; site owners still decide what signed agents may do. The ingestor's role may start and stop sessions on that browser only. `-c webReviewsBotAuth=false` keeps `aws.browser.v1` ([docs/web-reviews.md](docs/web-reviews.md#blocked-sites)).
- A Web Reviews browser profile (`voc_web_reviews`, on by default): each run's session starts from it and is saved into it before it stops, so review sites' cookies and local storage carry over between runs; one per deployment, public sites' state only. `-c webReviewsBrowserProfile=false` turns it off ([Sessions and profiles](docs/web-reviews.md#sessions-and-profiles)).
- A per-page reading method: `method` on a Web Reviews page (`POST /integrations/web_reviews/apps`): `browser` (the default, every existing page) or `bedrock_web_search`, which reads the page once per run from the Amazon Bedrock web search cache through an OpenAI GPT model on the Responses API (`model`, `openai.gpt-5.6-luna` by default; `external_web_access` false, the page's own site only, at most 20 reviews, summaries dropped). Every review stores its attribution in `metadata`: `method`, `model`, `site`, `source_url`, `fetched_at`, `opened_urls`, `cited_urls`; any other method is a 400. The web_reviews role gains `bedrock-mantle:CreateInference` on the default project and `bedrock-websearch:InvokeSearch` / `InvokeFetch` in the region, never `ExternalWebAccess` ([Methods](docs/web-reviews.md#methods)).
- Add a data source → A website link: **Amazon Bedrock web search index** opens the review page form with `method: "bedrock_web_search"` preset (name, URL, max reviews, model, an attribution note); saved review page cards show a **Bedrock web index** or **Browser** badge.
- A review-site eval: `voc-datalake/scripts/evals/web_reviews_sites.py` over `plugins/web_reviews/evals/sites.json` (27 review pages) reads page 1 of each by every method (the signed browser, `aws.browser.v1`, a direct fetch with an honest User-Agent that honours robots.txt, documented feeds, Bedrock web search with two models, the AgentCore Web Search API) and reports each against its expectation and the unsigned baseline; it writes nothing to the deployment ([Evaluating sites](docs/web-reviews.md#evaluating-sites)).
- `docs/deployment.md`: `webReviewsBotAuth` and `webReviewsBrowserProfile` rows.

### Changed

- The assistant's web search is on by default (the composer's globe; only where the deployment has web search): `voc-assistant-ui`'s persisted record moves to version 1, which turns it on once in a record from before (every such record stored the old default, off); a later choice of either is kept (`frontend/src/assistant/store/assistantStore.ts`).
- `POST /projects/{id}/documents` (`lambda/api/projects.py` `create_document`): a custom document may be created with empty or missing `content` (the blank canvas; before, 400 "Content is required"); a `content` that is not a string is refused (400); custom documents record `created_by_sub`. The frontend's `DocumentUpdate.content` is optional (a title-only rename).
- A Web Reviews run recovers once from a closed browser connection (a new session reads the page being read and the rest); a navigation that fails on the network or gets no answer is tried once more. Block detection names Cloudflare's hard block, AWS WAF's challenge script and Reddit's network-policy page.

### Fixed

- Data sources: each review page or app card shows its own last run after a reload (completed with N reviews, or its errors such as "blocked by Cloudflare" with a hint on what blocked means), and pages run at once each show their own run, never another page's. `POST /sources/{source}/run` keeps the body's `app_id` on the run row (a malformed one is a 400); `GET /sources/status?run_status=<source>` takes `app_id=` (that app's newest run) and `execution_id=` (that run), validated (400), and another workspace's id answers `never_run`. A run left `running` for over an hour reads "Did not finish".
- Administration → Sources → Plugins and the Data sources dialog: a plugin without a schedule (S3 import, synthetic reviews) shows "Runs on upload" / "Runs on demand — no schedule" instead of an Enabled/Disabled switch that answered 500; `PUT /sources/{source}/enable|disable` answers 400 "This plugin has no schedule" before any rule is toggled or breaker cleared.

### Upgrade notes

- The next deploy of VocIngestionStack creates the Web Reviews browser, its role and the profile; runs after it use them. Changing `webReviewsBotAuth` later replaces the browser, which holds no data.
- `bedrock_web_search` needs the account's AWS Marketplace subscription to the chosen OpenAI model (accept the offer once in the Amazon Bedrock console; the deployment never accepts one). Web Search is offered in us-east-1, us-east-2 and us-west-2. Read its acceptable-use terms in docs/web-reviews.md first.
- The assistant's web search preference turns on once for everyone (the stored preference's version 1); a later choice to turn it off is kept.

## [7.40.01] - 2026-11-15

`validate.sh` uses a big machine when it has one: with `VOC_VALIDATE_JOBS=N` (one line in that machine's shell profile) every step is a job of its own, its rebuildable caches and every step's temp files live in RAM, and the wider suites run on more workers. A laptop and CI leave it unset and run exactly as before. Measured on the 192-core build machine, on one tree, while other work kept it busy (load 80-185): the lanes 498, 527 (this release's parent's script) and 534 s (this script, unset), the pool 257 and 310 s with `VOC_VALIDATE_JOBS=32`, every run green; the pool is now bound by pytest (~250 s). Also: the ingestor assets no longer hash Hypothesis's local state, and 7.40.00's pyright and jscpd findings are fixed.

### Added

- `VOC_VALIDATE_JOBS=N` (N > 1), the pool (`scripts/validate.sh`): every selected step runs as its own job, at most N at once, the longest chain first (a step's duration in the last real run plus the heaviest chain waiting on it). The only orders the lanes kept are kept (`needs`): the vite build before the audit synth and the CDK suite, the synth before the detector tests. Same steps, commands, report table, step logs and exit code; the first failure stops the running jobs and names the step (`--keep-going`: every step whose prerequisites passed still runs, the others are `not-run`); `--pytest-first` runs pytest alone first, `--serial` turns the pool off. With the pool, CodeQL's two languages build and analyse side by side (`CODEQL_PARALLEL=1`, `scripts/codeql.sh`), the CDK suite runs on CPUs / 6 workers, 4 to 32, instead of its config's 4 (`VALIDATE_CDK_VITEST_WORKERS`) and the detector tests on CPUs / 12 pytest-xdist workers, 2 to 16 (`VALIDATE_AUDIT_TEST_WORKERS`); so the big consumers share the cores, pytest gets CPUs / 2 workers and each CodeQL language CPUs / 4 threads unless `VALIDATE_PYTEST_WORKERS` / `CODEQL_THREADS` are set. The step that stopped the run is reported FAIL with its log even when it died from a signal (the stopped jobs are `stopped`).
- `VOC_VALIDATE_RAM` (`scripts/validate-ram.sh`): with the pool and a `/dev/shm`, `.cache/codeql`, `.cache/coverage`, `.cache/audit` and `.cache/validate/tsc` move to `/dev/shm/voc-validate-<uid>/<tree>/` behind links at their old paths (the first move keeps their contents; a copy that fails leaves that cache on disk), and every step's `TMPDIR` is a folder of the run's own there (`/dev/shm/voc-validate-<uid>/t/<pid>`, in a private folder of its own, kept as short as a Mac's: see Known issue), removed at the end (write access restored first: some tests leave read-only folders) and at the next run's start when a run was killed outright. In the pool the stream suite gets the CDK suite's load timeouts (`VALIDATE_VITEST_TIMEOUT_MS`; its beforeAll crossed vitest's 10 s default twice beside every other job). Only folders this user made and no one else can open (mode 700, not links) are used; an absolute path is required; anything else keeps the caches on disk with a warning. The step logs stay on disk. After a reboot the folders are made again (a cold run); with RAM off, a link whose folder is gone becomes an empty folder and a live one is kept and named. `off` keeps the caches where they are; a dry run touches nothing. The audit's two synth steps keep the system's temp folder (`VALIDATE_DISK_TMPDIR`): see Known issue.
- `VALIDATE_DRY_RUN_CMD`: a dry run's no-op replaced by a command that sees the step in `$VALIDATE_STEP` (the pool's tests record starts and ends with it).
- The audit synth cache (`scripts/audit/py_assembly.py`) is written beside its file and renamed over it, so a reader in another process (the detector tests on xdist workers) never parses half a file.
- Tests: `scripts/validate.test.mjs` (the pool: every step once; at most N at once and more than one; the kept orders; fail fast with jobs still running (`stopped`) and with a first failure that died from a signal (FAIL); `--keep-going` with a failed prerequisite; the longest chain first; `--pytest-first`, `--serial`, 1 job, a bad value; the steps' environment exactly the old one without the pool, and sized from the cores with it (what is set by hand kept; `--pytest-first` keeps pytest's count); RAM named, never touched by a dry run; the existing tests pinned to the lanes), `scripts/validate-ram.test.mjs` (15: the move, a second run, a reboot, RAM off, mode 700, a folder others can open or a link refused and nothing made in it, a planted link in the tree refused, a relative path refused, a failed copy, a link repointed, an unwritable RAM folder, two trees of one name, a cache path that is a file; `--run-tmp` removes only dead runs' folders, read-only parts too, never a live one or behind a link, and refuses an open runs folder; `--remove`), `scripts/codeql.test.mjs` (4, a stub CLI: both languages at once with their logs in order, one failing fails the run, a failed analyse fails it even beside an earlier clean SARIF, one after the other without the setting), `scripts/audit/test_py_assembly.py` (the cache's rename).

### Fixed

- The plugin-ingestor assets, staged from `voc-datalake/`, did not exclude `.hypothesis/` (Hypothesis's gitignored local state, rewritten by every pytest run), so a local pytest run changed every ingestor's asset hash, and a CDK synth beside pytest could fail with `ENOENT: scandir .hypothesis/tmp` while walking it (seen in the pool's first run). `rootPluginAssetExcludes` excludes `.hypothesis/` at any depth (`lib/utils/lambda-asset-excludes.ts`; its tests red before).
- `lib/test-support/baseline.json` regenerated for the version bump (VocApiStack's and VocProcessingStack's template hashes; the name inventory unchanged, as in every release).
- 7.40.00's gate findings: pyright `reportOptionalMemberAccess` in `scripts/workspaces/enable_all_plugins.py` (`__doc__` may be None, as the other scripts handle it), and jscpd's three clones in its tests (Home.test.tsx's source-list reads in one helper; the workspaces rename and plugins suites share `handler_doubles` in `workspaces_api_world.py` and the members suite's ids). Behaviour unchanged; the suites pass as before.

### Known issue

- `py_layers`' verdict depends on the order the audit synth's output folder lists its templates (`py_assembly._synth` globs `*.template.json` unsorted). On the disk's order it reports nothing; on tmpfs's order, or sorted, it reports `cryptography` missing for `VocProcessingStack/AgentRuntimeAgentNodes` and `AgentRuntimeAgentPersonaPanel`, which is false: they reach `shared/prototypes.py` (through `agents/artifacts.py`), whose `cloudfront_signing` import is lazy inside `_signed_prototype_path`, a function the agents never call. Somewhere a function's reach or attachments takes another function's when the templates come in another order. Until that is fixed, the audit's synth steps keep the system's temp folder in the pool, so the result is the lanes' result. Repro: TMPDIR on a tmpfs, the audit cache removed, `python scripts/audit/py_layers.py`.
- `lambda/engineering/benchmark/test/test_runner.py::test_a_candidate_that_gives_up_fails_every_case_and_says_why` depends on the length of the host's temp folder: a case's `why` keeps the start and end of the check's output within `MAX_WHY`, that output names the case's temporary copy, and a TMPDIR of about 70 characters moves the cut so `'-104 !== -40'` reads `'…04 !== -40'`. It passes with `/tmp`, a Mac's TMPDIR and the pool's; the runner naming the copy relatively would end it.
- Once in the pool's ten runs a frontend vitest worker died with SIGSEGV while starting (every test passed; the step failed on the unhandled error). Not seen in the lanes; watch for it.

## [7.40.00] - 2026-11-15

A workspace can be renamed and, on a deployment that turns it on, deleted for good, both from Workspace settings. The hard delete no longer waits for a per-person export (owner decision): a confirmed delete removes the workspace with everything in it, its members' assistant conversations and personal memories included, and the web app says so before the admin confirms. The engineering agents' build runtimes are refused at synth until CloudFormation can size them.

### Added

- Rename a workspace: `PUT /me/workspaces/current` `{name}` (the workspaces API; `lambda/shared/workspace_rename.py`), for the workspace's admins (a member admin, or a platform admin who entered: live-checked and audited). The create's name rules (1 to 80 characters, no control character); the slug, and so every `/w/{slug}` address, stays. The audit row first (`workspace_renamed`: the actor, never a name, since an audit row is kept for good and a name may name a person), then ONE transaction: META's `name` while it is still the name read (409 "The workspace changed meanwhile: reload and try again" otherwise), the platform console's listing row moved to the new name's sort key (deleted under the old key only while the workspace is still `active`, so a delete that marked it `deleting` first wins with a 409, and the rename never revives it), and a member admin's check that they are still admin (403 otherwise). Then every member's "my workspaces" row (`USER#{sub}` / `WS#{ws}`), skipping a member removed meanwhile; the same name again repeats only this step (the repair). The workspaces API's role gains `UpdateItem` of `name` alone on `WS#*` and `USER#*` and `DeleteItem` on `WORKSPACES`. Route tables: workspace-admin only (`test_route_admin_gates.py`), and a cross-workspace case (A's rename touches A's rows only).
- Workspace settings: a **Workspace name** card (admins rename it in a dialog; everyone else reads it) and, with `-c workspaceHardDelete=true` only (`features.workspaceDelete` in `config.json`, `false` otherwise; deploy.sh reads VocApiStack's `WorkspaceDeleteAvailable` output, made only when on), a **Delete workspace** card: it lists what is deleted, says that it cannot be undone and that members' conversations and personal memories are not in the workspace's export, offers the export first, and its confirmation asks for the slug typed exactly and a reason (the delete's `legal_basis`, kept in the audit rows).
- `docs/deployment.md`: a `workspaceHardDelete` row in the deploy options.
- The AI assistant sets categories up before a new data source: before it proposes `create_scraper` or `create_app_connector` (in chat or as a plan step) it reads `list_categories`; with none configured it asks, in one message, what is being reviewed and proposes a category set (6-10 categories, each with its product, a line on what it covers and 3-5 subcategories), then asks the user to save it in the categories editor before it proposes the source (it has no tool that writes categories). `list_categories` now says when none are configured (generic default categories classify reviews until some are saved), only to a caller who sees every category (`lambda/stream/src/assistant/tools/guidance.ts`, `client/scrapers.ts`, `server/core.ts`).

### Changed

- Every plugin the deployment offers starts on in a new workspace: the creation's transaction also writes each plugin's `PLUGIN#{plugin}` / `WS#{ws}` row (`enabled_by` the creator; at most 94 plugins fit beside the creation's six rows, refused above). An admin no longer enables a plugin before its Run now or its schedule; Workspace settings → Plugins still turns one off. A scheduled run in a workspace where nothing is saved for the plugin yet (`WorkspaceCredentialsNotSet`) now ends `skipped` / `not_configured`, counted as `IngestorNotConfigured`, instead of failing the Lambda (an async retry and the `ingestor-errors` alarm on every tick); a Run now still fails, naming it. Workspaces created before: `scripts/workspaces/enable_all_plugins.py` (below).
- `-c workspaceHardDelete=true` builds the hard delete (the `voc-workspace-delete` job and the delete routes' grants) instead of failing the synth with `HARD_DELETE_REFUSED` (owner decision, 2026-11-15: the delete does not wait for the per-person export of members' conversations and personal memories). The test harness's own path to the job goes (`HARD_DELETE_TEST_SWITCH`, `withHardDeleteBuilt`, `lib/test-support/hard-delete-app.ts`): the suites and the audit synth set the context like any deployment. Off by default, as before. TENETS.md D5 and docs/multi-workspace.md ("Export and delete") say so; the cost rollup's double count of a deleting workspace's day stays a known gap (token counts only: every model is unpriced).
- `-c engineeringBuildMemoryMiB` defaults to `0` (every engineering role at AgentCore's standard 2 vCPU and 8 GB); `8192`, the build runtimes, is opt-in. CloudFormation is rolling the runtime's `ResourceConfigurations` out region by region (2026-11-15: in us-east-2's registry schema, not yet in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1 or ap-northeast-1), and the old default made a deploy with `engineeringAgents=true` and images in us-west-2 fail early validation ("Unsupported property [ResourceConfigurations]") before any change. The build runtimes' property override already uses CloudFormation's name and shape (`ResourceConfigurations: [{ MinimumMemoryInMiB }]`). aws-cdk-lib 2.277.0 (2026-11-13) has it typed, but also knows Python 3.15, which the dependency rule would move every Lambda to, so that upgrade is left for its own release.

### Fixed

- "Run now" of a review page, an app connector or a scraper inside a workspace answered "Failed to open the workspace" (500), and so would a workspace's webhook delivery: the integrations, scrapers and webhook roles' read of whether the workspace enabled the plugin (`PLUGIN#{plugin}` / `WS#{ws}`) allowed `dynamodb:Attributes` `pk` only (`PLUGIN_ROW_KEY`, lib/utils/workspace-resolution-grants.ts, since 7.14.00), and DynamoDB counts the request's key, `sk` included, so every GetItem of the row was AccessDenied. It now names `pk` and `sk`. A new whole-app test (`lib/workspaces-attribute-reads.test.ts`) holds every attribute-limited grant on voc-workspaces to both key attributes; it fails on the old grant for exactly those three roles. A workspace must still enable the plugin (Workspace settings → Plugins) before a run: 409 "Enable this plugin for the workspace first" otherwise.
- Home's setup checklist kept "Connect a feedback source" to do in a workspace whose sources are review pages or app connectors: it counted only the web scrapers (`GET /scrapers`). It now also counts the app configs of every plugin the Data sources page lists them for (`GET /integrations/{source}/apps`), under the all-app-configs query root so a save or delete refreshes it (`onboardingSteps.ts` `sourceConnected`, `useOnboardingSteps.ts`).

### Upgrade notes

- Workspaces created before 7.40.00 have only the plugins an admin enabled. To turn every plugin on in them, once, from `voc-datalake/`: `.venv/bin/python scripts/workspaces/enable_all_plugins.py --table <prefix->voc-workspaces-<account>-<region> --function <prefix->voc-workspaces-api-<account>-<region>` (a dry run that prints each plugin and workspace), then the same with `--apply` (through Workspace settings' own writer, each enable audited as `script:enable-all-plugins`). It also turns back on a plugin an admin turned off; `--workspace <id>` limits it.
- A deployment with `-c engineeringAgents=true` that relied on the old default (8192) now gets no build runtime; pass `-c engineeringBuildMemoryMiB=8192` to keep them, in a region whose CloudFormation has `ResourceConfigurations` (docs/deployment.md, the option's row).
- Turning the hard delete on is a deploy with `-c workspaceHardDelete=true` on every later deploy too (leaving it out turns it off again; a delete already requested can then still be cancelled, not resumed). The account's unreserved Lambda concurrency must stay at 100 or more with the delete job's 2 reserved (docs/deployment.md, "Reserved concurrency").

## [7.39.00] - 2026-11-15

Multi-workspace, phase 3g-a: a workspace's export holds its projects, their documents, personas, saved revisions, comment threads, jobs and list links, and the workspace's review links. Nothing changes for anyone yet: no route passes a workspace, so no workspace project exists, and an export of a workspace without one is the export it was, but for its manifest ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md#the-project-plan-phase-3)).

### Changed

- Internal: the workspace export (`voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/workspace_export/projects.py`) writes seven new entities after the company memory: `projects_documents`, `personas`, `document_versions`, `document_comments`, `review_links`, `project_jobs` and `project_lists`. The projects are found through the workspace's registry of project ids, read with each row's `deleted_at` (any mark but null reads deleted): a project deleted in the workspace is skipped and counted, and none of its rows is exported (its own partitions are never read; its review links' rows are read, to find the project they name, and dropped); the objects phase still copies any object left under its `projects/{id}/` prefix, which the per-project delete (3h) removes with it. A registry row not shaped like a project id is skipped and counted too, and one naming the persona library's reserved id is skipped. Each entity reads the registry again as it starts each project, so one deleted while the export runs is skipped from then on (`projects.deleted_during_export`, by entity). The workspace's company persona library is walked after them. Each project's partitions come from `project_partitions`: its own rows (only the listed kinds: `META`, the product context, the documents, the product documents' records), its personas, its document versions and saved revisions, its jobs in `voc-jobs` and its list links in `voc-participants`. Its comment threads are found through the series its partition lists, and the review links through the workspace's link registry, each kept only when its project is a live one. The product documents' uploads and extracted text were already among the workspace's objects.
- Internal: each new entity exports only the fields it lists (the versions, threads, links, jobs and list links), or, for a project's own rows and its personas, only the row kinds it lists, each the stored row through its classification (`voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/workspace_export/project_fields.py`): top-level attributes classified, each exported or excluded; nested maps exported after a secret-name check. A test fails on a top-level attribute in neither list among those the stored-attributes audit sees the writers store in a dict literal or an update expression, and the persona schema's fields; an attribute written another way (through a variable, or spread from a model's answer) is caught at run time instead, left out and named in the manifest (`projects.unclassified_fields`). Excluded there: credential-shaped attributes, a stored prototype URL, an unused stored prompt, index keys, a legacy migration's lease, a delete's fence and the verification fixtures' plumbing; a `META`'s `members` entries keep only their role, username, name, email, who added them and when. In every project entity, any nested key whose name looks like a secret's (a token, secret, hash, digest, signature, password, credential and the like) is left out at any depth and counted (`projects.secret_named_fields_refused`), and a job's configs lose the starter's category scope. Never exported: a review link's id (the secret its URL carries) and its key, a thread's link id (only whether it came from a link), a series' pointer to its link, a reviewer's email digest, the reviewers' daily counters, a version counter's migration lease, a job's `ttl` and status index keys, an assist job, and who marked a thread addressed. Email addresses (a project META's `owner_email` and `members` map, a link's audience, a reviewer's comments) and members' ids (an author, a link's creator, a job's starter) are the workspace's own collaboration data, needed to move it elsewhere, and are exported; the manifest says so. An erasure by email does not reach those copies yet: the plan's 3g-b makes it, and the switch (3h) waits for it.
- Internal: the manifest's `not_per_workspace` loses `projects_documents` and `personas` (`agents_workflows` stays, for slice 3g3); its new `projects` section counts the live projects, the deleted and malformed registry rows and the links skipped (their project not live, or their row already removed by its `ttl`; a link past its expiry whose row is still kept is exported, its `expires_at` saying so), names any unclassified attribute left out, and says where the product documents are; `not_exported` names the participant lists and people (not in this release's export), the assist jobs and the registries; `excluded` names what the project entities leave out. An export started by 7.38.00 or earlier and resumed past the entities finishes without the projects, and its manifest says so (`projects.exported` false, `not_exported.projects`); one resumed before them writes them.
- Internal: `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/project_tables.py` gains `REGISTRY_PROJECTION` and `registered_project` (a registry row's id, whether it is deleted and its `deleted_at`; a mark that is not a time still reads deleted), for a reader that skips deleted projects; `iter_registered_project_ids` is unchanged, so the hard delete still reaches every id. Four constants move into `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/project_keys.py`, where the export and their old homes now import them: the product context's row and the product documents' sort-key prefix (from `api/product_context.py`), a series id's shape (from the hard delete's sweeps) and an assist's job-type prefix (from `shared/assist_jobs.py`).
- Changed (IAM, VocProcessingStack): the export job's role may Query `voc-projects` only in the `PROJECT_IDS`, `PROJECT#*`, `DOCUMENT_VERSIONS#PROJECT#*`, `DCOMMENTS#*`, `DOCSHARE_IDS` and `DOCSHARE#*` partitions of any one workspace id (`WS#<one id>#…`), and `voc-jobs` and `voc-participants` only in the `WS#<one id>#PROJECT#*` partitions (`dynamodb:LeadingKeys`, no index, no write); it gains the `PROJECTS_TABLE`, `JOBS_TABLE` and `PARTICIPANTS_TABLE` environment variables. The patterns hold the role to that key shape, not to the export's own workspace: only the workspace layer's checks (every partition named from the job's own workspace) hold an export to it. Nor can IAM pin the sort key or the attributes, or tell a deleted project's partitions from a live one's: only the code keeps the export to the listed kinds and fields and skips a deleted project (TENETS.md tenet 6).
- Internal: the export's page helpers are one set in `voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/workspace_export/pages.py` (`Row`, `Page` with its counts, `only`, `sort_key`), which the feedback, memory and project entities share.
- Docs: docs/multi-workspace.md's 7.39.00 row; the project plan's 3g marks its export part done (3g-b, the erasure and the lineage marks, stays planned: an erasure by email that matches a reviewer's address or a project META's email reaches that workspace, so its exports are deleted, as a matched feedback item's already are), and 3h stays blocked until 3g-b ships, this being the first release to copy addresses an erasure cannot reach yet. TENETS.md tenet 6 and D5 name the export's project grants and what the export holds.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do: no table, index or API change. VocProcessingStack changes the export job (its code, its role's new Query grants on `voc-projects`, `voc-jobs` and `voc-participants`, and three environment variables) and its functions' `APP_VERSION`; VocApiStack changes its functions' `APP_VERSION`, and VocApiStack, VocCoreStack and VocProcessingStack give every function whose bundle holds `lambda/shared/` new code (`shared/project_tables.py` changes); VocWebSearchStack synthesizes the same template as the release before, and so does VocIngestionStack unless inbound email is configured (then only its intake function's `APP_VERSION`). An earlier release cannot read the new phases: an export whose hand-over names one when it is deployed again fails there (the job `failed`, the upload aborted, the lock released, the starter notified), so roll back when no export is running, or export again after.

## [7.38.00] - 2026-11-15

Multi-workspace, phase 3f: the product-doc extractor can take a product document uploaded inside a workspace and extract it there. Nothing changes for anyone yet: no route passes a workspace, so no such upload exists, and the deployment's uploads are extracted exactly as before; the extractor's role may reach fewer rows of `voc-projects` than it could ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md#the-project-plan-phase-3)).

### Changed

- Internal: the product-doc extractor (`voc-datalake/lambda/product_doc_extractor/handler.py`) takes a workspace's upload, `ws/{ws}/projects/{id}/product_docs/raw/{doc}.{ext}`, only when the key matches that form whole (one workspace id; a project and a document id with no `.`, `/`, `%` or `#`; one of the six upload extensions); another object under `ws/` is ignored, and a key that names `product_docs/raw/` without matching is refused. Before it writes anything it reads the project id's claim (`PROJECT_ID#{id}` / `CLAIM`, strongly consistent, its workspace id only) and the workspace's status: it goes on only when the claim names the key's workspace and the workspace is active, and refuses otherwise (a missing, malformed or other workspace's claim, a workspace being deleted, a read that fails), with nothing written and one log line that carries the error type alone. It then writes only that workspace's keys: the record `WS#{ws}#PROJECT#{id}` / `PRODUCT_DOC#{doc}` and the text `ws/{ws}/projects/{id}/product_docs/extracted/{doc}.txt`.
- Internal: three more checks hold in a workspace, each refusing with nothing more written: the record's `s3_raw_key` must be the event's key; the `extracting` write must land (any failure stops the extraction, not only a refused condition); and the workspace's status is read again just before the text is put, so a workspace whose delete began meanwhile gets no text under its prefix. A refusal's log line is written after the record's log context is cleared.
- Internal: an image uploaded in a workspace is marked `failed` there with its own reason ("Images can't be described in a workspace yet"), and nothing else is written or read, while the model picks it would be described with are the deployment's (`SETTINGS#model`, not per workspace yet); it is never left `pending` for the stall check to advise an upload that cannot help. A text upload reads nothing else. Before the switch (3h) lets a workspace upload, either the picks move or the upload route refuses an image in a workspace (docs/multi-workspace.md, 3f).
- Internal: `voc-datalake/schemas/project-keys-cases.json` holds every key the extractor spells itself, in both scopes (the upload, the text, the record and the attributes its updates name, the claim's and the status's reads, the upload extensions, and the keys it rejects); the extractor's tests and `lambda/shared/`'s read it, and shared/'s also hold the extractor's workspace-id and opaque-id expressions to `shared/workspace_ids.py` and `shared/row_ids.py`, so its spelling and shared/'s cannot drift apart. The raw-access guard counts the extractor's claim key.
- Changed (VocCoreStack): the raw data bucket notifies the extractor of objects created under `ws/` that end in `.gif`, `.jpg`, `.md`, `.png`, `.txt` or `.webp` (one rule each; S3 takes one prefix and one suffix per rule, and the whole of `ws/` would invoke it for every object a workspace writes), beside the deployment's `projects/` rule, which is unchanged.
- Changed (IAM, VocCoreStack): the extractor's role holds `voc-projects` by key only: GetItem and UpdateItem on `PROJECT#*` and one workspace's `WS#{ws}#PROJECT#*` (`dynamodb:LeadingKeys`), the UpdateItem held to the record's attributes it names (`pk`, `sk`, `status`, `error`, `s3_extracted_key`, `extracted_chars`; it held the table's reads and an UpdateItem of anything on any row before), and GetItem of a claim (`PROJECT_ID#*`) held to its key and `workspace_id`; a workspace's record is read projected to the five attributes it uses (`pk`, `sk`, `status`, `content_type`, `s3_raw_key`), and its GetItem on `WS#{ws}#PROJECT#*` is held to them (the deployment's read is the unprojected request it always sent, so `PROJECT#*` is not held to attributes); and `voc-aggregates` by key only, GetItem of the two model rows (`SETTINGS#model`, `SETTINGS#model_default`), where it held the table's reads. It gains the workspace status read on `voc-workspaces` (`META`'s `pk`, `sk` and `status` only), GetObject on `ws/{one id}/projects/*/product_docs/raw/*` and PutObject on `ws/{one id}/projects/*/product_docs/extracted/*`, and the `WORKSPACES_TABLE` environment variable. Its S3 grants are exact, in both scopes: GetObject of the uploads (it held the bucket's List and the other object reads before) and PutObject of the text (no tagging, retention or legal hold, which it held before). A failed read or write of a workspace's record logs the error's class, never its text.
- Docs: docs/multi-workspace.md's 7.38.00 row, 3f (done) and the extractor's load (its extra invocations for other `ws/` objects with an upload suffix, on the account's unreserved concurrency); 3h's refusal of an id held by both scopes no longer lists the extractor, whose key names its scope. TENETS.md tenet 6 names the extractor's grants, which IAM cannot pin to one workspace (only the code's claim check does).

### Fixed

- A product document deleted while it was being extracted no longer leaves its extracted text behind in the normal case. The text can still be left behind when the extractor fails or stops between writing it and recording it as ready (a timeout, a crash, a ready write that fails for another reason) or when its take-back delete itself fails; a failed write or delete is logged. The document's delete (`voc-datalake/lambda/api/product_context.py` `delete_doc`) deleted only the objects its record named, and the record names the text only once it is ready; it now also deletes the text by its derivable key (`product_doc_extracted_key`), and deletes the record before the objects, so an extraction that puts its text after that sweep finds the record gone when it marks it ready, and the extractor deletes that text itself (the exact version it put). The extractor's role gains DeleteObject and DeleteObjectVersion on `projects/*/product_docs/extracted/*` and `ws/{one id}/projects/*/product_docs/extracted/*` only (`voc-datalake/lib/customer-data-deletes.test.ts` names it).

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do: no table, index or API change. VocCoreStack changes the extractor (its code, its role's grants, now narrower on `voc-projects` and `voc-aggregates`, and one environment variable) and the raw data bucket's notification rules (six added); VocApiStack and VocProcessingStack change their functions' `APP_VERSION`, and every function whose bundle holds `lambda/api/product_context.py` (the projects API's among them) gets new code for the document delete (Fixed, above); VocWebSearchStack synthesizes the same template as the release before, and so does VocIngestionStack unless inbound email is configured (then only its intake function's `APP_VERSION`). A normal deploy (`npm run deploy:all`) does it.
- Rollback: no stored data changes (no workspace upload exists yet), so an earlier release deploys over it as it is; it removes the six `ws/` rules.

Series ids stay the same in every scope. In a workspace a project also lists its commented series in its own partition (`COMMENT_SERIES#{series}`) and the workspace keeps a registry of its review links (`WS#{ws}#DOCSHARE_IDS`), so the hard delete finds both by a Query.
- Internal: the comment threads (`lambda/shared/document_comments.py`), the persona review that files into them (`lambda/shared/document_review.py`), the review links (`lambda/shared/document_share.py`) and the review routes' helpers (`lambda/shared/document_review_routes.py`) take a workspace and keep every row in it, through the workspace layer; they no longer refuse one.

A project id's claim and a link's route are now one sealed type (`OutsideEntry`; a claim never expires, a route's expiry is a positive epoch second), and a transaction takes at most one (`outside=`, at `OUTSIDE_ENTRY_INDEX`, formerly `PROJECT_CLAIM_INDEX`); the project create's requests are unchanged. The registry row names its link's project and series, for the per-project delete (3h). The reviewer routes resolve a link by its id alone: a routing row sends the read to the workspace it names and nowhere else; one naming anything but a workspace id, or a workspace holding no link of that id, admits nobody.
- Internal: both readers of a review link refuse one kept in a workspace, under one name, until the switch (3h) gives them a workspace's status check: the reviewer routes (`/review/{share_id}…`) and the board pool's sign-up trigger (`lambda/auth/board_triggers.py`), which reads nothing of the workspace.

## [7.32.00] - 2026-11-15

Merge of voc-multiplayer-mut: property tests of the workspace isolation layer and its jobs, and the retention worker's paged walk made testable and bounded. What a deployment can see: a retention or erasure phase of more than a million rows now hands over once per million rows even with time left, and a run stops (fails, audited) past about 500 million rows scanned; a store that answers a page with the cursor it was read from stops the run too, a safety stop DynamoDB never triggers ([docs/mutation-notes-mut-voc-mp.md](docs/mutation-notes-mut-voc-mp.md), [docs/mutation-notes-testable-voc-mp.md](docs/mutation-notes-testable-voc-mp.md)).

### Changed

- The retention worker (`voc-datalake/lambda/jobs/retention/handler.py`) reads at most `MAX_PAGES` (10,000) pages per phase in one invocation, and each raw-data prefix the same, then hands over at the next page's cursor exactly as when its time runs low. For a store that pages, what is read and deleted, and in which order, is unchanged; a phase of more than a million rows hands over once per million rows even with time left. With the existing hand-over limit a run now stops (fails, audited) past about 500 million rows scanned.
- A page whose `LastEvaluatedKey` is the cursor it was read from stops the run before it is handled (`CursorStuck`): the run fails and is audited ("Run failed (CursorStuck)"), an erasure job's row reads failed and its erasure locks are released (a workspace's export lock goes stale after an hour, as on any failed run), and only the phase is logged (a cursor is a row key and may name a person). DynamoDB always moves past its start key, so a deployment never meets it.
- Internal: the walk's clock is injected (`Walk.time_left`, the Lambda's own `_lambda_clock` in production); two statements with no effect are removed (`_finish`'s pop of `_progress`, a redundant check before `job_scope` in `handle_event`).
- Internal: property tests (Hypothesis, `hypothesis==6.135.0` pinned in `voc-datalake/requirements-dev.txt`, `.hypothesis/` git-ignored) of the workspace key builders and scope, the table guard, request resolution, membership rules, workspace ids and credential names, message routing, the erasure and export job rows and export objects, the project-id claim and the erasure worker, each checked against a model of its documented rules; the mutation runs in the two notes above.
- Internal: two properties follow voc-multiplayer's newer code: the batch writer's refusal names `WorkspaceTable.batch_delete` (7.28.00), and an erasure's hold on the export lock leaves a workspace delete's lock alone and, in a workspace that is not active, takes only a lock row that exists (both branches generated); a new property pins that only its own condition's refusal is kept quiet (a throttle or an internal error is raised).

## [7.31.00] - 2026-11-15

Multi-workspace, phase 3d: a team's participant lists and people can be kept inside a workspace, and persona copies stay inside one. Two fixes to participants (an erasure that failed partway can be run again; an add racing an erasure fails); everything else is internal ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md#the-project-plan-phase-3)).

### Fixed

- A participant's erasure (`DELETE /participants/people/{id}`) that failed partway can now be run again. The person and their email guard were deleted in one batch, so a batch that removed the person but not the guard left the address guarding an erased id: a retry answered "Person not found", and the address could never be added again (adding it returned the erased id). The guard now goes first (only while it still names the erased person, so an address added again meanwhile keeps its new person's guard) and the person's own row last, on its own, so a retry finds the person and finishes. A retry also keeps the first tombstone as it was (put only if new), and the erasure's `AUDIT#delete` row now has a fixed key per person (`participant#{sha256 of the person id}`, put only if absent) written on every attempt: an erasure started on this release has exactly one record (one finished before it keeps its earlier, time-keyed row), and an erasure whose record cannot be written fails (and is retried) instead of finishing without one.
- Adding a person to a list (`POST /participants/lists/{id}/members`, a new person's lists, a board request's promote) now writes the member row and its mirror in one transaction that checks the person still exists: an add racing that person's erasure answers "Person not found" instead of leaving the erased id in the list, and an erasure reads the person's lists again once their row is gone, removing a membership an add committed meanwhile. The deployment's requests change: an add is one TransactWriteItems of the same two rows plus that check instead of two puts (sent up to three times when a concurrent write cancels it), and an erasure makes one more Query of the person's partition at its end.

### Changed

- Internal: the keys of `voc-participants`' people and lists are built in one place, `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/participants_keys.py`: a person `PERSON#{id}`, its address guard `EMAIL#{sha256}`, a list `LIST#{id}` and its members, the `gsi1` partitions `LISTS` and `PEOPLE`, and a project's links in `PROJECT#{id}`. Without a workspace each is exactly the key stored today; inside one it is `WS#{ws}#…`.
- Internal: the people and lists stores (`lambda/shared/participants_store.py`, `participants_lists.py`, `participants_intake.py`) and a person's erasure (`participants_erasure.py`) take a workspace and keep every row in it, through the workspace layer (`lambda/shared/participants_tables.py`), which refuses any key outside it before DynamoDB. In a workspace each new list is first listed in the workspace's index `WS#{ws}#PARTICIPANTS`, and each new person and address guard in the same transaction that writes them; a deleted list or person stays listed there (an opaque id) for the hard delete, and an erased person's address guard leaves it only while no guard of that address is back; an erasure's tombstone is the workspace's (`AUDIT#tombstone#participant` / `{ws}#{hash}`) and its delete record names the workspace beside the person id.
- Internal: the asks, their recipients, the tokens and the send counters are not per workspace yet. Of their stores (`lambda/shared/participants_asks.py`, and `participants_store.py` `remember_token`), `create_ask`, `asks_of_person` and `remember_token` (so no token is minted in one) take a workspace and refuse it; the others (`recipient_rows`, `resolve_token`, `mark_responded`, `sent_today` and the rest) take none yet and reach the deployment's rows only. An erasure of a workspace person holding asks or tokens is refused too. The public unsubscribe reads the workspace its stored token names, the deployment's when it names none (every token today).
- Internal: the engagement settings (who may be added) stay the deployment's: `upsert_person`, and so a participants intake, refuses a new person in a workspace (an existing one of that workspace is still found).
- Internal: the engagement API's brand name (`lambda/shared/engagement_config.py` `brand_name`) reads a workspace's own brand row when given one. The project access check of the participants routes (`lambda/shared/engagement_identity.py`) takes a workspace and refuses it, as the project gate still does. The voting sessions' helpers (`lambda/api/ballots_handler.py`) take one and refuse it themselves, before any table is opened: the ballots' own rows (`PRIORITIZATION`, `VOTING_SESSION`) stay the deployment's, whatever the gate decides.
- Internal: the query and single-item adapters are shared: `lambda/shared/ingest_tables.py` `ScopedUpdates` now has boto3's `get_item`, `put_item` and `delete_item` too, and `lambda/shared/scoped_query.py` `iter_partition` pages one partition on either path for the project stores and the participants stores.
- Internal: a persona copy (`lambda/shared/persona_copy.py`) and the promote into the company persona library (`lambda/shared/persona_copy_routes.py` `promote`, which checks the admin itself, and refuses a workspace until a workspace's admin decides it) take a workspace: a copy names one scope for its source and target (two are refused before any read), its rows are that scope's, and its avatar objects are under `ws/{ws}/avatars/` in a workspace (the deployment's stay under `avatars/`).
- Internal: a workspace's hard delete (still refused at synth, 7.28.00) also sweeps the workspace's company persona library (`WS#{ws}#PROJECT#company_personas`, after its registered projects; its verify pass checks it too), and gains a `participants` sweep: every list, person and address-guard partition the workspace's index names, deleted in full, then the index last, every read of keys alone. Its role's grant (`lib/stacks/workspace-delete-worker.ts`): Query and BatchWriteItem on `voc-participants`' `WS#{one id}#PARTICIPANTS`, `#LIST#*`, `#PERSON#*` and `#EMAIL#*` only, each Query for the key attributes alone.
- Internal: the raw-access guard (`lambda/shared/test/test_ws_raw_access.py`) counts `LIST#`, `PERSON#`, `EMAIL#`, `LISTS` and `PEOPLE` as keys that name no workspace (only `participants_keys.py` spells them), and a literal `workspace=None` passed to any of the stores above.
- Internal: a known gap is written down in TENETS.md D5: an erasure by email does not reach voc-participants (a participant is erased by its id); the project plan's new 3g2, before the switch, closes it.
- No route, job or assistant tool passes a workspace yet: every list, person, ask, unsubscribe, persona copy and promote works as before, with the same requests, but for the erasure and the list add (Fixed, above).

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do: no table, index, API or deployed IAM change (the hard delete's role is not built). VocApiStack and VocProcessingStack change only their functions' `APP_VERSION`; VocCoreStack and VocWebSearchStack synthesize the same templates as 7.30.00, and so does VocIngestionStack unless inbound email is configured (then only its intake function's `APP_VERSION`). Every function built from `lambda/` gets new code (the shared modules change). A normal deploy (`npm run deploy:all`) does it.
- Rollback: no stored data changes (no workspace writes a person or a list yet), so an earlier release deploys over it as it is.
- The erasure fix does not repair an address guard that an earlier release's failed erasure left behind: such an address still resolves to the erased person's id, and adding it again answers with that id. An `EMAIL#…` / `PERSON` row in voc-participants whose `person_id` has no `PERSON#{id}` / `META` row is one; deleting that row by hand frees the address (it holds the address's hash and the id, nothing else).
- A correction to 7.30.00's upgrade note: the account's concurrency quota it refers to is stated in [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#reserved-concurrency-of-the-mcp-endpoint--c-mcpreservedconcurrency), not in tech.md.

## [7.30.00] - 2026-11-15

Multi-workspace, cost per workspace (slice B): the voc-multiplayer-b track's daily cost estimate per workspace merged, for the platform console ([docs/multi-workspace.md](docs/multi-workspace.md)). Every model is unpriced for now, so tokens are counted and every estimate with calls in it is `null` until a deployer fills in the price list.

A day is written only when every query completed under the result cap; a rerun overwrites it. A workspace that is not active gets no row (its calls go to the deployment's `deleted_workspaces`). IAM lets it read any line those Lambdas logged; only the code, which sends one fixed query and keeps the counts of the `bedrock_usage` lines, holds it to numbers and ids (TENETS tenet 6). The workspaces API may Query the three cost partitions of voc-aggregates and is told `AGGREGATES_TABLE`.
