Autonomous engineering agents: a person's actions on an engineering run's board, from the run monitor's Board tab or the Agents API; the AI assistant answers what an engineering run's agents are doing; an alarm on the workspace's denied reads; and two fixes to the board's claim and the supervisor's re-post. Merged from the voc-autonomous-c branch. Off by default.

### Added

- A person's board actions on an engineering run (`POST /agents/engineering/<run_id>/board/tasks`, `…/board/tasks/<task_id>/<action>` with `priority`, `block`, `take`, `move` and `release`): administrators acting for themselves, through the Agents API only (no MCP tool). Each is the board store's own conditional write with a history row naming `human:<subject>`, published as the board's `task.*` event from the API's source with `from.kind` human. Taking a task holds it with no expiry, so its agent can move it no more and the supervisor leaves it alone; the person moves it on like any holder, or gives it back (`release`): open again at its next attempt, as a re-post, for the run coordinator to launch a new agent on. Blocking ends it as needing a person, with their reason. Never the coordinate task.
- The run monitor's Board tab gets an administrator's controls: post a task; take, take over, block, set priority, move and give back ("Give back to the agents") a task, in the nine locales and the dev mock.
- The AI assistant's `get_engineering_run {run_id?, agent?}` answers "what is agent X doing" on an engineering run, for administrators and read only: the run and each agent's status, task, step, why it looks stuck and its recent tool calls, live agents first, the run on screen by default (page context `engineeringRunId`). It reads the run monitor's existing routes with the administrator's own sign-in, and the agents' words reach the model as data. No API change and no MCP tool.
- The `engineering-denied-reads` alarm (alerting, only with `-c engineeringAgents=true`): the `EngineeringWorkspaceDeniedReads` of the workspace's three readers summed over 5 minutes, above 20 (docs/deployment.md).

### Changed

- The bus takes `task.*` from the API's own source only with `from.kind` human (a person's board actions), and the board's source proves `system` only (`FROM_KINDS`).
- The Agents API's role gets `dynamodb:PutItem` and `dynamodb:UpdateItem` on the engineering table only for keys whose leading key is a run's partition (`WS#default#RUN#` and a 26-character run id), never `DeleteItem`. IAM bounds it by partition only: the role can write every item of a run (META's every attribute, the TASK#, SPEC#, TASKLOG# and RUNLOG# rows, the agents' AGENT# session rows, the MSG# and INBOX# rows), and only the code keeps it to the board store's conditional writes (the task row, its SPEC# marker, its TASKLOG# row and META's `task_count`); `dynamodb:Attributes` cannot narrow it per row. Routing a person's actions through the board function, and dropping this grant, is the follow-up (docs/autonomous-engineering.md, "The board").
- Ending another person's hold, by a take or a block, needs `over: true` (the run monitor asks first), and the write holds the holder it read; an agent's signal to a task a person holds answers 409; a person's move to `needs_human` answers 400 (block it, with a reason).
- A person's board action publishes its event only when it changed the task (`updated_op` on the task row); a no-op publishes nothing, and an equal post re-sends its event only while that post is still the task's last change. A bus that cannot be reached after a board write is a `PublishError` from `EventBridgePublisher`, answered 503 "the board changed but its event was not published: retry".
- The supervisor reads a task ended with no holder (a person's block) as ended (`Lease(agent_id='', final_state=…)`), never as a lost lease it would continue in a new MicroVM.
- A plan's think step in the agents pack (`plan_contract.json` `admin_read_packs` gains `agents`) runs with the approver's admin rights only after the conductor's Cognito re-check, as in scrapers and settings.
- The assistant's create card for an engineering flow names the 409 a deployment without the engineering module answers.

### Fixed

- An agent's post equal to a task still under way publishes its event again only when the post is that task's last change and was this caller's own, so a person's post (or another agent's) is never re-published as the board's on another's behalf.
- An agent still booting whose open task a person blocked is ended on the supervisor's next tick, its MicroVM with it, instead of being left to boot and then refused its claim.
- The board's claim respects the launch recorded on a task: while a launch is recorded at the task's attempt, only that launch's agent claims it, and an agent launched for an older attempt (the task re-posted or given back since) is refused, in the write's own condition too (409). A task with no launch recorded at its attempt is still claimed by any agent of its role, the holder's repeated claim is still answered as it is, and the coordinate task keeps its own rule.
- The supervisor never re-publishes another sender's change as its own: a re-post stamps `updated_op` `repost`, and the board's `repost_task` publishes `task.posted` when it wrote the re-post, or when the store answers it as already done and the task's last change is still the supervisor's own re-post at that attempt (a retry after a lost event: the same event id, a redelivery; `BoardStore.repost_change`). A task open at the next attempt by a person's release (published as that person) or by another actor's re-post publishes nothing, on the supervisor's end of a session whose task moved on too.

### Upgrade notes

- A task row written before this release has no `updated_op`, so a person's retry of a change made before the upgrade publishes nothing (the change and its history row stay).
- A re-post written before this release has no `updated_op` `repost`, so the supervisor's retry of it after the upgrade publishes nothing (the task stays open at its next attempt).
- An agents think step in a plan now fails when Cognito cannot be reached (the re-check before it reads the agents pack), as a scrapers or settings one does.
- An agent launched for a task before this release and re-posted since can no longer claim that task at its new attempt; the coordinator's next launch numbers a new agent for it.

## [6.17.00] - 2026-11-13 (voc-autonomous)

Autonomous engineering agents: the benchmark harness, its first fixtures and the benchmark gate for skill versions. Nothing invokes them yet (the coach that proposes versions and runs the benchmark is planned); off by default.

### Added

- `voc-bench/1` benchmark cases (`voc-datalake/lambda/engineering/benchmark/cases.py`): a `case.json` per case directory (its id, which is the directory's name; its kind, `bug`, `review` or `feature`; a title; the task an agent is given; its fixture directory; its check). A bug's or a feature's check is an argv starting with `python3` or `node`, a directory of the repository to run it in, a timeout of 1-600 s, the paths a patch may not touch and, optionally, the only paths it may change (`allows`; every shipped case names them), both compared case aside; a review's is the findings it expects (a file, a line range, a short rule id) and how many others it may report. The loader checks every field and bounds the record (64 KB), every text, the fixture (400 files, 2 MB, 256 KB a file) and a suite (100 cases); it refuses a path with `..`, an absolute path, a `.git` path, any link in the case, and anything in a fixture but files and directories.
- Four fixture cases, fictional and MIT licensed, in `voc-datalake/engineering-benchmark/`: a Python bug with a failing unittest (`slug-cut-bug`), a Node feature with acceptance tests run by `node --test` with no dependencies (`duration-hours-feature`), a review with three known findings (`pagination-review`), and a monorepo with a Python and a Node package whose bug is in the Node package and whose Python package is protected (`monorepo-units-bug`). Each bug and feature case ships its known fix, which only the tests read.
- The benchmark runner (`benchmark/runner.py`): a candidate's `solve(case_view)` returns an `Attempt` (a unified diff, or a review's findings, with input and output tokens, cost and seconds) from its own copy of the fixture. A patch over 256 KB, or naming a path outside the repository, in `.git`, protected or outside the case's `allows`, or making a link, a submodule or a binary, is refused; the rest is checked with `git apply --check`, then applied to a fresh copy made a git repository (its git directory outside the working tree, hooks and the system and global git config off), and the tree is walked again. The check runs without a shell, its tool by absolute path (a Python check with `-I -P`, so the repository is not on `sys.path` at its start and a patch's `unittest.py` shadows nothing), with no credentials and no proxy in its environment (built from nothing: only its tools' directories on PATH, a temporary HOME and TMPDIR), and its process group killed at the timeout (a child that calls `setsid` escapes it); it passes on exit 0. It is not a sandbox: the check's network and file system are open, and the benchmark assumes an honest candidate (the code under test can still patch its test framework); a connection's cases will run in the runtime's MicroVMs. A failed check keeps the end of its scrubbed output, without NUL or other control characters (newlines and tabs kept); a patch header naming a quoted path (which git would unquote) is refused; a patch holding a line separator other than a newline (which Python would split on and git would not) is refused; and whatever a candidate's `solve` raises (a `sys.exit` included) or returns that is not an `Attempt`, a malformed attempt, or the machine's own failure while checking one, fails that case alone. A review passes when every expected finding is reported in its file, within its line range, with its rule, and the other findings stay within the case's bound. Each case gives a `CaseResult` (passed, why, tokens, cost, seconds); a candidate's run of a suite a `Scorecard` (pass rate, results, total cost and time).
- The benchmark gate (`benchmark/gate.py`): `decide(baseline, candidate, failure_case=None)` refuses two scorecards that did not run the same case ids, and passes only when none that passed in the baseline fails in the candidate and, when a failure's case is named, the candidate passes it and the baseline did not. Each reason is a sentence naming its case; past 12 regressions the rest share one line naming them, so a verdict always fits its record, whatever its checks printed. The `Verdict` carries the failure's case it checked, and `benchmark_run(baseline, candidate, verdict)` takes it from there, so a record never claims a gain the gate did not check.
- `SkillStore.record_benchmark`: an administrator records a proposed version's benchmark (`BenchmarkRun`: the pass rates before and after, the case ids, the verdict and its reasons, the failure's case; with when and who ran it) on its `VER#` row, once, with `benchmark_gate` (passed with a gain on a named failure's case) beside it: the write is conditioned on the row having none, in one transaction with a create-only `LOG#<version>#benchmarked` row, so a second record is refused (D1) and a failed or mis-recorded benchmark makes that version final (never accepted; the coach cannot propose again for the same run and failure kind, so a new proposal comes from a new failure in another run, or an administrator writes the fix as their own version, which needs no benchmark); the failure's case is the one the administrator who records it names, and nothing ties it to the version's own failure yet (that comes with the coach, whose proposal will store the expected case id for `record_benchmark` to check); the record is stored as UTF-8 JSON and its 40 KB bound measured the same way; it is refused when the row would pass its 256 KB; an agent or another person is refused (403). `SkillVersion.benchmark_run` reads it back, and is authoritative once present: `SkillVersion.trusted_rates` gives its pass rates, else the proposal's `benchmark_before`/`benchmark_after`, which are only the proposer's claim. Recording one announces nothing.

### Changed

- `SkillStore.accept_version` refuses a version an agent (the coach) proposed until its recorded benchmark passed with a gain on a named failure's case (409: it has no recorded benchmark, its benchmark passed without naming a failure's case, or it failed its benchmark), checked before the acceptance and again as its transaction's condition (`benchmark_gate`, the same test). A version a person wrote is accepted as before, measured or not.
- docs/autonomous-engineering.md: Evaluation describes what is built and what is still planned (the coach that proposes, real agents as candidates, published results, a connection's fixtures from its failures); the skills section describes the benchmark gate on acceptance; the phase table's rows 0 and 3 say the harness, its fixtures and the gate are built.

### Upgrade notes

- No stored version is changed. A coach's version proposed before this release has no recorded benchmark, so it can no longer be accepted until one is recorded on it; nothing writes coach versions yet.

Autonomous engineering agents: the run's start launches its coordinator and a person's Resume replaces one that failed, a run's status changes record who made them, the run monitor gains its Reports panel, and the AI assistant drafts engineering flows. ### Added

The coordinate task records that coordinator, and only it claims the task. A retried start launches it only when it has no session yet; a run without its connection, commit or language starts without one. A start whose coordinator does not launch (refused, or its MicroVM did not start) sends the run to a person (the `coordinator` decision point) and raises the failure, never leaving the run active with no coordinator; the person's Resume launches it.
- A whole-run Resume makes sure the run has a coordinator, as its start does: one whose session failed (it kept crashing, which sent the run to a person) is replaced, the coordinate task re-posted at its attempt (written, never published as `task.posted`) and a new `coordinator-<n>` recorded at the next by `BoardStore.launch_coordinator` (the runtime's only, never a board op) with the person as the actor of both history rows (`BoardStore.repost` takes an `actor`, `supervisor` by default; nobody named is `unattributed`, as on the run's own history). The supervisor ends a crashed coordinator's session as failed before it sends the run to a person, so a Resume in between still replaces it, and if sending it to a person fails, the next tick asks again for an active run whose newest coordinator failed and is still the coordinate task's. A coordinator that is live, held, or ended by a person's Shut down or Stop now is left alone (the run stays active until a person ends or resumes it); a board refusal (the agent cap, a racing Resume) is logged and the Resume still answered.
- D4 for a run's status: its start, its end, a decision point and a person's Resume each write a `RUNLOG#<at>#<status>#<hex>` row (status, actor, reason, time; create-only, never written over) in the same transaction as META's change, retried when another write of META races it. `start_run`, `end_run` and `signal` take an optional `actor` (`unattributed` when missing; `supervisor` for its own decision points; a start's or a Resume's whose coordinator did not launch names that start's or Resume's actor), and the run monitor's signals now send the signed-in person.
- The run monitor's **Reports** panel: a run's commit, PR and goal reports by level, goal first, each version's Markdown (rendered as Markdown only) with a version picker; it follows the latest version while the run is under way, and a version counted but never written says so.
- The AI assistant drafts engineering flows (`voc-workflow/2`) with its workflow tools behind its approval card; the web app creates a new one only where the engineering module is deployed (`features.engineering`), and changes one already saved anywhere.
- The `EngineeringWorkspaceDeniedReads` metric: each workspace read S3 denied and the reader took as missing (the report builder, the Agents API, the board's `knowledge`), flushed by the board and report handlers.

### Changed

- A replaced run coordinator is refused every board op (403 "the run has another coordinator now"): each coordinator op checks the caller is the coordinate task's recorded coordinator at its attempt, and the task's claim repeats the check in its own write.
- The coordinator's launch from the runtime follows the board's launch rules: a first start whose coordinator cannot be launched (no skill for the role, no MicroVM image for the language in this deployment) is refused before anything is written, and a Resume checks the same before it re-posts or numbers one; a repeat is answered from its session, and one while another launch still starts refuses a start (`SessionBusy`: ask again, the run is written) and is logged on a Resume; a Resume whose new coordinator is refused or whose MicroVM fails to start logs it and sends the run back to a person, as a start does; a bad request or another task's session clears the coordinate task's record with a `launch_refused` history row, so the next start or Resume numbers a new coordinator.

- The run monitor's signals re-read only what they change, not the reports.

The web app offers Save as on an engineering flow only where `features.engineering` is true, and the assistant's duplicate card answers that 409 with a plain sentence.
- An approved knowledge pack whose stored `pack.json` is not readable JSON is `PackUnavailable` (kind `unavailable`), which the board's `knowledge` answers 503 (try again) instead of 400.

### Fixed

- A running agent whose new MicroVM never starts counts each failed start as a crash, so it is escalated (its task re-posted, or a coordinator's run sent to a person) instead of retried forever.
- Gradle runs without its daemon in the Java image (`GRADLE_OPTS=-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false`), whose loopback the dependency step's code firewall rejects; every variable a toolchain image sets now reaches repository code (the runner had dropped `GRADLE_OPTS` and the Rust image's `CARGO_INCREMENTAL`).
- A session that stops without its finish says why in its task's last progress report before the task goes to a person. A run coordinator's stop without finish is a crash instead (the supervisor continues it, then sends the run to a person, whose Resume replaces it), never its coordinate task sent to a person, which left the run active with nobody planning it.
- A launch whose MicroVM failed to start runs its hold out (0) instead of removing it, so no key-only `AGENT#` row is left for the report builder to read as an agent with no role, and a retry launches at once; the hold is let go even when ending the MicroVM fails.

### Upgrade notes

- With `-c engineeringAgents=true`: a run's META gains `language` and starts `agent_count` at 1, and its coordinate task records `coordinator-1`; a run started before this release has neither, so its coordinator is not launched by a Resume and its agents number from 1 as before. Reads stay bounded: a scope holds at most 200 live and 500 stored memories per connection (a person's per person and connection) and a memory at most 21 confirmation rows. - The run's workspace (`voc-datalake/lambda/engineering/workspace/`): the key layout `ws/<ws>/runs/<run>/<agent>/commits/<sha>/<package | _kind>/attempt-<n>/<name>` (the agent right after the run, so one IAM prefix scopes an agent's writes; reports under `ws/<ws>/reports/…`), voc-finding/1 shard lines with credential-shaped strings and personal data redacted, bounded reads and create-only writes (D1). With `-c engineeringAgents=true`, a `voc-eng-workspace` bucket in VocCoreStack (the stack's KMS key, versioned, TLS only, access-logged, kept unless `-c protectData=false`; its policy refuses any write without `If-None-Match`, so no object is overwritten; nothing in it expires until an expiry that writes its `AUDIT#delete` row exists, TENETS.md D5).
- The commit, PR and goal reports (`lambda/engineering/reports/`): built from what the run recorded (its metering, the board's tasks and history, the objects their result keys name), every version new (D1); the PR report takes the quality gate's record only from an ended final-go task under the PR's head commit and checks it against the gate's own shapes before its Markdown goes into the PR description. The `voc-engineering-reports` Lambda builds them (nothing invokes it yet).
- The board's history: each post, claim and move writes a TASKLOG row with its actor and operation in the same transaction (D1, D4: no past state is overwritten); the reports show each task's history.
- Reads of a run (Agents API): `GET /agents/engineering/{run_id}/board`, `…/conversation`, `…/reports` and `…/reports/{level}/{subject}`, administrators only (403 for anyone else, an MCP credential included; 404 where the module is off), so no MCP tool (docs/mcp.md "Not tools, and why").
- Engineering flows (`voc-workflow/2`, `lambda/shared/workflow_engineering.py`): the agent, map, reduce, board, quality gate, learning loop, self-improvement, memory and stop-at-PR steps with their settings and graph rules (every map meets one reduce, a gate's NO-GO goes to a human decision point, a committer or PR author ends only at a stop at PR or a human decision point, no merge step). The two kinds never mix: no agent runs an engineering flow, a saved workflow keeps its kind, and `GET /workflows` leaves engineering flows out until the editor opens them.

### Changed

- The audit synth (`scripts/audit/py_assembly.py`) takes a function's flag-on bundle when it ships more code than the default one.
- The fixed-cost gate (`lib/fixed-cost-guard.test.ts`, TENETS.md tenet 7) now flags any CloudWatch alarm the app creates, and lists `-c engineeringSupervisorAlarm=true` among the opt-in fixed costs: it adds exactly one alarm, on the engineering supervisor's errors.
- 6.08.00's expiry of the raw bucket's `engineering/runs/` (90 days) is removed: a run's objects are kept until an expiry that writes its `AUDIT#delete` row exists (TENETS.md D5; planned). The `engineering/cache/` expiry (30 days, a rebuildable cache of repository code) stays.
### Upgrade notes

- Nothing changes for a deployment without `-c engineeringAgents=true`. With it, VocCoreStack gains the `voc-eng-workspace` bucket and the raw bucket loses its `engineering-runs-expiry` rule. Turning the flag off after it was on: deploy VocProcessingStack and VocApiStack first (both import from VocCoreStack; `--exclusively -c engineeringAgents=false`), then the rest (docs/deployment.md).

Autonomous engineering agents: the MicroVM runtime (one MicroVM per agent, the launcher, the runner's sandbox, sparse checkouts, checkpoints, the supervisor) and the harness each agent runs in. Merged from the voc-autonomous-b branch. Off by default, and not yet run against AWS.

### Added

- The harness (`runtime/harness/`): one interface, two adapters chosen per agent in its skill: a Bedrock Converse loop, and a coding-agent CLI headless at one pinned version with every built-in tool off and only the platform's tools, in a fresh home outside the checkout. The platform's tools: file tools confined to the checkout (no link, no `.git`, no file with two hard links), repository commands through the runner as the sandbox user, the dependency step, progress through the board, checkpoints carrying the working tree, and the work handed to the broker as a patch under the agent's own keys. Repository text reaches the model fenced as data. The board, inbox and broker ports refuse every call until the runtime is wired to them.
- The images (`voc-datalake/engineering-images/`): python, node, rust and java on one base and entry point, Mountpoint pinned by version and checksum, ready and validate hooks; they ship the harness, a pinned boto3 and the broker's agent identities (`connectors/identity.py`).

An agent role can be assumed only with all four session tags. `-c engineeringImageArns='{"python":"arn:…",…}'` names the MicroVM image per language (checked at synth; `{}` by default, so every launch is refused until it is set). The raw bucket expires `engineering/runs/` at 90 days and `engineering/cache/` at 30.

### Changed

## [6.06.00] - 2026-11-12 (voc-autonomous)

The connector broker gets its GitHub client: App tokens scoped to one repository and one operation, paged reads, a leased push and draft pull requests. Still off by default, and every permitted operation answers 503 until the run records and the board land.

### Added

- Autonomous engineering agents, phase 1, second slice: the broker's GitHub client and credential reader (`voc-datalake/lambda/engineering/connectors/github.py`, `credentials.py`; docs/autonomous-engineering.md "Repository connectors"). A connection's GitHub App credential (`app_id`, `installation_id`, `repository`, `private_key`) is read decrypted from the SSM SecureString `/[<prefix>-]voc/engineering/{connection_id}` and kept five minutes at most, never logged. Minting a token signs a nine-minute RS256 App JWT for an installation token for the connection's one repository and only the permissions that operation needs, kept until five minutes before it expires (within the hour GitHub gives it; none is revoked early: a stopped run's every further operation is refused before a token is used). Reads follow `Link` pagination by page number; a pull request read also returns its review comments and reviews; a file that is not UTF-8 text is refused. A rate limit (`Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, a secondary rate limit) is never waited out inside a call: it answers 503 with `Retry-After`. A push takes the parsed bundle (`BundleContents` now carries its base commit and each commit's file changes; its changed paths and added lines cover every commit), refuses a commit that changes a path the bundle does not list, refuses unless the branch's head is that base or, for a new branch, the base is the default branch's head or an ancestor of it (a base GitHub does not have is refused), rebuilds the commits with the Git Data API (text files inline in the tree, other files as blobs), refuses unless GitHub's resulting tree is the checked one, and moves the branch with `force: false` (or creates it). A draft pull request is opened or updated only when the branch's head has the checked tree, and its head is checked again afterwards: a pull request just opened on a branch that moved meanwhile is closed and the write refused (an update changes only the title and body; GitHub's REST API cannot turn a ready pull request back into a draft). Requests go only to `api.github.com`, follow no redirect and carry the token only in the `Authorization` header. A write whose answer was lost after it was sent answers 502 ("the write may have happened"), never a retryable 503, so a retry cannot make it twice (a lost answer to a token request stays retryable). An answer larger than the function URL can return is refused (502), never cut. New statuses: 404 (a read of what is not there), 409 for a host state other than the checked one (the branch moved, another tree), 502 a host error, 503 with `Retry-After` for a rate limit. Every write the broker completes gets an operational log line (a pull request it opened and closed again is logged as not closed only when the close fails) with what it wrote (operation, caller, connection, branch, tree hash, issue or pull request number), never its text; the durable audit row comes with the run records. The run records, the board's GO ledger and the bundle reader are not built yet, so every permitted operation still answers 503.
- With `-c engineeringAgents=true`, the broker's role also gets `ssm:GetParameter` on `parameter/[<prefix>-]voc/engineering/*` only and `kms:Decrypt` on the stack's key only through SSM (`kms:ViaService`) and only for those parameters (`kms:EncryptionContext:PARAMETER_ARN`), the env var `ENGINEERING_PARAMETER_PREFIX`, and the signing layer (cryptography, for the JWT); its timeout goes from 30 to 120 seconds, for a push's chain of Git Data API requests. The default synth adds no resource.

### Changed

- The GitHub REST API version string lives once, in `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/github_rest.py`; the GitHub plugin's client imports it from there.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing changes for a deployment without `-c engineeringAgents=true`.

The design of autonomous engineering agents: agents that learn how a connected GitHub or GitLab repository works and then hunt bugs, build features and review pull requests through a configurable quality gate, stopping at a pull request a person merges.

### Added

- [docs/autonomous-engineering.md](docs/autonomous-engineering.md): the design (nothing implemented yet; every design section is marked planned). ## [7.00.00] - 2026-11-13 (from main)

Prototypes show the company logo uploaded in the design system, an SVG logo can be uploaded again, and a large logo is made smaller instead of refused.

### Added

- A prototype now shows the company logo from Company → Design system (`/company?tab=design`) wherever it shows the company's logo, instead of a logo the model draws. The model writes a placeholder and the build puts the uploaded logo in its place as an inline image, so the prototype stays one offline file. It follows the build dialog's **Design system** box, and the prototype's "Built from" footer says whether the logo was used or left out (`derivation.company_logo_included`). A logo over 1 MB is left out and the prototype gets a drawn wordmark, as before. A revision uses the logo uploaded when it is built: when there is none any more (or the box is unticked), the model is told to draw a wordmark instead, and a leftover logo spot shows the brand or project name as text, never an empty image. Other inline images in a prototype are never mistaken for the logo. See [docs/company-context.md → How the AI uses them](docs/company-context.md#how-the-ai-uses-them).
- Company → Design system → **Upload logo** makes a large PNG, JPEG or WebP logo smaller in the browser instead of refusing it (up to 25 MB, was refused over 5 MB): at most 1,024 px on its longest side and under 1 MB, PNG first, then WebP so transparency is kept. A logo within 1 MB is uploaded as it is. See [docs/company-context.md](docs/company-context.md).
- A website design reference whose logo is a PNG, JPEG or WebP over 2 MB gets a logo preview again: the managed browser that reads the page draws it at up to 1,024 px and keeps that PNG, so **Use this logo** works (it was refused with "The logo is larger than 2 MB"). A GitHub repository's logo over 2 MB, or a reference read before this release, still cannot be used directly, and the message now says what to do: upload it as the company logo, or refresh a website reference.

### Changed

- **Breaking:** the company logo is at most 1 MB for every client: `POST /settings/design-system/logo` (was 5 MB) and **Use this logo** (`POST /settings/design-system/references/{id}/logo`, was 2 MB) answer 400 above it, so an API or MCP caller gets the same result as the web app, whose upload makes the image smaller first, and every saved logo fits a prototype.

### Fixed

- Company → Design system → **Upload logo** refused every SVG file with "could not be read as an SVG image. Export it as PNG and upload that." The browser converts an SVG to PNG before the upload, and it loaded the SVG from a `blob:` URL, which the site's Content-Security-Policy (`img-src 'self' data:`) blocks. It now loads it from a `data:` URL, and the policy is unchanged. PNG, JPEG and WebP uploads were not affected.

- Deploy the stacks (`npm run deploy:infra`, which deploys `VocCoreStack` before `VocApiStack`) and the frontend (`npm run deploy:frontend`). `VocCoreStack` gains one managed policy, `CompanyLogoReadPolicy` (`s3:GetObject` on the uploaded logos only, `company-context/design/logo_????????????.*` in the raw data bucket, so not the design references' logo previews), and `VocApiStack` attaches it to the document generator job role (`voc-job-document-generator`). **Breaking (the reason for the major version):** an API or MCP client that uploads its own company logo (`POST /settings/design-system/logo`) must send at most 1 MB (it was 5 MB), and **Use this logo** refuses a candidate over 1 MB (it was 2 MB); both answer 400 with what to do. The web app is not affected: it makes a larger image smaller before it uploads. Nothing else changes. Prototypes built before this release keep the logo they were built with; build or revise one to get the uploaded logo.

## [6.05.00] - 2026-11-11 (from main)

The repository's tooling needs Node.js 24, and the minimatch and fast-xml-parser security alerts are fixed.

### Changed

- Node.js 24.15+ is now the only supported line for the local tooling (root `package.json` `engines`, was `^22.22.2 || >=24.15.0`; `tools/kiro-acp-bridge` was `>=18.0.0`). It is the line CI and the Node Lambdas (`nodejs24.x`) already ran; Node 22 was never tested in CI. README, CONTRIBUTING and [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md) say so.

### Security

- minimatch (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, denial of service through glob-part amplification): every copy from 7.0.0 up to 11.0.1 is forced to `^11.0.1` by an npm override in `voc-datalake/`, `voc-datalake/frontend/` and `voc-datalake/lambda/stream/`. These copies are all used by build and lint tooling (ESLint, typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-sonarjs, Stryker); the repository-root project holds no minimatch. minimatch 11 drops `makeRe` and `AST`, which none of those use. The stream Lambda's `eslint-plugin-import-x`, which did, moves to 4.18.1, the first release that supports minimatch 11. glob 10 does not work on minimatch 11 (a pattern matches nothing), so the frontend's `quick-temp` (behind `i18next-parser`, the `i18n:extract` authoring tool) gets rimraf 6.1.4 through a second override, which brings glob 14, built for minimatch 11. When a lint-tooling bump brings a new minimatch consumer, check that it does not need `makeRe`, `AST` or glob 13 or older before keeping the override; when `quick-temp` changes, check that it still calls rimraf's `sync`, which the rimraf 6 override relies on. `scripts/dependency-overrides.test.mjs` (a `validate.sh` step) fails when any of the six committed lockfiles holds a minimatch in the vulnerable range other than the copy bundled in `aws-cdk-lib`, a glob older than 14 on minimatch 11, or an unaudited `quick-temp`. The copy bundled inside `aws-cdk-lib` stays at 10.2.6: npm cannot override a bundled dependency, and no `aws-cdk-lib` release ships minimatch 11 yet. That copy only matches the repository's own asset-exclude patterns at synth time and never sees user input.
- fast-xml-parser (GHSA-474x-hrwr-fgx4, quadratic CPU use on unterminated stop-node tags) moves from 5.11.2 to 5.12.0 in the frontend lockfile. `aws-amplify` pulls it in through `@aws-amplify/storage`. The SPA imports only `aws-amplify/auth`.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do for a deployment of the platform. A redeploy changes only the release number the Api and Processing Lambdas record (`APP_VERSION`, `6.5.0`), as every release does; that and the stream lockfile (the assistant's NodejsFunction `depsLockFilePath`) are why those two stacks' template hashes in `voc-datalake/lib/test-support/baseline.json` move, and no other stack's.
- Run `npm ci` again in `voc-datalake/`, `voc-datalake/frontend/` and `voc-datalake/lambda/stream/` to pick up the new lockfiles.
- Deploy from Node.js 24.15+ (`node --version`). On Node 22, npm warns `EBADENGINE`, and newer tooling may not run. On Node 24, `npm ci` in `voc-datalake/frontend/` still warns `EBADENGINE` once, for `i18next-parser` 9.4.0 (its latest release declares Node 22 or older); that warning is expected, and the tool runs on Node 24.

## [6.04.08] - 2026-11-11 (from main)

Workshop templates no longer reserve Lambda concurrency, so a Workshop Studio event's VocApiStack completes.

### Fixed

- `npm run generate:workshop-artifacts` synthesizes with `-c mcpReservedConcurrency=0`. Workshop Studio event accounts have only 110 unreserved Lambda executions (of a 1000 quota), and AWS keeps at least 100 unreserved, so the Global MCP endpoint's default reservation of 20 failed VocApiStack ("decreases account's UnreservedConcurrentExecution below its minimum value of [100]"). Without a reservation the endpoint shares the pool; its API Gateway method throttle (`GLOBAL_MCP_METHOD_THROTTLE` in `voc-datalake/lib/stacks/global-mcp.ts`) bounds the request rate, though not the concurrency. `voc-datalake/scripts/workshop-artifacts.test.ts` pins the flag, and `voc-datalake/lib/stacks/api-stack-mcp-global-ops.test.ts` already pins that 0 omits `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` instead of throttling to zero. See [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing changes for a deployment from `npm run deploy:infra`: the MCP endpoint keeps its reservation of 20 by default. Regenerate the workshop templates (`npm run generate:workshop-artifacts`) and republish them to the workshop's `development` assets.

## [6.04.07] - 2026-11-11

A fresh deployment's VocApiStack completes again: the API Gateway account setting accepts its CloudWatch role.

### Fixed

- The API Gateway CloudWatch role (VocApiStack, `lib/stacks/api-gateway-logging-role.ts`) grants its log writes on `Resource: "*"`. Since 6.00 the grants were scoped to `API-Gateway-Execution-Logs_*` and per-log-group ARNs, and API Gateway, which validates the role when the account setting (`AWS::ApiGateway::Account`) is written, refused it on every fresh account or region: "The role ARN does not have required permissions configured". Existing deployments were unaffected, because the setting is created once per account and region. The role still holds no AWS managed policy (cdk-nag IAM4) and gets no log-event reads: of `AmazonAPIGatewayPushToCloudWatchLogs`, it keeps the five write actions and leaves out `GetLogEvents` and `FilterLogEvents`, a combination API Gateway was verified to accept.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`). The role's inline policy changes; nothing is replaced.

## [6.04.06] - 2026-11-10

A fresh deployment completes again: the ModelPin custom resource can write its row.

### Fixed

- Roles with a write-only DynamoDB grant (`grantWrites`, `grantKeyScopedWrites` in `voc-datalake/lib/utils/table-write-grants.ts`) also get `kms:Decrypt` on the table's customer-managed key. A write needs it, and the write-only grants left it out, so the VocCoreStack `ModelPin` custom resource failed every FIRST deployment with "not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt" and rolled the stack back. Existing deployments were unaffected, because the pin is written only on create. The same grant also covers the roles that hold only a key-scoped delete or put on a table.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`): the change adds one KMS action to a few Lambda roles, nothing is replaced.

## [6.04.05] - 2026-11-10

Workshop templates pass Workshop Studio's template validation again.

### Fixed

- `voc-datalake/scripts/convert-template.mjs` (`npm run generate:workshop-artifacts`) keeps every `Description` CloudFormation requires as a literal string: the template's own and each Parameter's and Output's. Its region and account rewrite turned the VocWebSearchStack Description, which names its region, into an `Fn::Sub`, and the Workshop Studio build refused the template with "Every Description member must be a string". `voc-datalake/scripts/convert-template.test.ts` runs the converter on a scratch template.

## [6.04.04] - 2026-11-10

Workshop templates delete their data with their stacks.

### Fixed

- `npm run generate:workshop-artifacts` synthesizes with `-c protectData=false`, as [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#production-protectdata) asks of a workshop. Before, the Workshop Studio templates kept the DynamoDB tables (with deletion protection), both Cognito user pools, the KMS key, the raw-data and access-log buckets, the design-integrations secret and every log group when an event's stacks were deleted, so a second deploy into the same account failed with "already exists". `voc-datalake/scripts/workshop-artifacts.test.ts` pins the flag, the other workshop flags and the five converted stacks.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing changes for a deployment from `npm run deploy:infra`: `protectData` stays on by default. Workshop templates published before this release keep their data on teardown; regenerate and republish them.

## [6.04.03] - 2026-11-10

Operator tooling (a log sweep, an e2e users helper, a grouped e2e run), cheaper CPU for the integrations and logs APIs, and one vCPU for the settings API.

### Added

- `voc-datalake/scripts/ops/log_sweep.py`: a read-only sweep of one deployment. It lists every Lambda, Step Functions and stack error or warning line, e2e test traffic included, and the API requests by status class; every 5xx and every 4xx is listed except an e2e call that declared that status as expected. Exit 1 on a Lambda error / warning line, a 5xx or an undeclared e2e 4xx (real-traffic 4xx are listed only); exit 2 on an AWS error, or when it finds no log groups or no access log ([docs/deployment.md → Log sweep after a deploy](docs/deployment.md#log-sweep-after-a-deploy)).
- `voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/scripts/e2e-users.sh enable|disable`: turns the two e2e test users on (the `e2e` group, new random passwords, the suite's env file written outside the repository) and off again, reading the deployment from the stack outputs ([frontend/e2e/README.md → Run](voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/README.md#run)).
- The e2e suite declares each refusal it expects (`apiCall` / `e2eFetch` `{ expect: [<4xx>] }`, `expectRefusal` for page requests), sent as the User-Agent token `voc-e2e-expect/<status>`; `unit/expectedStatus.spec.ts` keeps assertions and declarations together.
- `run-sharded.sh --groups <file>`: one shard per named group of spec files, with per-group workers and Playwright flags; `e2e/shard-groups.txt` splits the production suite into 8 balanced groups, and `unit/shard-groups.spec.ts` keeps every spec in exactly one.

### Changed

- `GET /sources/status` (`voc-integrations-api`) describes the schedule rules on 2 parallel connections instead of 8, and the logs listing and `GET /logs/summary` (`voc-logs-api`) read DynamoDB on 2 instead of 8. Each connection after an idle gap is a new TLS handshake; measured on 8 sources, CPU per call drops from about 80 ms to about 40 ms, while the answer stays well under the 29 s gateway limit. Both functions were over the 60 % CPU rule at one vCPU ([docs/lambda-sizing.md](docs/lambda-sizing.md)).
- `voc-settings-api` runs at 1,769 MB (one vCPU) instead of 1,024 MB: it reached 86 % CPU at p95.

### Fixed

- The Dashboard's full-page states (no feedback in the time range, an empty workspace, a viewer with nothing in scope) give their heading as the page's `h1`; the page had no level-1 heading in those states.
- The e2e design track opens a project no e2e run created; it picked another shard's sharing project, which that spec deleted mid-run (a 404 on every later project screen).
- `/board/login` for someone already signed in to the app sends them to `/board`. Before, the page took `login` as a board's name and asked the API for it (a 404 "Board not found" on every such visit).
- The e2e `s2-agents` arrow test waits for the arrow's side panel to appear; `isVisible({ timeout })` answered at once and failed 1 run in 3. A unit check refuses that pattern in the suite.
- The Logs Insights filter documented for leaving out e2e traffic (`filter ispresent(test_run) = 0`, in the e2e README, `shared/e2e_tag.py` and the testing guide) does not compile; it now reads `filter not ispresent(test_run)`.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`): `voc-settings-api` moves to 1,769 MB, and the integrations and logs APIs get their new code. No data, permission or route changes.

## [6.04.02] - 2026-11-09

The web app's push notices reach the browser: 6.04 blocked their WebSocket with its own Content-Security-Policy.

### Added

- The production e2e suite covers the 6.00–6.04 features ([voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/COVERAGE.md](voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/COVERAGE.md)): push notices end to end (`realtime`), methodology, the feedback catalogue, workflow warnings and the erasure legal basis (`methodology-catalogue`), the 6.04 global MCP tools (`mcp-tools-6x`), and the scraper write rules, colour themes, two-editor unsaved guard and board Insights (`features-6x`).

### Changed

- Lambda sizes, per the 60 % rule ([docs/lambda-sizing.md](docs/lambda-sizing.md)): the board sign-up and custom-message triggers go from 128 to 256 MB (the sign-up trigger peaked at 74 % of its memory), and `voc-engagement-api` goes from 512 to 1024 MB (98.6 % CPU at p95).
- An agent run's review analysis and final review ask the model once more (one more call from the run's budget) when its answer holds no readable JSON, instead of failing the run with "The AI's answer could not be read" ([docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md)).

### Fixed

- Persona import (`voc-job-persona-importer`) reads every text block of the model's answer. A model that thinks answers with a reasoning block first; the import read only that block and failed with "Persona import failed: Expecting value".
- The web app's Content-Security-Policy (VocCoreStack, CloudFront `SecurityHeadersPolicy`) allows the AppSync Events WebSocket (`wss://*.appsync-realtime-api.<region>.amazonaws.com`). Before, every signed-in page logged "Connecting to 'wss://…' violates the following Content Security Policy directive", and the job, assistant and run notices of 6.04 never arrived, so the pages fell back to polling.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`). The CloudFront header change reaches the browsers within a few minutes; a page loaded before it still polls until it is reloaded.

## [6.04.01] - 2026-11-09

6.04.00 could not be deployed: VocCoreStack failed creating the realtime channel namespaces and rolled back. This release fixes the cause.

### Fixed

- The AppSync Events subscribe handler on the `jobs`, `chat` and `runs` namespaces (VocCoreStack) now compiles in AppSync. Its own-channel check is a private helper, because APPSYNC_JS refuses to call an exported function from inside the module ("Error processing APPSYNC_JS code"). A test now fails if the handler exports anything other than `onSubscribe`.

### Upgrade notes

- If a 6.04.00 deploy failed on an existing deployment, VocCoreStack rolled back by itself (`UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`) and the stacks that deploy after it (Ingestion, Processing, Api) still run the previous release. Deploy 6.04.01 the usual way (`npm run deploy:infra`, then `npm run deploy:frontend`). Nothing has to be cleaned up first.
- If 6.04.00 was the first-ever deploy, VocCoreStack is in `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (or `ROLLBACK_FAILED`), which CloudFormation cannot update. Delete that stack first (`aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name VocCoreStack`, or `<prefix>-VocCoreStack` for a prefixed deployment). Before deploying 6.04.01, look for a table, bucket or user pool that the failed create left behind (with `-c protectData=true` they carry deletion protection). Remove one only when its name carries THIS deployment's prefix, account and region (e.g. `voc-feedback-<account>-<region>`) and it holds no items or objects: other deployments in the same account use the same `voc-` names, and a leftover would block the new create on its fixed name.

## [6.04.00] - 2026-11-09

The browser hears when work finishes instead of asking every second and a half, the methodology is checked and reported by the server for every client, MCP can run the methodology steps, plugins declare what makes them different, the memory scanner stops scanning a whole table, the processed feedback item has a catalogue, and the SPA reads the code it shares with the assistant's stream Lambda from the stream package itself.

### Added

- **Push notifications over AWS AppSync Events.** The browser hears at once when an assist job ends, when an assistant answer it is following ends, and when an agent run or an approved plan changes status, and re-reads it then. One Event API in VocCoreStack with `jobs`, `chat` and `runs` channels; each person can subscribe only to their own channels, and only the platform's Lambdas can publish. Every other long job the web app polls tells the person who started it when it ends too: project jobs (persona generation and import, PR/FAQ / PRD generation and merge, research, the company persona library), category reprocess, erasure jobs, S3 import reprocess runs, the manual-import parse, memory page imports and the morning brief. Polling stays as the fallback after a reload or reconnect and for every other caller; only a design-reference capture still polls alone ([docs/realtime.md](docs/realtime.md)).
- **Methodology on the server** (TENETS.md tenet 2, [docs/project-workspace.md → Methodology](docs/project-workspace.md#methodology)): `GET /projects/{id}` carries `methodology`, the upstream steps each step is missing. Research, PR/FAQ, PRD, "Pursue" and prototype starts answer a `methodology` block (skipped steps, warnings, evidence), stored on the document they write and in the job result. The project Overview names the missing steps the server lists, and the Documents tab shows a document's methodology gaps.
- **Workflow methodology warnings**: `POST /workflows/validate` answers `warnings` (a PRD with no PR/FAQ, personas or evidence before it, …), shown above the workflow editor's canvas. They are advice: save and run are not refused ([docs/autonomous-agents.md](docs/autonomous-agents.md#methodology-warnings)).
- **Global MCP tools**: `generate` (personas, research, PR/FAQ, PRD, prototype, with the methodology block), `get_job`, `read_radar`, `edit_feedback`, `get_feedback_catalogue` (with `sources: true`, the source status), `get_prioritization`, `score_prioritization` (the minter's own scores), `write_feature_request` (post a request or +1 one on a board the minter can see, recorded under the minter's verified email and name: one +1 per person, whichever token), and `boards: true` on `search_feature_requests`. Imports, source switches, Prioritization axes and board status changes stay out: their routes are admin-only and an MCP token never acts as an admin ([docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md#tools)).
- **Methodology in agent runs and plans**: a run node or plan step that starts research, personas, a PR/FAQ, a PRD or a prototype records the methodology block in the run journal or on the plan step, and the run log and the plan card list the skipped steps and warnings.
- **Evidence on imported and copied personas**: an imported or copied persona stores `evidence {source, count, inherited, origin}` and a `no_evidence` warning when it carries none (a copy keeps the evidence of the persona it came from); the persona header says "No customer evidence: imported".
- **Data Explorer → Fields**: a reference panel in the processed view shows the feedback catalogue (field, type, meaning, set by, personal data, what a redact / summary-only source does to it, allowed values).
- `POST /scrapers` and `POST /integrations/{source}/apps` take optional `mode: create|update` and `base_etag`; the list routes add a computed `etag` ([docs/scrapers.md → Write rules](docs/scrapers.md#write-rules)).
- `GET /feedback/catalogue`: what every stored attribute of a feedback item means (type, meaning, the pipeline step that sets it, whether it holds personal data, what a `redact` / `summary_only` source policy does to it, the allowed values of each enum), for any signed-in user, ETag-cached. [docs/data-catalogue.md](docs/data-catalogue.md) is generated from the same source, and a test fails when a writer stores an attribute the catalogue does not list.
- Plugin manifests declare what the platform does differently for their source: `capabilities.updatesItems`, `infrastructure.ingestor.selfInvoke` and `infrastructure.webhook.memory` ([docs/plugin-architecture.md → Capabilities](docs/plugin-architecture.md#capabilities)).

### Changed

- A PR/FAQ or PRD request reads customer feedback unless `data_sources.feedback` is `false`; before, a request that named no data sources read none. A hand-written PR/FAQ or PRD is stored with `evidence: 0` and says so; a generator that leaves selected reference documents out (more than 3) records which ones.
- While the page is subscribed, assist jobs and the job views above poll every 10 s and a reloaded "still generating" assistant session every 15 s as a fallback; without the Event API (dev mock, older deployments) polling is as before. The runtime `config.json` carries a `realtime` block (the Event API hosts).
- The memory scanner (`voc-memory-scanner`, every 15 min) reads the last week of assistant sessions through the new `voc-conversations` index `gsi1-by-kind-updated-at` instead of scanning the whole table, so its idle cost no longer grows with stored conversations; its role holds `Query` on that index only.
- The `s3_import` ingestor runs on its own role (`IngestorRoleS3Import`, from the new manifest capability `infrastructure.ingestor.jobNotices`) instead of the shared ingestion role, so only it may publish job notices.
- The in-place refresh of GitHub issues, the app-review ingestors' self-continuation grant and the GitHub webhook's 512 MB are declared in those plugins' manifests instead of being keyed on plugin ids in platform code. Nothing changes for any plugin.
- The SPA imports the AG-UI contract, the plan schema and checks, the persona-result storage and the approval-card bounds (persona, product context, feedback form, review import, Radar, memory, company, agents, workflows, assist-job polling) from `voc-datalake/lambda/stream/src` through the `@stream/*` alias (`frontend/streamSource.ts`: vite, vitest and tsconfig, zod deduplicated). The bounds, rules and messages are the ones each side used before; where the two sides worded a message differently, each keeps its own.
- The stream Lambda lints every module the SPA reaches with a `browser-safe` block (no Node built-ins, `@aws-sdk` or `@smithy`, not even as a type, and no Node-only globals), and `src/browser-safe.test.ts` fails when the SPA reaches a stream module the block does not cover (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Code the SPA shares with the stream Lambda").
- One `IconBadge` component draws 18 icon badges (verdicts, run outcomes, plans, visibility, pins, release watch, model tests). Nothing on screen changes.
- The duplication excuses for the SPA ↔ stream copies go: 6 `.jscpd.json` file ignores, 10 inline `jscpd:ignore` blocks, 5 TypeScript clone allowlist entries for the mirrors and the knip and reachability entries that existed for them; 3 more clone allowlist entries go because their copies are now shared (the agent heartbeat and memory scanner builders, the scraper and user approval executors, the verdict and run-outcome badges).
- TENETS.md: tenet 7 says how work moves (EventBridge schedules, job + worker, AppSync Events notices, SSE for the live answer, MCP request/response, polling only as fallback), and the "Where the platform stands today" rows for tenets 2, 4, 5, 7 and D7 follow this release.

### Fixed

- `POST /projects/{id}/build-prototype` with no PRD and no PR/FAQ answers 409 before any job, instead of a 202 and a failed job.
- The users API refuses (409) an administrator's change to their own role, enabled state or account, and the demotion, disabling or deletion of the last enabled administrator, for every client, not only in the web app ([docs/account-vs-admin.md → Users](docs/account-vs-admin.md#users)).
- The scraper and app-connector create-never-overwrites and stale-update rules are enforced by the API (409 / 404) when the client sends `mode` / `base_etag` (the web app, the assistant and plan steps do), not only by the assistant's card.
- The "Adding a New Data Source" steps (`.kiro/steering/structure.md`) and the plugin template README describe the real procedure.

### Upgrade notes

- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`). VocCoreStack adds a global secondary index to `voc-conversations` in place (no replacement); DynamoDB builds it from the existing conversations and the stack update waits for it; no backfill is needed. VocCoreStack also adds the Event API, its log group and logs role, and one managed publish policy per channel namespace (`jobs`, `chat`, `runs`), with exports of the Event API host and those policies; the publishers in VocIngestionStack, VocProcessingStack and VocApiStack attach their namespace's policy and get the host in their environment. The default deploy order (Core first) is all it needs.
- Cost: AppSync Events is pay per use only (about $1 per million operations and $0.08 per million connection minutes); no fixed monthly cost.
- `npm run deploy:frontend` writes the `realtime` block only when VocCoreStack has the `RealtimeHttpDns` and `RealtimeDns` outputs.
- `voc-mcp-global-api` may now also invoke `voc-radar-api`, `voc-feedback-edit-api` and `voc-integrations-api`.
- Seven job workers of VocProcessingStack and VocIngestionStack (research, category reprocess, retention, memory extractor, briefing, the agent conductor, the `s3_import` ingestor) carry VocCoreStack's `jobs` / `runs` publish policy and the Event API host. `voc-retention` gains only that publish policy.
- Scripts that start a PR/FAQ or PRD without `data_sources` now ground it in customer feedback; send `data_sources: {feedback: false}` to keep the old behaviour. Scripts that demote, disable or delete the caller's own admin account, or the last admin, now get 409. Documents made before 6.04.00 carry no methodology block.

## [6.03.02] - 2026-11-08

The pull request AI review converges: later rounds review only the new commits and give every earlier finding a status. It also reads the changed files, follows a new `REVIEW.md`, and scales its depth to what changed. This is development tooling only: the platform, its stacks and the workshop packaging do not change.

### Added

- **`REVIEW.md`**: what failure looks like in each area of the repository, how to report (file:line evidence, one finding per class of mistake, at most 3 nits, a count first) and what to skip. Both AI reviews read it, `npm run validate:commit` / `validate:tenets` locally and the `AI review` workflow on pull requests.

### Changed

- **Rounds converge.** From the second push on, the `AI review` comment is a new round ([CONTRIBUTING.md → AI review on pull requests](CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-review-on-pull-requests)):
  - it reviews only the commits since the last review, with the whole diff as context;
  - every earlier finding keeps a stable id (`T1`, `C1`, …) and is listed once as **Resolved**, **Answered by the author** or **Still open**, above the new findings;
  - a blocking finding still open keeps the verdict at BLOCK, whatever the model's own verdict line says;
  - there is no limit on rounds;
  - each pass resumes from the last commit it reviewed to the end, so a pass that failed or was cut short reviews the commits it missed;
  - a rewritten history gets the whole diff again, still with the recap.
- **The reviewer sees the code around the change**: the current text of the changed files and of the files the change names by path, within a size limit, read from git objects only.
- **Depth follows the changed paths**:
  - documentation only (`*.md`, `docs/`, `LICENSE`; never TENETS.md, REVIEW.md, CONTRIBUTING.md or `.kiro/`) gets a short review;
  - CI, the git hooks and the gates that enforce the tenets, the reviewers, TENETS.md and REVIEW.md, IAM and stacks, data deletion, authentication and access checks, and the AI-writing guard get a deep one, with a larger output budget and context;
  - everything else gets the standard review.

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do for a deployment of the platform. A redeploy changes only the release number the Lambdas record (`APP_VERSION`, `6.3.2`), as every release does.
- The AWS role of the review (`tools/ai-review-ci/`) does not change. The new review applies from the first pull request after this one merges, because the reviewer is read from `main`.

## [6.03.01] - 2026-11-07

Duplicated code that the duplication checks had excused is now shared, and every excuse that is left names a constraint that was checked (one names its planned fix instead).

### Changed

- Shared helpers replace copies in the API and worker Lambdas: request-body checks (unknown fields, free text), the latest-run status of sources and scrapers, the category / source / project access reads, cursor encoding, update expressions, strong reads, the Cognito client, a worker's time budget and the GitHub API base. Answers, status codes and error wording are unchanged; JSON key order in `GET /sources/status`, `GET /scrapers/{id}/status` and the authenticated form view may differ.
- The SPA shares one component each for icon tab rows, labelled text inputs, enum and option selects, clamped number inputs, QR code panels and Data Explorer row actions, and one stale-approval check for the scraper, Radar and user cards. Nothing on screen changes.
- The duplication allowlists shrink (`scripts/audit/allowlists/`: Python clones 17 → 6, Python functions 8 → 5, shared constants 19 → 17, TypeScript clones 23 → 13) and `.jscpd.json` ignores one file fewer; each remaining entry's reason names what keeps it, except one icon-badge pair whose reason gives the planned shared component.

### Fixed

- A feedback list cursor that is not UTF-8 JSON is refused with a 400 like the Radar cursor, instead of being decoded.

## [6.03.00] - 2026-11-06

Processed feedback keeps its history and says how it was made, and a reprocess can replay a slice: every in-place change keeps the item as it was, every enriched item records its pipeline version, mode and the model that answered, and reprocessing takes sources, categories and a date range and resumes where it stopped.

### Added

- **Silver history**: after any in-place change to a feedback item (a category or dimensions edit, a Data Explorer edit, a GitHub issue refresh, a CSV correction, a reprocess), the item as it was is written once to `silver/{source}/{feedback_id}/` in the raw bucket, with who changed it, why and which fields; a change that was refused keeps no version. Data Explorer refuses to write under `silver/`. The bucket policy makes `silver/` write-once like `raw/`, and erasure and retention delete every kept version with the item ([docs/data-lake-structure.md](docs/data-lake-structure.md)).
- **How an item was made**: every enriched item records `pipeline_version` (the app release), `enrichment_mode` (`llm`, `defaults` when the model call failed, `reprocess_*`, `source_update`), `enriched_at`, and in `llm_metadata` the model that answered and the one requested (they differ after a capacity fallback).
- **Reprocess a slice**: `POST /settings/categories/reprocess` and Administration → Taxonomy → Reprocess take `sources`, `categories` and a `date_from` / `date_to` range on the processed or the review date (`date_basis`), next to `days`, up to 50 values per list (the panel says so when a list goes over and Start stays disabled) ([docs/categories.md](docs/categories.md)).
- **Resume a reprocess**: a job that stops at the 50,000-review limit ends `partial` with a cursor, and `{resume: <job_id>}` (the Resume button) continues where it stopped instead of starting over. A resume that fails or is cancelled hands the job back, so it can be resumed again.
- Reprocess jobs record the configuration they ran with (config version, categories digest, model, prompt version) and how many reviews fell back to their stored text (`raw_fallback`, `raw_fallback_sources`).

### Changed

- Edited items carry `updated_by {sub, kind}` (`kind`: `user`, `admin`, `agent`, `mcp`, `plan` or `system`), `updated_at` and `change_reason`; the API shows only `kind`. An edit leaves the enrichment provenance as it was, so `pipeline_version` and `enriched_at` keep describing how the item was enriched. Plan steps, agents and MCP tokens are told apart from a person.
- `PUT /data-explorer/feedback` writes only the fields that changed, checks each one and applies the source's PII policy: 400 for a bad value or for setting customer text on a summary-only source, 503 when the source settings cannot be read, and 409 when the record changed since it was read (the editor stays open and asks, in the interface language, to close and reopen the record; 404 when it is gone).
- The enrichment prompt version is 2.0.0 (the prompt had changed since 1.0.0); a test now pins the prompt text to its version.

### Fixed

- French, Spanish and Portuguese have the plural form their grammar uses for round millions ("1 000 000 de avis") on all 97 counted strings that lacked it; those counts no longer fall back to English.
- The dev mock (`npm run mock`) stamps every feedback edit like the API (`updated_at`, `updated_by`, `change_reason`), refuses a stale Data Explorer save with the API's 409, and checks a reprocess resume in the route's order.
- Data Explorer: saving an edit of a branded review (stored under its brand, not its source) no longer answers 404; the record is found by its id.
- `PUT /feedback/{id}/dimensions` now records who changed it, when, and the previous value.
- A raw-mode reprocess no longer writes a translation or a customer quote back on a summary-only source.
- A processed or dimensions reprocess now updates `llm_metadata` with the model that answered.
- A redelivered DynamoDB stream record (REMOVE / MODIFY) no longer moves the aggregates twice.

### Upgrade notes

- New grants: `s3:PutObject` on `silver/*` for the processor, the reprocess worker and the feedback-edit API (the Data Explorer writes its kept versions under its existing bucket-wide put); `voc-retention` may delete and list versions under `silver/*`. A slice by source is a filtered scan (sources are matched on `source_platform`, so branded reviews are included), so the worker needs no new table grant. The raw bucket's policy changes (VocCoreStack). Deploy with `--all`.
- Items stored before 6.03.00 have no `pipeline_version` and keep `prompt_version` 1.0.0 until reprocessed.
- A reprocess job's status can now be `partial`; before, a job stopped at the limit read `completed`.

## [6.02.00] - 2026-11-05

Feedback boards become their own evidence source: requests are enriched on their own row, can be cited in personas, research and documents, are searchable by the assistant and over MCP, and have their own Insights view. They never enter the review pipeline or its metrics.

### Added

- **Board request enrichment**: each feedback-board request gets a category, subcategory, sentiment, language and a one-sentence problem summary, stored as `enrichment` on the request in `voc-feature-requests` (one enrichment-surface model call per new request or per edit of its title / description; a failure is stored as `status: failed` and never fails the request). Admins backfill existing requests with `POST /feature-requests/insights/enrich` (≤ 200 per call, answers `{queued, remaining}`; a request queued in the last 15 minutes is not queued again, so a repeated click bills nothing twice) or the "Enrich requests" button ([docs/feature-requests.md](docs/feature-requests.md#enrichment)).
- **Board Insights**: `GET /feature-requests/insights?board=&days=` and an Insights tab on Feedback boards (`/feature-requests?tab=insights`): totals, the 20 most-supported requests, requests by category, status and sentiment, with a 30 / 90 / 365 / all window. Scoped by board access like every board route; never mixed into Dashboard or review metrics. Requests show their category and sentiment chips once enriched. Every enrichment result is kept as its own version row (`ENRICH#…`), so a re-enrichment never loses the previous one.
- **Feature requests as evidence**: the persona, research and PRD / PR/FAQ wizards have a "Feature requests" option (off by default) with an optional board picker and a count beside the review count. The API takes `include_feature_requests` + `feature_request_board_ids` (personas, research) and `data_sources.feature_requests` + `feature_request_board_ids` (documents). Prompts cite board requests as `[FR:<id>]`, apart from reviews; personas, research reports and document derivations store `input_feature_request_ids` (≤ 200), and the views link each citation to its request ("Written from N reviews and M feature requests") ([docs/project-workspace.md](docs/project-workspace.md)).
- **Search board requests**: `GET /feature-requests/search` (`q`, `board`, `category`, `status`, `days`, `limit` 1–100), scoped by board access, answers requests without any name or email. The AI assistant and `/mcp/global` (read scope) get the matching `search_feature_requests` tool ([docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md)).
- Personas and documents say how many of their cited reviews or board requests were erased (legal basis recorded), never which ones.

### Changed

- **An erasure by email reaches the feedback boards**: the person's requests and +1s are de-identified (email and name removed; a +1, whose id was derived from the email, moves to a new random id and still counts as a supporter), every version of their raw copies under `raw/feature_requests/` is deleted, each row gets a tombstone, and artifacts that read those requests are marked. Erasure jobs show the `boards` phase and `board_items_deidentified` ([docs/source-policies.md](docs/source-policies.md)).
- The legal basis field refuses an email address or phone number before the request is sent (the API stays the authority).
- Docs: the DELETE routes that carry a legal basis in a JSON body note that some HTTP clients drop DELETE bodies (the API then answers 400 and deletes nothing).

### Upgrade notes

- `voc-engagement-api` now calls the enrichment-surface model (pay-per-use, one call per new or edited board request). Run the backfill once after deploying to enrich existing requests.
- New grants: the persona generator, document generator and research step roles get `dynamodb:Query` on `voc-feature-requests` and its `gsi1` index; `voc-retention` gets Scan / GetItem / Query / UpdateItem on it, plus PutItem / DeleteItem pinned to the request partitions (`FR#*`) to re-key an erased +1; the global MCP Lambda may invoke `voc-engagement-api`. VocCoreStack adds one export that VocProcessingStack imports, so deploy with `--all` (or Core before Processing). No new fixed-cost resource.

## [6.01.00] - 2026-11-04

Five colour themes instead of one: an administrator picks the start theme for everyone, and each person can pick
their own.

### Added
- **Colour themes**: Nord, Dracula, High contrast and Quick next to Kiro, each in a light and a dark mode. The new
  palettes are adjusted where their upstream values missed WCAG AA (High contrast goes to 7:1 for text). Quick also
  brings its component look: Inter, ink pill buttons, blue links and focus ring, flat surfaces
  ([docs/kiro-design-system.md](docs/kiro-design-system.md) → Themes).
- **Administration → General → Default theme**: the theme everyone sees until they choose their own, stored for the

- **Account → Preferences → Colour theme**: "Workspace default" (the administrator's pick) or one of the five

  ghost: a snowflake for Nord, a bat for Dracula, a contrast circle for High contrast, Quick's four-point spark for
