- **Kiro dark contrast**: white text on a hovered primary button was 3.68:1 and the faint `muted-strong` text on a
  hovered row 4.23:1, both under WCAG AA's 4.5:1. The button hover now darkens (as in Kiro light) and the faint text
  is a shade lighter; every theme is now held to the same text contrast checks.
- **Unsaved changes with two editors on one page**: react-router allows one navigation blocker per page and the
  editor mounted last held it, even with no edits. On Administration, unsaved brand edits were lost without the
  "Unsaved changes" prompt when a link was followed while a board editor was open; the new Default theme card would
  have done the same on every visit to General. Only an editor with edits holds the blocker now, and when several
  editors hold edits, leaving asks each of them in turn (Save / Discard / Cancel); a Back stays a Back.

### Upgrade notes
- Nothing to do: without a saved default the app stays on Kiro, and a person's earlier light/dark choice is kept.

## [6.00.02] - 2026-11-04

Pull requests get the tenets review and the code review of `scripts/validate.sh` as an automated comment. This is development tooling only: the platform, its stacks and the workshop packaging do not change.

### Added

- **The `AI review` workflow** (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`, `scripts/ai-review/ci-review.mjs`) reviews every pull request from this repository. It runs the tenets review first, then the code review, and posts both as one comment ([CONTRIBUTING.md → AI review on pull requests](CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-review-on-pull-requests)).
  - **Model and prompts:** Claude Opus 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock, with the prompts of `npm run validate:tenets` / `validate:commit`, read from `main`.
  - **What it sees:** TENETS.md, the pull request's description and comments, the commit messages and the diff. It is called with no tools, and nothing of the pull request is checked out or run.
  - **Advisory:** it fails no check. A push that leaves the diff unchanged gets no new review.
  - **When it skips:** forks, drafts, Dependabot, and a repository without the `AI_REVIEW_ROLE_ARN` secret.
- **The review's AWS role** (`tools/ai-review-ci/`) is a standalone CloudFormation stack, deployed by hand and never with the platform. It holds the GitHub OIDC provider and a role that only this repository's `pull_request` runs can assume, limited to `bedrock:InvokeModel` on Opus 5.5 and its two fallback models. `scripts/ai-review/ci-role.test.mjs` fails when the trust or the permissions widen ([tools/ai-review-ci/README.md](tools/ai-review-ci/README.md)).

### Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do for a deployment of the platform. A redeploy changes only the release number the Lambdas record (`APP_VERSION`, the connector version of the raw objects they write, `6.0.2`), as every release does; that is why the Api and Processing template hashes in `voc-datalake/lib/test-support/baseline.json` move.
- To turn the review on, a maintainer deploys `tools/ai-review-ci/ai-review-role.json` into the account that pays for the reviews, with Bedrock access to the three Claude models. Then set the repository secret `AI_REVIEW_ROLE_ARN` and the variable `AI_REVIEW_REGION`. Until then the workflow skips with a notice.
- The reviewer is read from `main`, so the pull request that adds it is not reviewed itself; the next one is.

## [6.00.01] - 2026-11-04

Faster Python cold starts: every Lambda bundle ships its own code compiled.

### Changed
- **Python Lambda bundles ship bytecode.** Every function built by the CDK bundling now includes `.pyc` files
  compiled by the Python 3.14 bundling image (unchecked-hash, PEP 552), so a cold start no longer compiles the
  function's own modules (about 35,000 lines for the Projects API). Each deployment zip grows by roughly the size
  of its source. Measured in production: the Projects API's cold start went from 1.58 s to 1.24 s (p50), the other
  APIs by 7–14 %. See [docs/lambda-sizing.md](docs/lambda-sizing.md) → Cold starts.

### Fixed
- Production e2e suite: the participant erasure gives the legal basis 6.00.00 requires, in the erase dialog and in
  the suite's own cleanup (`DELETE /participants/people/{id}` with `{legal_basis}`), so test people are erased again.

## [6.00.00] - 2026-11-03

Deletes follow the tenets: customer data is deleted only for a stated legal basis and leaves a tombstone, workspace deletes really delete and are recorded, no role holds a delete it does not use, and no role can change an audit row. Major: the erasure routes require a legal basis.

### Added

- **Every customer-data delete states its legal basis** (TENETS.md D5): `POST /settings/erasure` takes `legal_basis` (≤ 300 characters), source profiles take `retention_legal_basis`, and `DELETE /participants/people/{id}` takes `{legal_basis}`. The text is kept on audit rows that are never deleted, so a basis that contains an email, phone number, card, IBAN or IP address is refused (400): use a case or ticket number. Administration → Privacy & access → Source policies asks for it in the person erasure, the "Delete all data from a source" dialog and a source's retention setting, and the participant's erase dialog asks for it too ([docs/source-policies.md](docs/source-policies.md#retention-and-erasure), [docs/participants.md](docs/participants.md)).
- **Tombstones**: `voc-retention` writes one contentless row per deleted item (`AUDIT#tombstone#<source>` / `<feedback_id>` in `voc-aggregates`: source, job, mode, legal basis, time; no `ttl`) before the delete. A participant erasure writes `AUDIT#tombstone#participant` (person id hash) and an `AUDIT#delete` row in `voc-participants`, with no email or name.
- **Erasure and retention reach Radar**: matching `voc-radar` reviews, their dedupe markers and their raw archives are deleted (the brand's daily counters are kept); the job shows `deleted_radar_items` ([docs/radar.md](docs/radar.md)).
- **Erased evidence is marked**: personas, research reports and documents that cited an erased review lose its id from `input_feedback_ids` / `evidence_feedback_ids` and carry `erased_evidence: {count, job_id, mode, at}`; the job shows `artifacts_marked`. Their text is not rewritten.
- Erasure jobs show their legal basis, Radar and marked-artifact counts, and any uploaded CSV / JSON file kept for review (`files_needing_review`, keys only).
- **Workspace deletes are recorded**: every delete of a project, persona, company persona, document (and a research / custom document's saved revisions), product doc, document comment, feedback request, +1, feedback board, participant list, list member, chat conversation and an archived design reference's copies writes one `AUDIT#delete` row in the table that held it: what (ids only), who (`{sub, kind}`: user, admin, agent, MCP token, plan or system; never an email) and when. The rows never expire; a record that cannot be written never fails the delete, and is counted in the `DeleteRecordFailures` metric (namespace `VoC`). A replace-mode persona regeneration records each persona it removed (`persona_replaced`) as the person who started it ([docs/project-workspace.md → Deleting](docs/project-workspace.md#deleting)).
- **Documents say when a source was deleted**: when a persona, document or product doc is deleted, the documents of the same project that were written from it gain `deleted_sources` (returned by the projects API), and the document view shows "Written from a persona that was later deleted: <name>" (or a document / product document). The ids stay in the document's lineage.

### Changed

- **Deletes remove every S3 version**: persona avatars (persona delete, regeneration, a failed copy), a deleted prototype's HTML (a deleted prototype document now takes its HTML with it), product doc uploads and extracted text, a project's prototypes / product docs / avatars, and an archived design reference's logo preview and icons are deleted with every version and delete marker.
- The raw data bucket no longer expires noncurrent versions under its workspace prefixes (`avatars/`, `company-context/`, `memory-imports/`, `projects/`, `prototypes/`): deleting a workspace artifact removes every version itself. `scratch/` still expires after 2 days, now its noncurrent versions too ([docs/data-lake-structure.md](docs/data-lake-structure.md)).
- "Delete all data from a source" also deletes the CSV and JSON files uploaded to that source (`raw/csv_upload/…`, `raw/json_upload/…`, every version). Retention and other erasures keep such a file when it holds a deleted row, and list it on the job / audit row for review.
- The Sources page flags a retention period saved without a legal basis, and a save needs one.
- **The feedback processor and the aggregator run as separate IAM roles**, each with only what its handler uses: the aggregator can no longer call Bedrock, Comprehend or Translate, write `raw/`, read the processing queue or touch feedback items (`voc-datalake/lib/stacks/processing-roles.ts`).
- **DynamoDB writes are granted per action**: every API, job, ingestor and worker role keeps its reads and gets only the writes its code makes. The metrics API is read-only on `voc-aggregates`; no role but `voc-retention` can delete feedback or Radar items; the document generator, persona importer and product-doc extractor can no longer delete S3 objects.
- `voc-retention` gets exact grants for its new reach: PutItem / BatchGetItem on `voc-aggregates` (tombstones are written one PutItem each: a batch write would also allow deletes), Scan / DeleteItem on `voc-radar` plus the `SETTINGS#radar` cache-version bump, Scan / UpdateItem on `voc-projects`; its explicit Deny on the whole-file upload prefixes is gone (a whole-source erasure now deletes the source's own uploads). New env `RADAR_TABLE`, `PROJECTS_TABLE`.
- `POST /s3-import/reprocess`'s 404 for an expired staged file names the import bucket's real expiry, passed to `voc-s3-import-api` as `IMPORT_STAGED_EXPIRATION_DAYS`.

### Security

- No role holds a delete it does not use. A role that deletes operational rows in a shared table (a circuit-breaker row, the morning-brief subscriber row, a form config, validation logs, a Prioritization row and its ballots) has the delete pinned by `dynamodb:LeadingKeys` to those rows' partitions. The whole-app inventory of deleters covers every customer-data, workspace and audit table and every raw-bucket prefix (`voc-datalake/lib/customer-data-deletes.test.ts`).
- **Audit rows are protected by IAM**: `AUDIT#*` rows in `voc-aggregates`, `voc-projects`, `voc-participants`, `voc-feature-requests` and `voc-conversations` carry an explicit Deny: no role can update or delete one, a batch delete included, and only its named writer can put one (`voc-retention`; the projects API and persona generator; the engagement API; the chat API; the settings API only `AUDIT#delete` in `voc-aggregates`) (`voc-datalake/lib/utils/audit-row-guard.ts`).
- The projects API, the persona generator and the settings API's design-preview cleanup may delete object versions (`s3:DeleteObjectVersion` + `s3:ListBucketVersions`), on their own prefixes only, never `raw/`.
- Audit trails of customer-data deletes carry no `ttl` and no content: the `AUDIT#retention` run row records the legal basis (`legal_basis` / `legal_bases`), and tombstones record each deleted item.

### Upgrade notes

- **Breaking API change:** `POST /settings/erasure` answers 400 without a non-empty `legal_basis` (≤ 300 characters), and so does `DELETE /participants/people/{id}` without `{"legal_basis": "…"}` in its body. Update scripts and integrations that call them.
- `PUT /settings/sources` answers 400 for a profile that sets `retention_days` without `retention_legal_basis`. Existing profiles with a retention period and no basis keep running unchanged (their audit rows and tombstones say `legal_basis: "not recorded (set before 6.00.00)"`); add the basis on the Sources page before the next save. An erasure job queued before the deploy runs with that same value.
- The aggregator gets a new IAM role (`AggregatorLambdaRole`); CloudFormation creates it and switches the function over in one deploy. The processor keeps `ProcessingLambdaRole`. No table, bucket or queue is replaced.
- Roles lose write actions they did not use. A custom Lambda or script that runs as one of the platform's roles and deleted rows with it now gets `AccessDenied`; a process that changes or deletes an `AUDIT#` row is denied whatever its role.
- After this release, overwritten or deleted objects under the raw bucket's workspace prefixes are no longer purged after 90 days. Versions left by an artifact deleted BEFORE this release (a delete marker over noncurrent versions) are not purged either: remove them once with a temporary lifecycle rule or by version.

## [5.78.00] - 2026-11-03

Follow-ups to the 5.77.00 review: the opt-in WAF keeps its rule exceptions off the public routes, and the tests now
check what deploys.

### Changed
- **`-c enableWaf=true`**: the core-rule-set rules the API only counts (body size, cross-site scripting, LFI, RFI,
  EC2 metadata SSRF, query-string size, query-argument RFI) block again on the unauthenticated routes: the feedback
  widget's config and iframe, ballot config, `POST /unsubscribe`, `/.well-known/*` and `/oauth/*`. A new rule on each
  web ACL blocks a counted rule's label there, except where a legitimate request carries it: the two public submit
  routes and webhooks keep every body rule counted (a customer's feedback or ballot note may be long and hold HTML,
  paths or links), and the MCP loopback `redirect_uri` stays counted on
  `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/register` and `/oauth/token`. The SPA's CloudFront web ACL counts the query-argument
  RFI rule only on `/oauth/authorize`. One more rule per web ACL: about $20 a month for both instead of $18
  ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md) → AWS WAF, which also says how to check the rule once after turning it on).

### Fixed
- Tests: the per-stack CDK tests apply the same whole-app rewrites as the deploy (`lib/utils/app-aspects.ts`), so
  they check the exact grants and log groups that deploy; a test runs every boundary body of the two public
  request models through the handlers' own validation and a draft-4 validator (a model may never refuse what its
  handler accepts); every function whose role holds a shared Claude policy is pinned to wait for it during a deploy.

## [5.77.00] - 2026-11-02

Most cdk-nag findings are fixed in the infrastructure instead of acknowledged (114 findings remain in the default synth, from 588 in 5.75.00), and
AWS WAF and the Cognito Plus plan become opt-ins.

### Added
- **`-c enableWaf=true`**: AWS WAF on the SPA's CloudFront distribution (a CLOUDFRONT-scope web ACL in
  `VocWebSearchStack`, us-east-1, read by `VocCoreStack` through a cross-region reference) and on the API's `v1`
  stage: AWS managed IP reputation, known bad inputs and core rule set, plus a per-IP rate limit. About $9 a month
  per web ACL ($18 for both) plus $0.60 per million requests. Seven core-rule-set rules only count on the API (MCP
  loopback callbacks, long `?ids=` lists, large imports and stored text are legitimate), one on CloudFront. See [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md).
- **`-c cognitoPlus=true`**: both user pools on the Cognito Plus plan with threat protection in audit mode (it
  scores sign-ins and never blocks one). $0.020 per monthly active user, no free tier.
- `-c performanceTier=true` now turns on both opt-ins too (it already turned on SnapStart).

### Changed
- **Exact IAM grants** (`voc-datalake/lib/utils/exact-grants.ts`): no identity policy carries CDK's grant wildcards
  any more. KMS grants list the exact actions (`kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:Decrypt`, …); the DynamoDB-only KMS
  actions are allowed only through DynamoDB. S3 grants list the actions the code calls (`s3:GetObject`,
  `s3:ListBucket`, `s3:DeleteObject`, …). DynamoDB grants name each index instead of `<table>/index/*`.
- **Lambda logging**: no role uses `AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole`; each function's role writes only its own log group
  (`logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents`) and cannot create log groups. The API Gateway account logging role
  has an inline policy instead of `AmazonAPIGatewayPushToCloudWatchLogs`.
- **Claude model grants** use AWS's documented cross-Region shape (inference profile, in-Region model, Region-agnostic
  model, with `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` and `aws:RequestedRegion` conditions) in shared customer-managed policies
  per stack; no Region wildcard. With `-c inferenceScope=eu` they list the `eu.` profiles' destination Regions
  ([docs/eu-deployment.md](docs/eu-deployment.md)).
- **Lambda invoke grants** no longer carry CDK's version/alias wildcard (`<function arn>:*`) for a function that has
  no version or alias: every caller (Step Functions tasks, CDK custom-resource providers, the Projects API's job
  starts) invokes it unqualified. A SnapStart function (`live` alias) keeps it.
- **API Gateway request validation** on the public JSON write routes (`POST /feedback-forms/{form_id}/submit`,
  `POST /voting-sessions/{session_id}/submit`): a body that does not match what the handler accepts is answered
  400 at the gateway (`{success:false, reason:'invalid', error:'invalid_request', …}`, with the usual CORS
  headers) before any Lambda runs. The models are never stricter than the handlers. Not modelled: the form-encoded
  `POST /unsubscribe`, `POST /oauth/token` and `POST /oauth/revoke`, and `POST /oauth/register` (its handler answers
  the RFC 7591 error codes and logs the client).
- **Point-in-time recovery** on the idempotency table (usage-based cost).
- **Board user pool password policy**: 16 characters with every character class (board sign-in is by email code;
  the SPA's generated password already meets it).

### Security
- Most acknowledged cdk-nag findings are fixed rather than accepted (114 remain in the default synth); every remaining acknowledgement is a wildcard
  AWS requires, a public route by design, or a paid opt-in that is off ([docs/code-audit.md](docs/code-audit.md)).

### Upgrade notes
- Deploy every stack (`npm run deploy:infra`): IAM policies change in place; no resource is replaced.
- A Claude call that does not go through an allowlisted `global.` / `eu.` inference profile, or from another Region,
  is now denied. An SCP or permissions boundary must allow `aws:RequestedRegion` `unspecified` for global inference
  (AWS requirement).
- Lambda log groups are no longer created on first invocation: do not delete one by hand. Nothing recreates it
  (CloudFormation does not restore a resource deleted outside it), so that function's logs stop; recreate the group
  with the same name. During the upgrade deploy a function, and API Gateway's logging through the account role, may
  drop log lines for a few seconds, between a role losing its managed policy and its inline grant landing.
- WAF outside us-east-1 needs the us-east-1 CDK bootstrap.
- **A deployment already on `-c performanceTier=true`** gets two web ACLs (about $18 a month) and the Cognito Plus
  plan (no 10,000-MAU free tier) on its next deploy, and outside us-east-1 needs the us-east-1 bootstrap. To keep only
  SnapStart, deploy with `-c snapStart=true` instead, or leave features out of the tier with `-c enableWaf=false` /
  `-c cognitoPlus=false` (a feature's own flag now overrides the tier).
- `-c inferenceScope=eu` now refuses, at synth, a region that is not a source Region of the `eu.` profiles (listed in
  [docs/eu-deployment.md](docs/eu-deployment.md)): the grant has to name the profiles' destination Regions.
- With WAF on, seven AWS core-rule-set rules only count on the API (`GenericRFI_QUERYARGUMENTS`,
  `SizeRestrictions_QUERYSTRING`, `SizeRestrictions_BODY`, `CrossSiteScripting_BODY`, `GenericLFI_BODY`,
  `GenericRFI_BODY`, `EC2MetaDataSSRF_BODY`) and `GenericRFI_QUERYARGUMENTS` on CloudFront: MCP loopback OAuth
  callbacks, long `?ids=` lists, imports and stored text that quotes HTML, paths or URLs are legitimate. The per-IP
  rate limit is shared by everyone behind one egress IP, an e2e runner included (docs/deployment.md → AWS WAF).
- Turning WAF off: deploy `VocCoreStack` first; if `VocWebSearchStack` held only the web ACL, delete it in us-east-1
  afterwards (docs/deployment.md → AWS WAF).

## [5.76.00] - 2026-11-02

The raw data lake keeps history: raw objects are write-once and versioned, name the connector that wrote them, nothing under `raw/` expires, every ingested source keeps a raw copy when its policy allows one, and audit trails no longer expire.

### Added

- Every ingested source keeps a raw copy in the raw lake, write-once and versioned, when its source profile permits one ([docs/data-lake-structure.md → Every ingested source has a raw copy](docs/data-lake-structure.md#every-ingested-source-has-a-raw-copy)):
  - feedback-form submissions under `raw/feedback_form/`, opt-in (only once an admin saves a `feedback_form` source profile that permits a copy, because the route is public): only what the public route validates: `text` and `dimensions` as validated (stripped, cleaned), `rating`, `page_url`, `custom_fields`, and `email` / `name` only when the form collects them; never another body field or the participant link token; the queued item's `s3_raw_uri` names the copy ([docs/feedback-forms.md](docs/feedback-forms.md#processing-pipeline));
  - feedback-board requests (on create and every content edit) and +1s (on create and every edit) under `raw/feature_requests/`, opt-in: only once an admin saves a `feature_requests` source profile that permits a copy (they hold reporters' and supporters' emails); boards are still not queued into `voc-feedback` ([docs/feature-requests.md → Raw copies](docs/feature-requests.md#raw-copies));
  - received email (`.eml`) under `raw/email_intake/` when the `email_intake` profile is set to `pii: allow`, filtered mail (repeats in a thread, replies without news) included with an S3 `drop-reason`; duplicates and mail over the sender cap are not kept, so the caps still bound storage ([docs/email-intake.md](docs/email-intake.md#raw-copies));
  - S3 import originals under `raw/s3_import/` (metadata `original-key`) when the `s3_import` profile keeps whole files (allow, no retention period);
  - the processor archives a message's inline `raw_data` when its producer's archive write failed (connector `processor`).
- Plugins archive the payload they received next to the mapped item (`raw_content`): the App Store RSS entry, the Google Play review, the scraped review element's outer HTML or the JSON-LD `Review`, the S3 import row; at most 256 KB, with a truncation marker.

### Changed

- **Raw objects are write-once and versioned.** Every raw write uses `If-None-Match: *` at `raw/{source}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{item}/{sha16}.json`: one folder per item, one object per distinct content (`{sha16}` hashes the content, never a timestamp). Ingesting identical content again writes nothing; changed content (an edited review, a GitHub issue update, a CSV dataset correction) becomes a new object next to the old one. Plugins, webhooks and the API writers share one helper, `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/raw_versions.py` ([docs/data-lake-structure.md](docs/data-lake-structure.md)).
- A confirmed CSV dataset correction files its new raw version in the stored item's folder and points the item's `s3_raw_uri` at it; the previous version stays ([docs/csv-import.md](docs/csv-import.md)).
- Every new raw object carries S3 metadata `connector` and `connector-version`: the plugin id and its manifest version (`webhook_<plugin>` for a webhook), or the API writer (`manual_import`, `csv_upload`, `json_upload`, `feedback_form`, `feature_requests`, `data_explorer`, `processor`, …) and the platform release. Plugin envelopes also carry `connector` and `content_sha16` ([docs/plugin-architecture.md](docs/plugin-architecture.md)).
- Every webhook, not only GitHub's, archives its delivery (`BaseWebhook`).
- VocCoreStack: the raw data bucket no longer expires noncurrent versions under `raw/`. Its other prefixes (`avatars/`, `company-context/`, `memory-imports/`, `projects/`, `prototypes/`, `scratch/`) keep the 90-day noncurrent expiry, each in its own lifecycle rule; `scratch/` keeps its 2-day expiry.
- Retention and erasure (`voc-retention`) delete an item's raw objects in both layouts: the older `…/{item}.json` object and every object under `…/{item}/`, every version and delete marker ([docs/source-policies.md](docs/source-policies.md)).
- Audit trails no longer expire: the global MCP token audit log (`MCPAUDIT#{token_id}`, under Connect → token details and `GET /connect/tokens/{token_id}`) and the import history (`IMPORT_RUN` rows, the **Import history** section of the Data sources page and `GET /scrapers/manual/history`) are written without a `ttl` ([docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md), [docs/import-history.md](docs/import-history.md)). The Import history section no longer says it shows "the last 90 days" (every language).
- `POST /s3-import/reprocess` on a staged file that has expired answers 404 with a message naming its raw copy; staged files still expire after 90 days (the import bucket is an inbox).

### Security

- The raw data bucket's policy denies any `s3:PutObject` / `CompleteMultipartUpload` under `raw/` without `If-None-Match` (statement `DenyRawWritesWithoutIfNoneMatch`, multipart parts exempted as [AWS documents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes-enforce.html)), so no writer can overwrite a raw object; CopyObject into `raw/` is refused as a consequence.

### Upgrade notes

- Existing raw objects (`raw/{source}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{item}.json`) stay where they are; nothing is moved. New writes use the folder layout; readers and erasure handle both.
- Noncurrent versions under `raw/` are no longer expired, so raw storage grows with every changed re-ingest (identical content adds nothing).
- Any custom or out-of-band process that writes under `raw/` (a script, a replication job, an S3 batch copy) must send `If-None-Match: *` on PutObject / CompleteMultipartUpload, or it gets 403; CopyObject into `raw/` no longer works.
- New IAM grants, all put-only and write-once (no read, no delete): `voc-feedback-form-api` on `raw/feedback_form/*`, `voc-engagement-api` on `raw/feature_requests/*`, the processing role (processor and aggregator) on `raw/*`, the opt-in `voc-email-intake` on `raw/email_intake/*`. These Lambdas, the manual-import Lambda and `voc-data-explorer-api` get `APP_VERSION`; each new writer gets `RAW_DATA_BUCKET`. Plugin ingestors and webhooks get `PLUGIN_VERSION`.
- `APP_VERSION` is the platform release, so every release now changes the VocApiStack template (a version-only redeploy of the API Lambdas' configuration).
- The email inbox's default profile is `pii: redact`, so by default it writes no raw copy; nothing changes for an existing inbox until an admin sets the `email_intake` profile to `allow`. The `inbound-raw/` 90-day copy is unchanged.
- Feedback-form and board raw copies are off until an admin saves a `feedback_form` / `feature_requests` source profile, so an upgraded deployment starts persisting neither silently. Once on, they carry the reporter's and supporter's email and name (what the board row stores); an erasure by email does not reach them yet, a whole-source erasure of `feature_requests` does.
- An API-side item (manual / JSON import) received again on a later day is archived in that day's folder; erasing that item removes the folder its `s3_raw_uri` names, while a whole-source erasure removes all of them.
- MCP audit and import-history rows written before this release keep the 90-day `ttl` they were written with and still expire on it; rows written from this release on are kept.

The last held dependency upgrades land: jsdom 30, knip 6.44.1 in the frontend, cdk-nag 3 and mutmut 3. The deployed

- **Dependabot**: no update is held any more (docs/dependencies.md → Held updates).

### Fixed

  dependencies (libcst, textual).

## [5.74.00] - 2026-11-02

Safer defaults: customer data survives a stack delete unless a demo opts out, every operational log keeps 30 days, and the deployment has one customer-managed KMS key.

### Changed

- `protectData` is on by default (`voc-datalake/lib/utils/data-protection.ts`): the data tables, the raw-data bucket, the KMS key, the `voc/design-integrations` secret and the Cognito user pool are kept when the stacks are deleted or a resource is replaced, tables and the user pool get deletion protection, the raw bucket has no auto-delete provider, log groups and the access-log bucket are retained, and every stack gets termination protection. Demos, workshops and temporary environments deploy with `-c protectData=false` ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#production-protectdata)).
- Every operational log keeps 30 days: every Lambda log group (CDK's own provider functions included), the API Gateway access log, the Step Functions logs (`LOG_RETENTION` in `lib/utils/log-retention.ts`), in protected and unprotected deployments alike, and the S3 server access-log bucket expires current objects and noncurrent versions after 30 days. Before, Lambda and API logs kept 14 days (7 for some providers, 365 under `protectData=true`), and access logs 90 days (noncurrent versions 7). Audit evidence stays in the DynamoDB audit rows.
- One customer-managed KMS key per deployment: the operational alarm topic (`voc-ops-alarms-…`) and the scheduled-ingestion dead-letter queue (`voc-ingest-schedule-dlq-…`) are encrypted with the Core key instead of keys of their own. The Core key's policy admits CloudWatch only from this account (`aws:SourceAccount`, as the old alarm key did; the topic policy still limits publishing to this deployment's `voc-*` alarms) and EventBridge only under the SQS encryption context of that one queue.
- The fixed-cost gate (`voc-datalake/lib/fixed-cost-guard.test.ts`) also counts the resources billed per resource per month in the default synth: exactly one KMS key, and the known baseline of three Secrets Manager secrets, which may only shrink ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)).

### Upgrade notes

- **protectData flips to on.** An existing deployment that never set `protectData` switches, on its next deploy, its data tables, raw-data bucket, user pool, KMS key, design-integrations secret, log groups and access-log bucket to `RetainExceptOnCreate` / `Retain`, turns on DynamoDB and Cognito deletion protection, removes the raw bucket's auto-delete provider and turns on termination protection. Nothing is replaced. To keep a demo's one-step teardown, deploy with `-c protectData=false` (or `"protectData": false` in `cdk.context.json`) and keep passing it: the value must be deployed BEFORE `cdk destroy`, or the retained resources stay in the account. A redeploy into the same account and region after a protected teardown fails while those fixed-name resources exist: delete them by hand or deploy with a different `-c deploymentPrefix` ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#production-protectdata)).
- **Log retention.** The deploy sets every existing log group to 30 days. Groups that kept 365 days lose their events older than 30 days (CloudWatch removes them shortly after the change); groups that kept 7 or 14 days keep their events longer from now on. Access-log objects older than 30 days are expired by the S3 lifecycle within a day or two. Export anything you need to keep longer before deploying. The cross-region export provider groups still need the one-time `aws logs put-retention-policy ... --retention-in-days 30` ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#log-retention-of-cdks-own-provider-lambdas)).
- **Two KMS keys go away.** The alarm topic and the schedule DLQ switch to the Core key in place (no replacement; the DLQ and topic names stay). CloudFormation then deletes the old `OpsAlarmsKey…` (VocCoreStack) and `IngestScheduleDLQKey…` (VocIngestionStack) keys, which KMS schedules for deletion with the default 30-day pending window. A key pending deletion cannot decrypt, so a message already in the schedule DLQ (encrypted under the old key) cannot be read after the deploy: inspect or re-drive it first (Administration → System → Logs shows the failure queues). The 30-day window outlasts the DLQ's 14-day message retention, so if one is found later, `aws kms cancel-key-deletion` and `aws kms enable-key` on the old key make it readable until it expires; then schedule the key's deletion again.

## [5.73.01] - 2026-11-01

TENETS.md now describes the code as it is, and four tenets say what was decided about erasure, AI modes, Gold and the one KMS key.

### Changed

- **Tenet 3**: the three ways of working (Human-driven, AI-assisted, AI-driven) apply to writing the PR/FAQ and the PRD; an AI may not file that text under another document type. Personas, research and prototypes are AI-backed in every mode, and ingestion, browsing, metrics and hand-written documents work without a model ([TENETS.md](TENETS.md#3-teach-before-you-accelerate-ai-is-a-dial-not-a-dependency)).
- **Tenet 7**: one customer-managed KMS key (about $1 a month) is the accepted fixed-cost baseline, because tenet 6 ranks higher.
- **D1**: an item received again with new content is stored as a new raw version next to the old one.
- **D2**: Gold is derived data only; configuration, access rules, votes, the documents people write and the audit trail are primary data, kept and protected. A *redact* or *summary only* source keeps no unredacted copy (privacy over a full Bronze copy).
- **D5**: customer data (raw items and the feedback derived from them) is deleted only for a legal obligation, an erasure request or a declared retention limit, each with its legal basis, logged and tombstoned. Workspace artifacts (projects, personas, documents, boards, lists, conversations) are deleted when their owner deletes them, and the deletion is recorded.
- **Where the platform stands today** lists the gaps found by a full audit of the code against every tenet: Bronze files are overwritten on re-ingest and old versions expire after 90 days, the missing raw copies and connector version, the methodology and AI-mode gaps, MCP coverage, the delete permissions, `protectData` off by default, and the KMS keys and secrets the cost guard does not count. The enforcement section no longer claims that only `voc-retention` holds a delete permission, or that the AI-mode check covers every path.
- The reviewer prompts (`.kiro/steering/tenets.md`, `.kiro/agents/prompts/security-reviewer.md`) and [docs/source-policies.md](docs/source-policies.md#retention-and-erasure) follow the new D5 and tenet 3 wording.
- The steering notes no longer describe the raw bucket as immutable, and give the global MCP token expiry as 1–90 days, the bound the mint route enforces (`MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS` in `voc-datalake/lambda/shared/mcp_global_tokens.py`; it was written as up to 365).

## [5.72.01] - 2026-11-01

`scripts/validate.sh` reviews the change with the developer's own coding agent, against TENETS.md and like the GitHub PR review, and can re-run only what failed.

### Added

- Two AI review steps in `scripts/validate.sh` (`scripts/ai-review/review.mjs`): `tenets: AI review` checks the change since `origin/main` against TENETS.md, and `commit: AI review` reviews the whole change with its commit messages, as the GitHub pull request review does, so its findings are fixed before the push. ## [5.72.00] - 2026-11-01

The AI assistant no longer sets up review sources it cannot back up: app ids are checked against the store, and review-page URLs must come from a web search result.

  click. The trend has labelled axes, a legend, straight lines and the whole window, and below 10 reviews a sentence
  replaces it. The admin scan block is one status line (last scan, **Scan now**) beside **Configure**; every window
  reads "Last N days"; content text is 14 px. See [Radar](docs/radar.md#the-radar-page).
- **Compared with us needs 10 of their reviews** (`GET /radar/brands/{brand}/compare` and `/page`): a category with
  fewer reads "Not enough reviews to compare" (`too_few: true`, `verdict: null`) with one footnote, instead of a
  verdict from 1 or 2 reviews; the morning brief's "where they beat us" card follows the same rule. The response gains
  `overall: {theirs, ours}`, the whole window per side (the summary strip's tile).
- **One release per name**: a news item with the same headline as a stored release of the brand merges into it at any
  date, and the releases route folds older same-name records into one (citations unioned, mentions summed). The All
  brands release counts count distinct names.

### Fixed
- **Radar release links named another story**: an index page (a changelog or news list, or a page several releases
  cite) no longer shows the title of whichever story headed it when searched; it shows its site and path.
- **Radar releases cited unrelated pages**: a link is kept only when it is on the brand's own domains or its title or
  address names the brand (or one of its search terms). The scan drops the others before filing, and stored releases
  show only the links that pass. See [Radar → News](docs/radar.md#news-web-search-exa-and-the-brands-feeds).

### Upgrade notes
- No migration: older release records read merged and filtered on the way out; nothing stored is rewritten or deleted.
  Deploy as usual (`npm run deploy:infra`): the API and SPA (`VocApiStack`) and the scan and morning brief workers
  (`VocProcessingStack`) change; the scan applies the new rules from its next run. No new permission: the Radar API
  already reads the aggregates table.

## [5.67.01] - 2026-11-01

The quality-gate CI run takes as long as its slowest lane instead of all of them in a row.

### Changed
- **CI runs one job per gate lane** (`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`): `validate (py|tsc|lint|test|web)` run on
  separate runners with `scripts/validate.sh --lane <name>`, and the `scripts/validate.sh` check is a final job that
  is green only when every lane is. pytest has the py job to itself, so CI no longer needs `--pytest-first` and gives
  it 4 workers. See [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md#how-validatesh-runs).
- **`scripts/validate.sh`**: a `--lane <lanes>` option (only those lanes' steps; the lanes partition every step),
  the frontend vitest suite in its own `web` lane, and ESLint on worker threads (`--concurrency auto`) for the CDK,
  frontend and stream packages, which also shortens local runs.
- **A local gate run deletes a graduated coverage-baseline row itself** (`check-per-file-coverage.mjs
  --prune-graduated`, passed by `scripts/validate.sh` off CI): a listed file that reaches the 80 % floor no longer
  fails the step locally; its row is removed and named, to commit with the change. CI stays strict and the floor is
  unchanged. See [coverage gate](docs/coverage-gate.md).

Review-type pills on the Categories page, and pills that do what a reader expects on both pages.

- **Categories → review types**: the Problems page's review-type pills (Problems only, All types, one pill per

  breakdown card. The page opens on every type; the choice is in the URL (`/categories?types=feature_request`).

  `dims=feedback_type:<value>` opens as that one pill. See [categories](docs/categories.md#review-types).

- **Problem Analysis → review types**: **Clear** now unpresses every type pill (every type, no type filter)

  while Problems only shows selects only that type (one click for "only feature requests"); later clicks add

  [problem analysis](docs/problem-analysis.md#review-types).

- Frontend only: no API, stack or data change. While most reviews have no type yet, a type choice changes
  little on either page, because untyped reviews always stay in view; run **Administration → Taxonomy →
  Dimensions → Classify review types for existing reviews** to type stored reviews (one enrichment-model call

Dependency upkeep: one held lint plugin and one updated.

## [5.66.00] - 2026-10-31

Ideas from @aws-bryan's PR #429 rebuilt on the current platform: model agreements without a shared use-case form, the assistant kept to the filters on screen, multi-value and usefulness filters, persona match counts, citations and protection, project export/import, and a per-source data profile.

### Added

- `-c modelAgreementRetry=<value>`: a deploy with a new value attempts every Bedrock model agreement again (best
  effort, like the first attempt), for example after filing the use-case form in the console
  ([docs/deployment.md → Retry a refused agreement](docs/deployment.md)). Without it a refused agreement was never
  retried. (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- AI Chat (`/chat`) has a filter panel above the composer: time range, source, categories, sentiment, rating,
  channel, tag and "Urgent only". It shows a live count of the matching reviews and a non-blocking warning when
  the scope holds more than 1,000 reviews, the most one assistant search reads. The scope belongs to the
  conversation and is sent with every message as `forwardedProps.scope` on `POST /chat/stream`
  ([docs/assistant-chat-scope.md](docs/assistant-chat-scope.md)). (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- Every feedback read route (`/feedback`, `/feedback/urgent`, `/feedback/search`, `/feedback/entities`,
  `/feedback/problems`, `/metrics/*`) takes several values of `source`, `category`, `subcategory` and
  `sentiment` as a comma list meaning any of them; one value works as before. The caller's category and
  source access still applies, so a list never shows a hidden source
  ([docs/categories.md](docs/categories.md#filtering-by-several-values)) (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- A `usefulness` filter on the same routes (`low`, `medium`, `high`, several allowed; `unrated` for reviews
  without a band), with a Usefulness filter on Categories and Problem Analysis (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- Dashboard filters for source, category, sentiment and usefulness, kept in the URL like Categories. A filtered
  window with no reviews keeps the filters and offers Clear filters (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- A usefulness badge (High / Medium / Low) on feedback cards and in the review modal; unscored reviews show
  none (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- The persona and research wizards show a live "N reviews match" line at the foot of the feedback-filters step: a
  quick estimate first ("About N"), then the exact count, which is the generation's own read of the window, filters
  and your category access, so the number and the run agree. The persona wizard also says whether the personas read
  every match or an even sample of them. New route `POST /projects/{id}/feedback-preview` (edit access, under the
  existing projects proxy; the exact count stops after 20 seconds and then says "at least N"; answers are reused for
  five minutes) (docs/project-workspace.md) (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- A generated persona now records which reviews it cites: the model's "Review #N" references in its supporting
  evidence are resolved to the feedback ids of that run's prompt order and stored as `evidence_feedback_ids`.
  "Written from N reviews" on the persona says how many it cites, and the list opens on a "Cited" view next to
  "All used". A reference that names no review the model read stays as text only. Personas generated before
  this release have no Cited view (docs/project-workspace.md) (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- Protect a persona: a lock in the persona header (edit access) marks it protected, and a "Replace existing
  personas" generation then keeps it, next to the existing add/replace choice. The new personas are written knowing
  the protected ones (like an add run), a new persona with a protected one's name is dropped, the wizard counts only
  the unprotected personas it deletes, and a persona protected while a run is going is still kept. The list shows a
  lock on protected personas. New route `PUT /projects/{id}/personas/{persona_id}/protection` `{protected: true|false}`
  under the existing projects proxy (docs/project-workspace.md) (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- Projects can be copied between deployments with two operator scripts, `voc-datalake/scripts/project-export.py`
  and `project-import.py`, run with your own AWS credentials (no new route or Lambda). A versioned bundle carries
  the whole project: personas, PR/FAQs, PRDs, prototypes, documents and their versions, decision records, comment
  threads, prototype pins, product docs and avatars. The owner and members are matched in the target user pool by
  email (`--owner-email` when the owner is not there), `--new-ids` imports a second copy under fresh ids, and
  `--dry-run` prints the plan. Review links, MCP tokens and jobs are not carried.
  See [docs/project-export.md](docs/project-export.md). (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- Data Explorer → Processed Feedback → Data quality shows a **Source profile** below the usefulness bands: per
  source, its star ratings, sentiment split and text-length buckets, one facet at a time. `GET /metrics/data-quality`
  adds a `profile` object to every source row and to `overall` (additive; existing fields unchanged), read from new
  daily aggregator counters (`METRIC#daily_profile_rating|sentiment|length#<source>#<value>`), with no model call
  and no new worker. See [docs/data-quality.md](docs/data-quality.md#per-source-profile). (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)

### Changed

- The Claude model agreements (EULA + Marketplace subscription per allowlisted model) are now created by
  `VocCoreStack` in the app's region, best effort, on the first deploy that includes them (and again on a deploy
  with a new `-c modelAgreementRetry`): a refused agreement, a model not offered in
  the region, throttling or a dropped connection is logged in the agreement Lambda's log group and reported, and
  never fails or rolls back the deploy. They used to be created by the us-east-1 `VocWebSearchStack`, and only
  alongside the use-case form. With web search off (`-c enableWebSearch=false`) and no form, no stack deploys to
  us-east-1 any more. See [docs/deployment.md → Anthropic Model Access](docs/deployment.md#anthropic-model-access-first-time-setup)
  (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- Anthropic's use-case form is opt-in: the committed `cdk.context.json` no longer carries an `anthropicUseCase`
  block, so a deploy no longer files the form in your account under another company's name. File it once in the
  Bedrock console (Model catalog → an Anthropic model → Submit use case details), or pass your own block.
  `skipUseCaseSubmission` still works, and with it a block alone no longer creates `VocWebSearchStack`
  (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- The AI assistant can no longer read past the filters on screen. The Categories and Problem Analysis filters and
  the AI Chat panel's scope are a floor for `search_feedback`, `list_feedback`, `get_urgent_feedback`,
  `get_entities` and `get_metrics`: the assistant can narrow within them, an argument outside them returns
  nothing, and a filter a tool cannot apply makes it refuse rather than widen. A Usefulness filter is part of the
  floor too (`unrated` = reviews without a band). A long filter list (up to 50 values) reaches the assistant whole, and
  filters that cannot be sent make the assistant read nothing rather than everything. Without filters the assistant reads as before ([docs/assistant-chat-scope.md](docs/assistant-chat-scope.md)). (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- Categories: choosing several categories, sources or sentiments (the sentiment chips now multi-select) and a
  subcategory filters on the server, so the list's counts and pages are exact. Before, extra categories and the
  subcategory were filtered in the browser over the loaded page only. Problem Analysis takes several sources
  (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan).
- An unknown `sentiment` value on the read routes is now a 400 instead of an empty answer.

### Fixed

- An agreement offer without an offer token is reported as `NO_OFFERS` instead of failing the agreement step
  (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- Persona regeneration in replace mode (Projects → Personas → Generate, "replace the current personas") now removes
  every existing persona. It used to read only the first page of a project's personas and to stop at the first
  failed delete, so some old personas could survive next to the new set. Each persona is now deleted on its own, a
  failed delete is logged and the rest still go, and only the deleted personas' avatar images are removed.

### Upgrade notes

- `anthropicUseCase`: the docs now match what the deploy has always validated. `intendedUsers` is an index (`"0"`
  internal users, `"1"` external customers, `"2"` both; default `"0"`) and `industryOption` one of a fixed list
  (default `Technology`). A block written from the old docs with a sentence in `intendedUsers` is skipped with a
  synth warning, as before; use the index ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)).
- An unknown `sentiment` value on the read routes (`/feedback`, `/metrics/*`, `/feedback/entities`,
  `/feedback/problems`) now answers 400 instead of an empty result, like the other facets. A saved link or an
  API caller sending a value other than `positive`, `neutral`, `negative` or `mixed` (for example `sentiment=all`)
  must drop the parameter to mean every sentiment.
- On the next deploy, `VocCoreStack` adds one agreement custom resource per allowlisted Claude model; the
  agreement Lambda it already had for the image model runs them. Models that already have an agreement are
  reported `ALREADY_AVAILABLE`. `VocWebSearchStack` drops its agreement resources and their Lambda and provider;
  if you deploy without a use-case block it also drops the submission resource, and with web search off the
  whole stack leaves the app (CDK does not delete a stack dropped from the app: remove it with
  `cdk destroy VocWebSearchStack` once nothing imports from it). Nothing in your account is revoked: the
  agreement handler leaves agreements in place on Delete, and the form, once filed, stays filed. No table,
  bucket or other data resource is renamed or replaced (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- If you relied on the committed `anthropicUseCase` block to file Anthropic's use-case form, nothing files it
  any more. File it in the Bedrock console, or pass your own block in an uncommitted context file or in your
  deploy job (`docs/deployment.md` → "Submit the form from CDK instead"). An account that already has access
  needs neither (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)
- The source profile counters start when this release is deployed: reviews stored earlier are counted in the
  source totals but not in the profile, and the Data quality section shows that share. To profile an older window,
  run `scripts/retention/rebuild_aggregates.py` for it. Each new review writes three more aggregate rows.
  (ported from #429 by @aws-bryan)

## [5.65.00] - 2026-10-31

Security hardening from a Well-Architected security review: opt-in passkeys, tighter IAM, logs and edge, and
safer handling of customer text in prompts.

### Added
- **Passkeys (opt-in).** After sign-in the app asks once whether to add a passkey (fingerprint, face or screen
  lock); **Account → Profile → Passkey** lists the person's passkeys, adds one and removes one (a lost or
  replaced device), and **Login** has *Sign in with a passkey*. The
  password keeps working; MFA is not enforced. The app user pool allows WebAuthn as a first factor, with the
  site's own domain as relying party and the choice-based `USER_AUTH` flow on the web client
  (`features.passkey` in `config.json`). See [docs/deployment.md → Passkeys](docs/deployment.md#passkeys).
- **Per-sender email cap.** A non-administrator's asks (`POST /participants/asks`) send at most 50 emails a UTC day,
  checked before queueing (429 `sender_daily_cap`) and again on every send; the deployment cap (default 500) still
  applies, and is an administrator's only limit.

### Changed
- **API Gateway** uses the enhanced TLS 1.2+ forward-secret policy `SecurityPolicy_TLS12_PFS_2025_EDGE`
  (endpoint access mode BASIC). Execution logs are at ERROR (were INFO). The access log no longer records the
  request path (a ballot link's id is a bearer value) and adds `sub`, `principalId` and `tlsVersion`.
- Every app API answer (the shared resolver behind every `/…` domain route, and `/mcp/global`) and every gateway
  error carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- **SPA headers:** CSP adds `form-action 'self'` and drops the unused Lambda Function URL source; `X-XSS-Protection: 0`
  and a `Permissions-Policy` are added. A legacy inline-HTML prototype is offered as a download only, and its
  preview frame can no longer submit forms.
- **Feedback form themes** accept hex colours and a pixel radius only, on save and again in the widget; a stored
  non-hex colour falls back to the default.
- The **feedback processor** runs at most 20 invocations at once, so a flood of widget submissions cannot take the
  account's Lambda concurrency.
- **IAM:** ingestors and manual import may only write `raw/*` (no read, no delete); the S3 import ingestor only
  reads its bucket. `GET /integrations/{source}/credentials` never returns a value the plugin marks secret (the
  GitHub token and webhook secret are write-only once saved).
- **Prompts:** review text in the enrichment prompt and memory-extraction transcripts are fenced as data, and the
  AI assistant treats tool results as data, never as instructions. Dot-only ids are refused at the assistant's
  tool and approval boundaries.
- **Memory:** memory routes by id and the review queue's linked memories follow the reader's category access.
- **Links built from stored data** (a review's source, a release citation, a design reference) render only for
  http(s) URLs.
- A scraped page is read up to 5 MB (web scraper and *Analyze URL*). A failed manual-import start stores a fixed
  reason, and an unparseable model answer is logged by its length, never its content.
- Localhost is allowed only for a `-c environment=dev` deployment: the app client's OAuth redirect URLs and the
  raw bucket's CORS origins.
- `scripts/test-api.sh` has no default test password: set `VOC_TEST_PASS`.
- `frontend/scripts/fix-i18n.mjs` translates only the delta: keys missing or empty in a target locale (write the
  English first). `--ns` and `--keys` narrow a run further; `--recheck-english` brings back the old full pass over
  values still identical to English.

### Fixed
- A file reprocessed from `processed/` in the S3 import keeps its original folder's source label in the import
  history.

### Security
- **protectData deployments** keep Lambda and API log groups 365 days and retain them on stack deletion, keep the
  S3 access-log bucket, and turn on CloudFormation termination protection on every stack. Demo deployments keep
  14-day logs and delete everything with the stack.
- `scratch/` copies in the raw bucket expire after 2 days; files staged in the S3 import bucket expire after 90 days.

### Upgrade notes
- **Cognito feature plan.** The app user pool is set to the **Essentials** plan (needed for passkeys). Pools created
  since November 2024 already are; an older Lite pool moves on deploy. The first 10,000 monthly active users are
  free, then Essentials is about $0.015 per user.
- **TLS.** Clients that cannot negotiate TLS 1.2 with a forward-secret cipher can no longer reach the API. Check
  `tlsVersion` in the access log before moving to the STRICT endpoint access mode later.
- **Execution log group.** The existing `API-Gateway-Execution-Logs_<api id>/v1` group is not managed by the stack;
  set its retention once: `aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name API-Gateway-Execution-Logs_<api id>/v1
  --retention-in-days 14` (365 with protectData).
- **Tearing down a protectData deployment** now needs termination protection turned off first
  (`aws cloudformation update-termination-protection --no-enable-termination-protection --stack-name <stack>`),
  and the retained log groups and access-log bucket are left behind to delete by hand.
- **Deploy order:** `npm run deploy:infra` (all stacks, then the API stage refresh), then `npm run deploy:frontend`.
- **Deployment test user:** set `VOC_TEST_PASS` before `scripts/test-api.sh`, and disable the test user after
  validating.

## [5.64.00] - 2026-10-31

The SPA no longer reads the Cognito identity pool, which nothing has used since 5.61.00.

### Changed
- The frontend no longer reads `cognito.identityPoolId` or `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID`: `frontend/scripts/update-env.sh`
  stops writing the variable and no longer fails when the `IdentityPoolId` output is missing.

### Deprecated
- `cognito.identityPoolId` in `config.json` is still written (by VocApiStack and `npm run deploy:frontend`) for this
  release only: a browser on a cached pre-5.64 page still requires it. The next release stops writing it, and the
  one after deletes the unused identity pool, its authenticated role (no permissions) and VocCoreStack's
  `IdentityPoolId` output. VocCoreStack already exports the pool id explicitly, so the release that drops
  VocApiStack's import can deploy (CloudFormation refuses to delete an export that is still imported).

### Upgrade notes
- Deploy every stack together (`npm run deploy:infra`), as usual. Nothing to change in `cdk.context.json`. A local
  `frontend/.env` may keep `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID`; it is ignored.

## [5.63.00] - 2026-10-31

Global MCP server: OAuth sign-in for Kiro, Claude Code and Cursor, more of the app through the existing tools, MCP prompts and resources, alarms and env-var config snippets; and faster, cheaper releases (skipped layer builds, changed-stacks deploys, a parallel production e2e run on Claude Haiku 5.5).

### Added

- MCP prompts on `/mcp/global`: `weekly_summary`, `triage_urgent` and `prfaq_from_feedback`. A read-only token's
  PR/FAQ prompt drafts in the chat; only a write token's mentions saving it, after the user confirms
  ([docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md#prompts-and-resources)).
- MCP resources: `voc://categories` and `voc://company-context`, read through the settings routes as the token's
  minter. Both protocol eras advertise the new capabilities; each prompt or resource read is audited like a tool
  call (`prompt:<name>` / `resource:<uri>`, never the arguments).
- Existing MCP tools reach more of the app: `get_metrics` gains `view=github` (GitHub issues per release and
  label) and `view=entities` (the filter values in use with counts), `search_feedback` takes `urgent: true`, and
  `get_feedback` takes `include_similar: true` (up to 5 slim similar items).
- Four runtime alarms for `/mcp/global` (refused credentials, denied tool calls, failed tool calls, rate limiting),
  created with the other alarms when an admin turns alerting on in Administration → System → Logs → Alerts
  ([docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md#alarms-and-concurrency)). The endpoint now emits an `AuthDenied` metric.
- Connect: the `mcp.json` card has one snippet per client. Claude Code, Cursor and Kiro (the default tabs) read the
  token from `VOC_MCP_TOKEN`, so the file holds no secret; "Other clients" keeps the pasted-token variant.
- Cognito group `e2e` (VocCoreStack). For a member, every model call the app makes for that user, on
  every AI surface (assistant and plan steps, API routes, project and assist jobs, manual-import
  enrichment, agent runs the user starts), resolves to Claude Haiku 5.5, with the capacity fallback kept
  on Haiku. Real users and the admin model picker are unaffected; the image model is not part of it. The
  profile comes only from verified Cognito groups or a job record a verified request wrote
  ([docs/deployment.md → E2E Test Users Run on Haiku 5.5](docs/deployment.md#e2e-test-users-run-on-haiku-55-the-e2e-cognito-group)).
- `CDK_DEPLOY_CHANGED=1 npm run deploy:infra` runs `cdk diff` once and deploys only the stacks with
  differences (`--exclusively`), always ending with the API stage refresh (also when VocApiStack did not
  change or nothing did, so an earlier interrupted refresh never leaves removed routes live); it
  falls back to the full deploy when the diff fails or cannot be read. The default deploy is unchanged
  ([docs/deployment.md → Faster deploys](docs/deployment.md#faster-deploys-skip-what-did-not-change)).
- e2e suite: the read-only specs run in their own fully parallel projects (`admin-read`, `user-read`,
  `E2E_READ_WORKERS`, default 4) while the writing specs stay one at a time (`E2E_WRITE_WORKERS`); only specs
  that depend on no data a write can change are listed (`request-counts`, `error-states`,
  `workflow-custom-arrows`). `run-sharded.sh` with only `E2E_SHARD_WORKERS` gives the writing specs at most 2
  workers and the read-only ones the rest, and refuses a per-project cap above that total; an
  assistant conversation is capped at 8 runs per spec page so each model call's context stays small
  (`voc-datalake/frontend/e2e/README.md`).
- OAuth sign-in for `POST /mcp/global` ([docs/mcp.md → OAuth sign-in](docs/mcp.md#oauth-sign-in)): discovery
  documents under `/v1/.well-known/` (protected-resource and authorization-server metadata), a registration
  facade that answers pre-registered public PKCE clients, `GET /oauth/authorize`, a loopback relay
  (`GET /oauth/callback`, any port) and token/revocation facades (`POST /oauth/token`, `POST /oauth/revoke`).
  The nine routes are anonymous by design and throttled per method.
- Consent page `/oauth/authorize`: the signed-in person sees which assistant asks, chooses read only or read and
  write and an optional project, then signs in. The assistant acts as that person exactly like a personal token:
  never admin, at most editor, `run_agent` only for an administrator and re-checked per call, every tool call
  audited.
- Connect page: "Sign in with your account" snippets per client (no token in them) and "Signed-in assistants"
  with revoke; revoking refuses the assistant's next request.
- Web assistants (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Amazon Quick) can be given callback URLs with `-c mcpOAuthWebCallbacks`;
  their sign-in is untested until signed in live.
- `-c mcpTokenMinting=false` turns minting of personal tokens off (Connect hides the form, `POST /connect/tokens`
  answers 403); existing tokens keep working until they expire or are revoked.

### Changed

- `voc-mcp-global-api` reserves 20 concurrent executions; `-c mcpReservedConcurrency=<n>` changes it, `0` = no
  reservation ([docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md#reserved-concurrency-of-the-mcp-endpoint--c-mcpreservedconcurrency)).
- For a 2026-07-28 client, an `Mcp-Name` header sent with `prompts/get` or `resources/read` must match the body's
  name or URI (refused with `-32020` otherwise); it stays optional there.
- `npm run build:layers` skips a layer whose requirements, install recipe, build image and platform are
  unchanged since its last build (a `.build-stamp` next to `python/`); `FORCE_LAYER_BUILD=1` or `--force`
  rebuilds every layer. A stamp older than 7 days rebuilds anyway (`LAYER_STAMP_MAX_AGE_DAYS`), so
  dependencies without an exact pin are re-resolved at least weekly.
- Plan steps now read the approver's Cognito groups on every step (they used to only for admin-only
  steps), so an approver in `e2e` runs on Haiku 5.5. An ordinary step still runs when that lookup fails.
- e2e setup fails fast when a test user is not in the `e2e` group (`E2E_ALLOW_FULL_MODELS=1` downgrades
  it to a warning).
- A 401 from `/mcp/global` names the protected-resource metadata in `WWW-Authenticate` (`resource_metadata=…`).
  The API-wide 401 for a request without credentials now carries `Bearer resource_metadata="…"` instead of
  `Bearer error="invalid_token"`; the SPA does not read it.
- Signing in from a deep link keeps the link's query string (the consent page needs it).

### Security

- MCP OAuth access tokens are verified in full on every request (RS256 only, issuer, access token, MCP client,
  expiry, audience when present) and accepted only from a sign-in the person approved; refresh tokens are never
  stored. The tokens API role gains Put/Delete on the jobs table's `MCPOAUTH#` relay rows only.
- MCP OAuth clients get no app session: their Cognito clients allow only the `<mcp url>/read|write` scopes (no
  `openid`, so no ID token) and no SRP or password sign-in, and `POST /oauth/token` never returns an `id_token`
  ([docs/mcp.md → OAuth sign-in](docs/mcp.md#oauth-sign-in)).
- Every REST API Lambda and the assistant stream (`/chat/stream`) answer 401 to a Cognito token issued to any app
  client but the SPA's web client and the board pool's client (new env `APP_CLIENT_IDS` on every VocApiStack
  function). The Cognito authorizer accepts a token of any client of the pool, so an MCP client's token could
  otherwise have called every route with the person's full rights.
- The MCP OAuth consent page follows a redirect only to the deployment's Cognito hosted UI, a loopback
  callback (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]` with a port from 1024 to 65535) or the exact https callback the assistant's request
  named; anything else shows the page's error. `config.json` gains `cognito.hostedUiDomain`
  ([docs/mcp.md → OAuth sign-in](docs/mcp.md#oauth-sign-in)). `npm run deploy:frontend` prints a WARNING (and
  still deploys) when VocCoreStack's `UserPoolDomain` output is missing or not a
  `<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com` host: until VocCoreStack is redeployed the consent page refuses every approval.
- A consent opens its sign-in window for that one authorize request only: the token exchange's `code_verifier`
  must match the consented PKCE `code_challenge` before a sign-in is recorded.

### Upgrade notes

- The reserved concurrency (20) comes out of the account's unreserved Lambda pool, which must stay at 100 or
  more: an account whose Lambda concurrency quota is under 120 fails the VocApiStack deploy. Raise the quota
  first (new accounts can start at 10), or deploy with `-c mcpReservedConcurrency=0` (no reservation) or a
  smaller number.
- Where alerting is already on, turn it off and on again once to create the four MCP alarms;
  they add 4 alarm metrics (about $0.40 a month at list price). Two deployments in one account and region share
  the MCP metrics, so each one's MCP alarms count both.
- Kiro IDE users of the env-var snippet must approve `VOC_MCP_TOKEN` under Settings → Mcp Approved Env Vars.
- Deploy VocCoreStack to create the `e2e` group, then add each e2e test user once (admin only):
  `aws cognito-idp admin-add-user-to-group --user-pool-id <UserPoolId> --username '<e2e user>' --group-name e2e`.
  The users must sign in again to get a token with the group. Without it the e2e setup stops.
- Deploy VocProcessingStack before VocApiStack (the usual order): the processor must accept the new
  optional `model_profile` queue field before the manual-import Lambda starts sending it.
- VocApiStack adds 25 resources (Cognito resource server, three app clients on the existing user pool, nine
  routes): 384 with every plugin, under this release's ceiling of 388 and the stack's fixed gate of 425
  (500 minus 75 headroom). Deploy with `npm run deploy:api` (or end with `scripts/refresh-api-stage.sh`).
- The new clients use the user pool's existing hosted-UI domain; nothing changes in VocCoreStack. Deploy
  VocApiStack (or run `npm run deploy:frontend`) so `config.json` names it: until then the consent page refuses
  to send the browser to the sign-in.
- `resource` (RFC 8707) is dropped before Cognito unless `-c mcpOAuthResourceIndicator=true`; set it only on a
  pool whose hosted UI accepts resource binding.
- Before announcing OAuth to users, run the live-test runbook in docs/mcp.md.
- A consent approved but not yet completed while this release deploys must be approved again (the grant has no
  stored challenge). Requests to the REST API with a token of another app client of the user pool (a script
  signing in through its own client) now get 401; use the SPA's client (`UserPoolClientId`).

## [5.61.00] - 2026-10-31

Sign-in moves from the deprecated amazon-cognito-identity-js to Amplify v6, and the library is removed.

### Changed
- App sign-in (`/login`, the first-login new-password step, forgot password, Account → Change password, and the
  silent token refresh behind every API call and the assistant stream) runs on Amplify v6 (`aws-amplify/auth`).
  The screens and messages are unchanged. Amplify keeps the session under the same
  `CognitoIdentityServiceProvider.<client id>.*` localStorage keys the former library used, so people signed in
  before the upgrade stay signed in.
- Signing out now also revokes the refresh token at Cognito (Amplify's `signOut`), so a copied refresh token stops
  working at sign-out instead of at its expiry. Sign-out still clears the browser at once when the revoke cannot
  reach Cognito.
- The SPA no longer calls the Cognito identity pool on sign-in and on every refresh: nothing in the app uses AWS
  credentials (every API call carries the Cognito ID token). The identity pool and `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID` stay
  as they are.
- Feedback boards and document review links (the board pool) keep their own session, now stored and refreshed by
  `services/boardSession.ts` (Cognito `REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH`, one refresh at a time) under the same keys as before,
  so board users stay signed in too. A refresh Cognito refuses signs the board user out; a network failure keeps
  the session for the next try.

### Removed
- The `amazon-cognito-identity-js` dependency.

### Fixed
- The frontend docs no longer claim the app's refresh token is kept in memory only: the former library already
  stored it in localStorage, as Amplify does now. `authStore` no longer carries an unused `refreshToken` field.

Every dependency, Lambda runtime and layer moves to its newest release within its current major, starting from

  moves. `@vitest/eslint-plugin` stays at 1.6.27 (1.6.28 requires TypeScript 6, a major), knip at 6.44.0 (6.44.1

  environment already installed, since a `>=` floor resolves to the newest release; lxml 6.1.3 and cryptography

  lint tools move to pytest 9.2, pytest-mock 3.17, moto 5.2.5, boto3 1.43.123 and ruff 0.17.3. ruff 0.17's new rules found 47 lines:
  implicit string concatenation inside lists is parenthesized, `os.path.commonprefix` is replaced, and the eight

- `npm audit` still reports only moderate advisories (no high or critical), all one minimatch denial of service
  (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249) reached through eslint, typescript-eslint, Stryker and the `aws-cdk-lib` synth. It is
  fixed only in minimatch 11, which those packages adopt in their next major versions.

### Upgrade notes

  pin pydantic 2.14.2.
- Deploying updates the `voc-chat-stream` and `voc-plan-step` functions to the `nodejs24.x` runtime in place.

## [5.60.00] - 2026-10-31

Company personas: a persona library on the Company page that projects copy from and promote into.

## [5.57.03] - 2026-10-31

A freshness report lists every dependency, Lambda runtime, toolchain and workflow pin that is behind its newest release.

### Added

- `npm run deps:freshness` (`scripts/dependency-freshness.mjs`): compares the six npm lockfiles, the Lambda layers'
